descriptions.name: 1,4-Dioxane
descriptions.description_en: A by-product formed when surfactants are ethoxylated, so it appears as a contaminant rather than a listed ingredient. IARC classifies it Group 2B, possibly carcinogenic, and manufacturers are expected to strip it out.

descriptions.name: 100 cacao
descriptions.description_en: 100 cacao supports heart health with antioxidants, magnesium, and fiber from pure cocoa mass.

descriptions.name: 100 cocoa
descriptions.description_en: 100 cocoa supports heart health with antioxidants, magnesium, and fiber from pure cocoa mass.

descriptions.name: 100 카카오
descriptions.description_en: 100% cocoa chocolate provides antioxidants, magnesium, and fiber that support overall health and well-being.

descriptions.name: 2-Butoxyéthanol
descriptions.description_en: A solvent in window and multi-surface cleaners. It passes readily through the skin and, at high exposure, damages red blood cells, the liver and kidneys. Workplace exposure limits apply in the EU and US.

descriptions.name: 2-chloroethanol
descriptions.description_en: The reaction product of ethylene oxide with chloride, measured together with it under the same EU residue limit. Its own genotoxicity is debated, but its presence indicates treatment with a banned carcinogenic fumigant.

descriptions.name: 4-hexylresorcinol
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic anti-browning agent used mainly on crustaceans to slow discoloration. Current use is narrow and residue-controlled. Health: No major concern is established at authorized residues. Broader or higher exposure would require additional safety evidence.

descriptions.name: abats
descriptions.description_en: Exceptionally rich in vitamin A, B12, iron and copper - one of the most nutrient-dense foods there is. Its preformed vitamin A is so concentrated that health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid liver and liver products entirely, and a single weekly portion is enough for everyone else.

descriptions.name: acesulfame
descriptions.description_en: An artificial sweetener (E950) roughly 200 times sweeter than sugar, often blended with aspartame. Approved in the EU and US with an acceptable daily intake of 9–15 mg/kg, but it is a marker of ultra-processed formulation.

descriptions.name: acetate de sodium
descriptions.description_en: The sodium salt of acetic acid (E262), used as a preservative and to give salt-and-vinegar flavour. It is well tolerated but contributes sodium to the diet.

descriptions.name: acetylated distarch phosphate e1414
descriptions.description_en: Acetylated distarch phosphate (E1414) is a doubly modified starch that adds texture and shelf life without nutrition. It indicates an industrially engineered recipe and provides no nutritional benefits.

descriptions.name: acetylated oxidized starch
descriptions.description_en: A starch both oxidised and acetylated (E1451) to improve stability, clarity and texture. EFSA found no safety concern for the modified-starch family, but the double chemical treatment leaves a refined carbohydrate used purely as a structural ingredient.

descriptions.name: acide acetique
descriptions.description_en: Consuming acetic acid with meals can help lower blood sugar response.

descriptions.name: acide adipique
descriptions.description_en: An acidity regulator (E355) used in powdered desserts and drink mixes. It is produced industrially and considered safe at the low levels permitted.

descriptions.name: acide alginique
descriptions.description_en: A gelling fibre (E400) extracted from brown seaweed. It is not absorbed and behaves as soluble fibre, though large amounts can reduce mineral absorption.

descriptions.name: acide ascorbique
descriptions.description_en: Ascorbic acid supports immune function and helps protect cells from oxidative damage.

descriptions.name: acide azelaique
descriptions.description_en: Azelaic acid is gentle and safe for sensitive skin, helping to treat acne and rosacea.

descriptions.name: acide borique
descriptions.description_en: Boric acid (E284), a preservative now allowed in the EU for caviar only. It is classified as toxic to reproduction under EU chemical law and accumulates in the body, which is why its use is so tightly limited.

descriptions.name: acide citrique
descriptions.description_en: The acid that gives citrus fruit its sharpness - though the E330 on a label is produced industrially by fermenting sugar with Aspergillus niger, not extracted from lemons. It is one of the most benign additives there is, used to adjust acidity and protect colour. Its only real drawback is that it erodes tooth enamel in acidic drinks.

descriptions.name: acide fumarique
descriptions.description_en: An acidity regulator (E297) that occurs naturally in plants and in human metabolism. It is considered safe at food levels, though the food-grade version is synthesised industrially.

descriptions.name: acide glutamique
descriptions.description_en: Glutamic acid (E620), the free amino acid behind the savoury "umami" taste. It is used to intensify flavour in industrial foods and signals a product built on additives rather than real ingredients.

descriptions.name: acide glycolique
descriptions.description_en: An alpha-hydroxy acid that exfoliates the skin surface and improves texture. EU rules cap consumer concentrations, and it increases sun sensitivity, so daily sunscreen is necessary while using it.

descriptions.name: acide guanylique
descriptions.description_en: Guanylic acid is an umami flavor enhancer metabolized into purines and not advised for people with gout.

descriptions.name: acide inosinique
descriptions.description_en: Inosinic acid is an umami enhancer produced by bacterial fermentation that boosts MSG taste; not advised for people with gout due to purines.

descriptions.name: acide kojique
descriptions.description_en: A skin-lightening agent produced by fermentation, used to fade dark spots. The SCCS caps it at 1% in cosmetics because of concerns about skin sensitisation and thyroid effects at higher levels.

descriptions.name: acide lactique
descriptions.description_en: An acidity regulator (E270) produced by fermentation, the same acid found in yoghurt and sourdough. It is one of the safest additives, though industrial versions are made in fermenters, not from milk.

descriptions.name: acide malique
descriptions.description_en: Malic acid is industrially synthesized for food use and rarely extracted from fruit.

descriptions.name: acide phosphorique
descriptions.description_en: An acidity regulator (E338) that gives colas their sharp bite. EFSA set a combined phosphate limit of 40 mg/kg in 2019 and warned that some groups already exceed it; high phosphate intake concerns kidney and bone health.

descriptions.name: acide propionique
descriptions.description_en: A mould inhibitor (E280) used mainly in industrial bread. It occurs naturally in some cheeses and is considered safe by EFSA, but its presence signals bread built for long shelf life.

descriptions.name: acide salicylique
descriptions.description_en: A beta-hydroxy acid that exfoliates and unclogs pores, effective against acne. Its concentration is capped in EU cosmetics, and it should not be used on children under three or during pregnancy without medical advice.

descriptions.name: acide sorbique
descriptions.description_en: A mould inhibitor (E200) and one of the gentler preservatives, occurring naturally in rowan berries. It is well tolerated, though it can cause mild skin or digestive reactions in sensitive people.

descriptions.name: acide succinique
descriptions.description_en: Succinic acid is an industrial acidifier with little long-term research on its effects.

descriptions.name: Acide tartrique
descriptions.description_en: Tartaric acid helps regulate acidity and is well tolerated in foods.

descriptions.name: acides gras
descriptions.description_en: Fatty acids (E570) used as anti-foaming and glazing agents rather than as a food fat. They are refined industrial derivatives, typical of processed formulations.

descriptions.name: acidifiant acide citrique
descriptions.description_en: The acid that gives citrus fruit its sharpness - though the E330 on a label is produced industrially by fermenting sugar with Aspergillus niger, not extracted from lemons. It is one of the most benign additives there is, used to adjust acidity and protect colour. Its only real drawback is that it erodes tooth enamel in acidic drinks.

descriptions.name: acrylamide
descriptions.description_en: A compound that forms when starchy foods are fried, roasted or baked at high heat. IARC rates it Group 2A, probably carcinogenic, and EFSA confirmed it raises cancer risk across all age groups.

descriptions.name: acrylates
descriptions.description_en: Synthetic polymers that form films in nail products, hair styling and long-wear make-up. Cured polymers are stable, but uncured acrylate monomers in nail products are strong skin sensitisers.

descriptions.name: advantame
descriptions.description_en: An artificial sweetener (E969) derived from aspartame and roughly 37,000 times sweeter than sugar, so it is used in minute amounts. Authorised in the EU and US, but a purely synthetic high-intensity sweetener.

descriptions.name: aflatoxine
descriptions.description_en: A natural mold toxin that forms on poorly stored grains, nuts and spices. Classified IARC Group 1 human carcinogen — the confirmed level. Chronic exposure damages the liver and is a leading cause of liver cancer.

descriptions.name: agar agar
descriptions.description_en: Agar agar acts as soluble fiber, supporting digestive health without being absorbed.

descriptions.name: ail
descriptions.description_en: Garlic is a whole, unprocessed food containing sulfur compounds with antibacterial properties and beneficial effects on blood pressure.

descriptions.name: aioli
descriptions.description_en: An emulsion of oil, egg yolk and garlic - essentially a garlic mayonnaise. Made with olive oil it is a good fat, but it is almost entirely fat: a couple of tablespoons carry more calories than the dish they accompany.

descriptions.name: alcool benzylique
descriptions.description_en: Alcohol benzylique is an aromatic alcohol used mainly as a solvent or carrier in flavorings. Large systemic doses can depress the nervous system and disturb metabolism; newborns are particularly vulnerable to high medicinal exposure, although food amounts are far lower.

descriptions.name: alcool ethylique
descriptions.description_en: Ethanol in alcoholic beverages is an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen. It is linked to cancers of the mouth, throat, oesophagus, liver, colon and breast, and no safe intake level has been established.

descriptions.name: alginate d ammonium
descriptions.description_en: A seaweed-derived thickener (E403) used to stabilise texture. It passes through the gut undigested and is considered safe at food levels.

descriptions.name: alginate de propylene glycol
descriptions.description_en: A chemically modified alginate (E405) used to stabilise beer foam and dressings. Unlike plain alginates it is reacted with propylene glycol, making it a synthetic derivative rather than a simple seaweed extract.

descriptions.name: algue
descriptions.description_en: Seaweed provides iodine, iron, magnesium and soluble fibre, supporting thyroid function and overall nutrition. Nori and wakame are moderate, but kombu is by far the most iodine-dense food known and can disturb thyroid function if eaten regularly - health agencies advise limiting it, and using it for stock rather than eating it.

descriptions.name: algue eucheuma transformee
descriptions.description_en: Processed eucheuma seaweed (E407a) is a less purified carrageenan variant linked to gut inflammation and banned in EU infant formula.

descriptions.name: algue marine
descriptions.description_en: Seaweed provides iodine, iron, magnesium and soluble fibre, supporting thyroid function and overall nutrition. Nori and wakame are moderate, but kombu is by far the most iodine-dense food known and can disturb thyroid function if eaten regularly - health agencies advise limiting it, and using it for stock rather than eating it.

descriptions.name: algues
descriptions.description_en: Seaweed provides iodine, iron, magnesium and soluble fibre, supporting thyroid function and overall nutrition. Nori and wakame are moderate, but kombu is by far the most iodine-dense food known and can disturb thyroid function if eaten regularly - health agencies advise limiting it, and using it for stock rather than eating it.

descriptions.name: Alkylphénols éthoxylés (APEO)
descriptions.description_en: Surfactants used in detergents and textile processing. They break down into alkylphenols, recognised endocrine disruptors that are highly toxic to aquatic life, and their use is restricted under EU REACH rules.

descriptions.name: allulose
descriptions.description_en: A rare sugar that sweetens with almost no calories and no effect on blood glucose. It is authorised in the United States, Canada, Japan and Korea, but not in the European Union or the UK, where it is still going through novel food assessment. Large amounts cause bloating and digestive upset.

descriptions.name: Aluminium (casseroles, papier)
descriptions.description_en: Aluminium cookware and foil release small amounts of metal into food, especially with acidic or salty dishes at high heat. EFSA set a weekly tolerable intake that many diets already approach.

descriptions.name: Aluminium chlorohydrate (déodorants)
descriptions.description_en: The active salt in antiperspirants, which works by physically plugging sweat ducts. Health agencies have not established a link to breast cancer, but it is absorbed in small amounts and adds to total aluminium exposure.

descriptions.name: aluminium sulfate
descriptions.description_en: Aluminium sulfate is an aluminum-containing processing salt used in limited applications that contributes to total dietary aluminum exposure. Aluminum can accumulate, so repeated exposure may exceed tolerable weekly levels, especially in those with reduced kidney function.

descriptions.name: aluminum chlorohydrate
descriptions.description_en: The active salt in antiperspirants, which plugs sweat ducts to block perspiration. No link to breast cancer has been established, but it is absorbed in small amounts and adds to total aluminium exposure.

descriptions.name: aluminum silicate
descriptions.description_en: Aluminum silicate is a calcium-aluminum anti-caking agent found in powdered products. It adds to aluminum burden, which is neurotoxic and linked to Alzheimer's; restricted in the EU.

descriptions.name: aluminum sulfate
descriptions.description_en: An aluminum-containing processing salt used in limited applications. It contributes to total dietary aluminum exposure. Health: Because aluminum can accumulate, repeated exposure from many sources may push intake above the tolerable weekly level, especially in people with reduced kidney function.

descriptions.name: alun d ammonium
descriptions.description_en: Alun d ammonium is an aluminum-containing industrial salt used for firming or processing in limited foods. Repeated intake contributes to total aluminum exposure, which can accumulate in the body.

descriptions.name: alun de potassium
descriptions.description_en: Potassium alum, also called alun de potassium, acts as a firming or processing agent and adds aluminum to the diet. The main health concern is cumulative aluminum exposure over time.

descriptions.name: amande
descriptions.description_en: Almonds supply vitamin E, magnesium, fiber, and healthy fats that support heart health.

descriptions.name: amarante
descriptions.description_en: Amaranth is a South American pseudo-cereal rich in complete protein, iron, and magnesium, and contains no gluten.

descriptions.name: amidon
descriptions.description_en: Starch extracted from grains or tubers, used to thicken and bulk out food. It is a refined carbohydrate with a high glycemic response and none of the fibre or nutrients of the original grain.

descriptions.name: amidon acetyle
descriptions.description_en: Acetylated starch (E1420), chemically treated to stay stable through processing. It is a refined carbohydrate with no fibre or micronutrients, used purely for texture.

descriptions.name: amidon de ble
descriptions.description_en: Wheat starch separated from the protein and bran of the grain. It behaves like a fast sugar in the body, with little nutritional value — the whole grain is always the better option.

descriptions.name: amidon de pomme de terre
descriptions.description_en: Potato starch extracted industrially. Gluten-free and thickening, but a refined carbohydrate stripped of the potato’s fibre and potassium.

descriptions.name: amidon hydroxypropyl
descriptions.description_en: A chemically modified starch (E1440) that stays stable through freezing, heating and storage. EFSA's 2017 opinion raised no safety or genotoxicity concern, but it is a refined carbohydrate whose only purpose is texture in industrial recipes.

descriptions.name: amidon modifie
descriptions.description_en: A generic label covering any starch altered chemically or physically to thicken and stabilise industrial food, without saying which one. EFSA considers modified starches safe with no numerical ADI needed, but they are refined carbohydrates with no nutrients and one of the clearest markers of ultra-processing.

descriptions.name: amidon modifie acetyle
descriptions.description_en: Acetylated modified starch is an industrially acetylated starch with a high glycemic index affecting blood sugar control.

descriptions.name: amidon octenylsuccinate de sodium
descriptions.description_en: Starch modified with octenyl succinic anhydride (E1450) to act as an emulsifier and encapsulating agent in drinks, dressings and powdered flavourings. EFSA's 2017 re-evaluation of modified starches found no safety concern and no need for a numerical ADI, but it remains a refined carbohydrate with no nutrients and a marker of industrial formulation.

descriptions.name: Ammoniac
descriptions.description_en: Ammonia and its compounds, used as acidity regulators and processing aids. They are neutralised in the finished food, but ammonia processing can generate unwanted by-products in some applications.

descriptions.name: ammonium aluminium sulfate
descriptions.description_en: Ammonium aluminium sulfate is used for firming or processing in limited foods and contains aluminum. Repeated consumption adds to total aluminum exposure, which can accumulate in the body.

descriptions.name: ammonium aluminum sulfate
descriptions.description_en: An aluminum-containing industrial salt used for firming or processing in limited foods. Health: Repeated intake contributes to total aluminum exposure, which is limited because the metal can accumulate in the body.

descriptions.name: ammonium bicarbonate
descriptions.description_en: Ammonium bicarbonate releases carbon dioxide and ammonia during baking, used in dry biscuits and crackers. Poorly baked or heavily dosed products may retain ammonia odor and cause irritation, but normal use is not a major health risk.

descriptions.name: ammonium carbonate
descriptions.description_en: Ammonium carbonate is an industrial raising agent releasing carbon dioxide and ammonia during baking, commonly used in dry biscuits and crackers. Poorly baked or heavily dosed products may retain ammonia odor and cause irritation, but normal use is not a major health risk.

descriptions.name: ammonium carbonates
descriptions.description_en: Industrial raising agents that release carbon dioxide and ammonia during baking. They are commonly used in dry biscuits and crackers. Health: Poorly baked or heavily dosed products may retain an unpleasant ammonia odor and cause irritation, but normal baked use is not considered a major health risk.

descriptions.name: ammonium hydroxide
descriptions.description_en: An ammonia solution used in controlled processing and pH adjustment. Most ammonia is removed, reacted, or present at very low residual levels. Health: High residual concentrations would irritate the eyes, airways, and digestive tract and produce a strong odor.

descriptions.name: ammonium sulfate
descriptions.description_en: An industrial salt used in flour treatment, fermentation, and acidity control. Health: No major specific harm is established at permitted levels. Excessive quantities may irritate the digestive system.

descriptions.name: anchois
descriptions.description_en: Anchois offers omega-3 fatty acids that promote cardiovascular and cognitive functions.

descriptions.name: anchovy
descriptions.description_en: Anchovy supplies omega-3 fatty acids beneficial for heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: anhydrous caffeine
descriptions.description_en: Caffeine is a natural stimulant that boosts alertness and physical performance.

descriptions.name: annatto
descriptions.description_en: A yellow-orange colouring (E160b) extracted from achiote seeds, one of the few plant-based dyes still widely used in industry. Generally well tolerated, though it can trigger allergic reactions in a small number of people.

descriptions.name: anthocyanes
descriptions.description_en: Purple-red pigments (E163) extracted from grape skins, berries or red cabbage. They are plant-derived and carry antioxidant activity, but the food-grade version is a concentrated industrial extract.

descriptions.name: Antimoine
descriptions.description_en: A metal used as a catalyst in PET bottle manufacture, which can leach in trace amounts when bottles are heated or stored a long time. IARC classifies antimony trioxide Group 2B.

descriptions.name: aquaculture
descriptions.description_en: Aquaculture is intensively farmed salmon with industrial feed, antibiotics, synthetic colorants, and possible contaminants like PCBs and dioxins. Consumption should be occasional due to these potential contaminants and additives.

descriptions.name: arachide
descriptions.description_en: A good source of plant protein, fibre and heart-healthy fats.

descriptions.name: araignee de mer
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: arborio rice
descriptions.description_en: Arborio rice is a short-grain rice used in cooking that provides carbohydrates for energy.

descriptions.name: argent
descriptions.description_en: Silver (E174), used as a decorative coating on confectionery. EFSA could not conclude on its safety in 2016, and its 2025 follow-up confirmed that the data on nanoparticle content, silver-ion release and genotoxicity are still inadequate. Nearly a decade on, its safety as a food additive remains officially unresolved.

descriptions.name: argon
descriptions.description_en: An inert gas used to displace oxygen and slow oxidation in packaged food and beverages. Health: It does not react significantly with food and is not considered a safety concern in authorized packaging use.

descriptions.name: arome artificiel
descriptions.description_en: Entirely synthetic molecules, usually petrochemical-derived, built to imitate natural tastes. Their exact composition is not disclosed on the label, and they are one of the clearest markers of ultra-processed food.

descriptions.name: arome bio
descriptions.description_en: Flavouring made from certified organic raw materials, which limits solvents and synthetic inputs. Still a concentrated industrial extract, but a step above conventional natural flavouring.

descriptions.name: arome naturel
descriptions.description_en: Despite the name, these are extracted and concentrated in industrial processes, often using solvents. The precise composition is a trade secret, and their presence signals a product engineered for taste rather than made from whole ingredients.

descriptions.name: arsenic
descriptions.description_en: A heavy metal contaminant found in water, rice and some seafood. Arsenic and inorganic arsenic compounds are IARC Group 1 human carcinogens, linked to skin, lung and bladder cancer.

descriptions.name: ascorbate de calcium
descriptions.description_en: Calcium ascorbate provides vitamin C and calcium, supporting antioxidant protection and bone health.

descriptions.name: ascorbate de sodium
descriptions.description_en: Sodium ascorbate delivers vitamin C antioxidant benefits while preventing food oxidation.

descriptions.name: ascorbic acid
descriptions.description_en: Ascorbic acid supports immune function and helps protect cells from oxidative damage.

descriptions.name: asiago
descriptions.description_en: Asiago cheese provides calcium and protein which are vital for healthy bones and muscle growth.

descriptions.name: aspartame
descriptions.description_en: An artificial sweetener (E951) in diet drinks and sugar-free products. IARC classified it Group 2B, possibly carcinogenic, in 2023, while WHO's JECFA kept the daily limit at 40 mg/kg. Best not consumed daily.

descriptions.name: atrazine
descriptions.description_en: A herbicide banned in the EU since 2004 but still detected in groundwater decades later. It is widely regarded as an endocrine disruptor affecting hormonal and reproductive function, and remains in use in North America.

descriptions.name: avocat
descriptions.description_en: Monounsaturated fats and vitamin E in avocado support heart health and improve absorption of fat-soluble vitamins.

descriptions.name: avoine
descriptions.description_en: Beta-glucan in oats helps lower cholesterol and provides slow-releasing energy to keep you full longer.

descriptions.name: ayran
descriptions.description_en: Ayran is a fermented yogurt drink that helps maintain gut health and hydration.

descriptions.name: azodicarbonamide
descriptions.description_en: A flour treatment agent (E927) used to bleach dough and speed up baking. Banned in the EU and Australia, still permitted in the US. During baking it breaks down into semicarbazide and urethane, both flagged for cancer concerns.

descriptions.name: azorubine
descriptions.description_en: Carmoisine (E122), a synthetic red azo dye. EU law requires a label warning that it may affect activity and attention in children, and it is not authorised in the United States.

descriptions.name: azote
descriptions.description_en: Nitrogen gas is inert and safe, helping preserve food freshness without adding residues.

descriptions.name: baba ganoush
descriptions.description_en: Baba ganoush benefits the body by offering antioxidants and fiber from roasted eggplants.

descriptions.name: babeurre
descriptions.description_en: Smaller fat globules in goat, sheep and buffalo milk may make them easier to digest for some people. Nutritionally they are close to cow's milk, with slightly more medium-chain fats.

descriptions.name: bacon
descriptions.description_en: Salted, cured and smoked pork. It falls under processed meat, classified IARC Group 1 human carcinogen in 2015: regular intake raises colorectal cancer risk through nitroso-compounds formed during curing.

descriptions.name: baharat
descriptions.description_en: Baharat benefits the body by providing natural antioxidants and essential nutrients from dried herbs and spices.

descriptions.name: baies roses
descriptions.description_en: Pink pepper berries support the body with their natural antioxidants and mild resinous flavor.

descriptions.name: baking chocolate
descriptions.description_en: Baking chocolate supports heart health with antioxidants, magnesium, and fiber from pure cocoa mass.

descriptions.name: bakuchiol
descriptions.description_en: Bakuchiol may reduce fine lines with less irritation and is considered safe during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: bamboo
descriptions.description_en: Okra provides soluble fibre that helps regulate blood sugar and cholesterol, with very few calories. Its mucilage is what thickens stews and gumbo.

descriptions.name: bamboo shoots
descriptions.description_en: Bamboo shoots are low in calories and a good source of fibre and potassium, but fresh shoots contain cyanogenic glycosides and must be boiled before eating - canned shoots are already processed and safe. Bean sprouts and lotus root, often sold alongside them, raise no such issue.

descriptions.name: bambou
descriptions.description_en: Bamboo shoots are low in calories and a good source of fibre and potassium, but fresh shoots contain cyanogenic glycosides and must be boiled before eating - canned shoots are already processed and safe. Bean sprouts and lotus root, often sold alongside them, raise no such issue.

descriptions.name: banon
descriptions.description_en: Banon goat cheese supports digestion and provides lower fat content compared to hard cheeses.

descriptions.name: basic methacrylate copolymer
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic polymer used mainly to coat food supplements and control how tablets dissolve. Health: It is poorly absorbed. Safety relies on low residual monomers, controlled purity, and restricted use.

descriptions.name: bean sprouts
descriptions.description_en: Bamboo shoots are low in calories and a good source of fibre and potassium, but fresh shoots contain cyanogenic glycosides and must be boiled before eating - canned shoots are already processed and safe. Bean sprouts and lotus root, often sold alongside them, raise no such issue.

descriptions.name: beans
descriptions.description_en: Beans are a nutritious source of plant protein, fiber, vitamins, and minerals that support bodily functions.

descriptions.name: bee pollen
descriptions.description_en: Bee products carrying enzymes, amino acids and antibacterial compounds. They are also documented allergens: royal jelly and propolis have caused severe allergic reactions including anaphylaxis, rare but well recorded, and are best avoided by people with asthma or a known allergy to bee products. Pollen can trigger reactions in people allergic to the source plants.

descriptions.name: beet
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: beetroot
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: benzene
descriptions.description_en: An industrial solvent and petroleum by-product. IARC Group 1 human carcinogen with an established causal link to leukaemia. It has no legitimate use in food or cosmetics and appears only as a contaminant.

descriptions.name: benzoate de potassium
descriptions.description_en: A preservative (E212) closely related to sodium benzoate. It can form traces of benzene when a product also contains vitamin C, and may trigger hives or asthma in sensitive people.

descriptions.name: benzyl alcohol
descriptions.description_en: An aromatic alcohol used mainly as a solvent or carrier in flavorings. Food exposure is limited, but it is biologically active at high doses. Health: Large systemic doses can depress the nervous system and disturb metabolism. Newborns are particularly vulnerable to high medicinal exposure, although food amounts are far lower.

descriptions.name: benzylparaben
descriptions.description_en: A family of preservatives with weak hormone-like activity in laboratory tests. The EU banned five of them from cosmetics in 2014 for lack of safety data (isopropyl-, isobutyl-, phenyl-, benzyl- and pentylparaben) and capped propyl- and butylparaben at 0.14%, with an additional ban on the nappy area of children under three. The 2004 study that detected parabens in breast tissue established no causal link; the real issue is cumulative exposure across food, cosmetics and medicines.

descriptions.name: bergamot
descriptions.description_en: Bergamot contains vitamin C and antioxidants, which help strengthen the immune system and improve skin health.

descriptions.name: bergamote
descriptions.description_en: Bergamote provides vitamin C and antioxidants that support immune health and skin protection.

descriptions.name: beta carotene
descriptions.description_en: Beta carotene (E160a) is an orange plant pigment converted to vitamin A and acts as an antioxidant.

descriptions.name: beta-cyclodextrin
descriptions.description_en: A ring-shaped carbohydrate manufactured from starch and used to trap, protect, or carry flavors and other compounds. It has a relatively low acceptable daily intake. Health: High exposure can exceed the recommended daily limit. The restriction is based on systemic effects observed at higher doses, not on a cancer classification.

descriptions.name: betterave
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: beurre
descriptions.description_en: Butter provides natural saturated fat that should be consumed in moderation.

descriptions.name: beurre clarifie
descriptions.description_en: Clarified butter supplies healthy fats that help the body absorb fat-soluble vitamins.

descriptions.name: beurre cru
descriptions.description_en: Raw butter offers natural fats that contribute to energy and nutrient absorption.

descriptions.name: beurre de baratte
descriptions.description_en: Churned butter provides essential fatty acids that support energy and cell function.

descriptions.name: beurre de cacahuete
descriptions.description_en: Peanut butter is rich in good fats, fiber, magnesium, and vitamin E, supporting cardiovascular health.

descriptions.name: beurre de cacao
descriptions.description_en: Cocoa butter is a stable natural fat that distinguishes real chocolate from vegetable fat products.

descriptions.name: bha
descriptions.description_en: Butylated hydroxyanisole (E320), a synthetic antioxidant in fats, snacks and cosmetics. Classified IARC Group 2B, possibly carcinogenic to humans, and flagged by EFSA as a suspected endocrine disruptor.

descriptions.name: bht
descriptions.description_en: Butylated hydroxytoluene (E321), a synthetic antioxidant in fats, cereals and cosmetics. EFSA re-evaluated it as safe within a low daily limit; IARC does not classify it as carcinogenic.

descriptions.name: bicarbonate
descriptions.description_en: Baking soda is a simple, effective raising agent free from aluminium additives.

descriptions.name: bicarbonate d ammonium
descriptions.description_en: Bicarbonate d ammonium is an industrial raising agent releasing carbon dioxide and ammonia during baking; poorly baked or overdosed products may cause irritation or ammonia odor.

descriptions.name: bigeye tuna
descriptions.description_en: Long-lived top predators that concentrate the most methylmercury of any commercial fish. The FDA and EPA place swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel, bigeye tuna, orange roughy and Gulf tilefish on the Choices to Avoid list: pregnant women, breastfeeding women and children should not eat them at all, and other adults only rarely.

descriptions.name: bigorneau
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: bisulfite de calcium
descriptions.description_en: A sulfite preservative and firming agent (E227). It carries the same allergen labelling requirement as other sulfites and can provoke asthma symptoms in sensitive individuals.

descriptions.name: bisulfite de potassium
descriptions.description_en: A sulfite preservative (E228) used in wine and processed fruit. Like the whole sulfite family, it must be declared above 10 mg/kg and can trigger reactions in sulfite-sensitive people.

descriptions.name: bisulfite de sodium
descriptions.description_en: A sulfite preservative (E222) used to prevent browning and microbial growth. Like all sulfites it must be labelled above 10 mg/kg and can trigger reactions in sulfite-sensitive individuals.

descriptions.name: black pn
descriptions.description_en: Black PN is a synthetic black dye used in confectionery, sauces, and decorations. Frequent consumption can increase exposure beyond the acceptable daily intake, especially in children.

descriptions.name: black rice
descriptions.description_en: Black rice is a whole grain rich in antioxidants and fiber, supporting heart and digestive health.

descriptions.name: ble
descriptions.description_en: Whole wheat - the intact grain with its bran and germ - supplies fibre, B vitamins, magnesium and plant protein. Refining strips most of that away, so the wholemeal version is a different food nutritionally from white flour.

descriptions.name: ble khorasan
descriptions.description_en: Khorasan wheat provides more protein and selenium than modern wheat, supporting muscle and antioxidant functions.

descriptions.name: bleu
descriptions.description_en: Blue cheeses concentrate calcium, protein and B12, and their moulds give them their character. They are among the saltiest cheeses there are, and health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid blue-veined cheese unless it has been cooked until steaming hot.

descriptions.name: bleu 1
descriptions.description_en: Brilliant Blue FCF (E133), a petroleum-derived synthetic dye. It is authorised in the EU and US, but the FDA is working to phase it out of the American food supply by the end of 2027.

descriptions.name: bleu 2
descriptions.description_en: Indigotine (E132), a synthetic blue dye made from petroleum. Authorised in the EU and US, it is among the six certified dyes the FDA is pushing manufacturers to remove.

descriptions.name: bleu d auvergne
descriptions.description_en: Blue cheeses concentrate calcium, protein and B12, and their moulds give them their character. They are among the saltiest cheeses there are, and health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid blue-veined cheese unless it has been cooked until steaming hot.

descriptions.name: bleu patente v
descriptions.description_en: Bleu patente V is a synthetic blue dye used only to change appearance and provide no nutritional value. People with a history of reactions to synthetic dyes should be cautious due to possible hypersensitivity.

descriptions.name: blue cheese
descriptions.description_en: Blue cheeses concentrate calcium, protein and B12, and their moulds give them their character. They are among the saltiest cheeses there are, and health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid blue-veined cheese unless it has been cooked until steaming hot.

descriptions.name: bœuf
descriptions.description_en: Red meat provides complete protein, heme iron, zinc, and vitamin B12, best eaten fresh.

descriptions.name: bone phosphate
descriptions.description_en: Bone phosphate (E542), a calcium phosphate obtained by degreasing and calcining animal bones, used in small amounts to keep powders free-flowing. It is of animal origin, so it does not suit vegetarian, vegan, halal or kosher diets unless specifically certified, and it adds to total phosphate intake, which EFSA already considers high in European diets. Its use in food today is marginal.

descriptions.name: bouillon
descriptions.description_en: Stock used as a flavour base. Homemade versions are nutritious, but industrial bouillon is usually dominated by salt, flavour enhancers and fat, with very little real meat or vegetable.

descriptions.name: BPA (Bisphénol A)
descriptions.description_en: A plastic and epoxy resin building block that leaches into food from can linings and containers. EFSA cut its tolerable daily intake 20,000-fold in 2023, and the EU banned it in food contact materials in 2025.

descriptions.name: brazil nut
descriptions.description_en: The richest natural source of selenium on the planet, which supports thyroid function and antioxidant defences. One or two nuts already cover a full day's requirement, and eating them by the handful every day can exceed the tolerable upper intake - a rare case where a whole food needs a portion limit.

descriptions.name: brazil nuts
descriptions.description_en: The richest natural source of selenium on the planet, which supports thyroid function and antioxidant defences. One or two nuts already cover a full day's requirement, and eating them by the handful every day can exceed the tolerable upper intake - a rare case where a whole food needs a portion limit.

descriptions.name: brie
descriptions.description_en: Soft ripened cheeses provide calcium, protein and vitamin B12, and develop their character through surface moulds. Because their moisture and low acidity suit listeria, health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid soft ripened cheeses unless they are made from pasteurised milk or have been cooked until steaming hot.

descriptions.name: brilliant black bn
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic black dye used in confectionery, sauces, decorations, and other processed foods. Some high-consuming children may approach or exceed the acceptable daily intake. Health: Frequent consumption of several products containing this dye can increase exposure beyond the level intended for daily use.

descriptions.name: broad bean protein
descriptions.description_en: Fava bean protein is extracted by dry milling and air classification, rich in lysine and allergen-free but still a protein concentrate; it is acceptable as a supplement but not as the sole protein source.

descriptions.name: brocoli
descriptions.description_en: Broccoli's vitamin C, K, fibre, and sulforaphane support immune health and cellular protection.

descriptions.name: bromate de potassium
descriptions.description_en: A flour improver (E924) classified IARC Group 2B, possibly carcinogenic. Banned in the EU, UK, Canada, Brazil and China, but still permitted in US bread. Residues can remain in the finished loaf.

descriptions.name: bronopol
descriptions.description_en: A preservative (2-bromo-2-nitropropane-1,3-diol) that slowly releases formaldehyde, an IARC Group 1 carcinogen. It is also a frequent cause of contact allergy, and its use in EU cosmetics is restricted.

descriptions.name: brown ht
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic brown dye used in bakery, dessert, and confectionery products. Exposure estimates have indicated that some high consumers, particularly children, may exceed the acceptable daily intake. Health: The main concern is repeated high intake from multiple colored products.

descriptions.name: brun ht
descriptions.description_en: Brun HT is a synthetic brown dye used in bakery, dessert, and confectionery products. Repeated high intake from multiple colored products is a health concern, especially for children.

descriptions.name: buffalo milk
descriptions.description_en: Smaller fat globules in goat, sheep and buffalo milk may make them easier to digest for some people. Nutritionally they are close to cow's milk, with slightly more medium-chain fats.

descriptions.name: bulot
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: burrata
descriptions.description_en: Burrata cheese supplies proteins and fats that support energy levels and tissue repair.

descriptions.name: butane
descriptions.description_en: Butane, isobutane and propane (E943/E944) used as propellants in aerosol food products such as cooking sprays and whipped cream. They are technical gases with no nutritional purpose.

descriptions.name: buttermilk
descriptions.description_en: Smaller fat globules in goat, sheep and buffalo milk may make them easier to digest for some people. Nutritionally they are close to cow's milk, with slightly more medium-chain fats.

descriptions.name: butylparaben
descriptions.description_en: A family of preservatives with weak hormone-like activity in laboratory tests. The EU banned five of them from cosmetics in 2014 for lack of safety data (isopropyl-, isobutyl-, phenyl-, benzyl- and pentylparaben) and capped propyl- and butylparaben at 0.14%, with an additional ban on the nappy area of children under three. The 2004 study that detected parabens in breast tissue established no causal link; the real issue is cumulative exposure across food, cosmetics and medicines.

descriptions.name: butylparabene
descriptions.description_en: A family of preservatives with weak hormone-like activity in laboratory tests. The EU banned five of them from cosmetics in 2014 for lack of safety data (isopropyl-, isobutyl-, phenyl-, benzyl- and pentylparaben) and capped propyl- and butylparaben at 0.14%, with an additional ban on the nappy area of children under three. The 2004 study that detected parabens in breast tissue established no causal link; the real issue is cumulative exposure across food, cosmetics and medicines.

descriptions.name: c ur
descriptions.description_en: Exceptionally rich in vitamin A, B12, iron and copper - one of the most nutrient-dense foods there is. Its preformed vitamin A is so concentrated that health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid liver and liver products entirely, and a single weekly portion is enough for everyone else.

descriptions.name: cabillaud
descriptions.description_en: Lean white fish provide complete protein, iodine, selenium and B12 with very little fat, and sit among the lowest-mercury species there are - which is why the FDA and EPA place them on the Best Choices list, two to three servings a week.

descriptions.name: cacao
descriptions.description_en: Flavanol-rich cocoa supports vascular health and supplies magnesium and iron.

descriptions.name: cadmium
descriptions.description_en: A heavy metal that accumulates in the kidneys and bones over a lifetime. Cadmium and its compounds are IARC Group 1 human carcinogens, linked to lung cancer. It reaches food through polluted soil.

descriptions.name: cafe
descriptions.description_en: Coffee delivers antioxidants and is linked to lower risks of type 2 diabetes and liver disease.

descriptions.name: cafeine
descriptions.description_en: Caffeine boosts alertness and physical performance but can disrupt sleep and should be limited in pregnancy.

descriptions.name: caffeine anhydrous
descriptions.description_en: Caffeine is a natural stimulant that boosts alertness and physical performance.

descriptions.name: calamar
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: calcium benzoate
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic preservative that releases benzoate to slow microbial growth in acidic foods and drinks. It adds to total exposure from benzoic acid and other benzoates. Health: Sensitive individuals may experience hives or asthma-like reactions. High combined exposure should remain below the acceptable daily intake.

descriptions.name: calcium chloride
descriptions.description_en: A refined calcium salt used to firm vegetables, set cheese, and stabilize texture. Health: High concentrations can irritate the digestive tract and taste bitter, but normal authorized use is not considered a major health concern.

descriptions.name: calcium ferrocyanide
descriptions.description_en: A stable mineral complex used to keep salt and powders free-flowing. Health: No major safety concern is established at authorized use levels. The principal controls are dose and chemical purity.

descriptions.name: calcium gluconate
descriptions.description_en: A calcium salt used for firming, fortification, and stabilization. Health: Very high calcium intake can cause constipation and may be unsuitable for people with certain kidney or calcium-balance disorders.

descriptions.name: calcium hydroxide
descriptions.description_en: Also known as slaked lime, it is used to firm foods, process corn, and regulate acidity. Health: Concentrated material is irritating and alkaline. Excess residues could irritate the mouth or digestive tract, so processing controls are essential.

descriptions.name: calcium oxide
descriptions.description_en: Also called quicklime, it is a highly reactive industrial material used in controlled processing. It reacts to form less aggressive calcium compounds. Health: The raw powder is corrosive and can burn tissue. Finished food must not contain unsafe unreacted residues.

descriptions.name: calcium silicate
descriptions.description_en: A mineral anti-caking agent used in dry powders. Modern long-term toxicology data have been insufficient for a fully updated safety conclusion. Health: The concern is incomplete evidence on repeated exposure, not a proven disease effect at ordinary food levels.

descriptions.name: calcium sorbate
descriptions.description_en: A preservative deleted from the EU list of authorised food additives in 2018 because no company ever supplied the genotoxicity data EFSA had asked for - a data gap, not a proven toxicity. EFSA had already excluded it from the group ADI shared by sorbic acid (E200) and potassium sorbate (E202), partly because the related sodium salt tested positive for genotoxicity. It is no longer permitted in EU food.

descriptions.name: calcium stearoyl lactylate
descriptions.description_en: Calcium stearoyl lactylate (E481) is a dough conditioner that improves volume and shelf life in industrial bread. It is authorized at limited levels but unnecessary in traditional bread.

descriptions.name: calcium sulfate
descriptions.description_en: A mineral ingredient also known as food-grade gypsum, used for firming, flour treatment, and tofu production. Health: Very high intake can cause digestive discomfort or unnecessarily increase calcium exposure; normal food use is generally low risk.

descriptions.name: calcium sulphite
descriptions.description_en: Calcium sulphite is a rare sulfite preservative found mainly in ciders and fruit juices and can cause reactions in sulfite-intolerant people.

descriptions.name: calmar
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: camembert
descriptions.description_en: Soft ripened cheeses provide calcium, protein and vitamin B12, and develop their character through surface moulds. Because their moisture and low acidity suit listeria, health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid soft ripened cheeses unless they are made from pasteurised milk or have been cooked until steaming hot.

descriptions.name: camphre
descriptions.description_en: An aromatic compound used in balms and decongestant rubs. It is effective in small amounts, but it is neurotoxic if swallowed and should never be applied to the face of infants or young children.

descriptions.name: cannelle
descriptions.description_en: Cinnamon helps regulate blood sugar, with Ceylon cinnamon preferred for regular use.

descriptions.name: cantal
descriptions.description_en: Cantal cheese supplies calcium and protein, contributing to strong bones and muscle maintenance.

descriptions.name: canthaxanthin
descriptions.description_en: An orange-red carotenoid color with a low acceptable daily intake. Excessive exposure can cause canthaxanthin crystals to accumulate in the retina. Health: High intake may produce retinal deposits and visual changes. This is a genuine dose-related health concern and is why use is tightly restricted.

descriptions.name: cape gooseberry
descriptions.description_en: Small tart fruits eaten fresh - physalis, tamarillo and feijoa. They are low in sugar and supply vitamin C, fibre and carotenoids.

descriptions.name: capsanthine
descriptions.description_en: Capsanthine is a concentrated red-orange color extracted from paprika and standardized for pigment strength. Quality control is important for solvent residues and purity; rare allergic reactions may occur in sensitive individuals.

descriptions.name: capsorubine
descriptions.description_en: Capsorubine is a concentrated red-orange color extracted from paprika and standardized for pigment strength. Quality control is important for solvent residues and purity; rare allergic reactions may occur in sensitive individuals.

descriptions.name: caramel ammoniacal
descriptions.description_en: Caramel ammoniacal is an ultra-processed caramel coloring made with ammonia, containing 4-MEI, a possible carcinogen (IARC Group 2B).

descriptions.name: caramel ammoniacal sulfite
descriptions.description_en: Caramel colour made with ammonia and sulfites (E150c/E150d). The process forms 4-methylimidazole, classified IARC Group 2B, possibly carcinogenic. EU rules cap its use, and California requires warning labelling above set levels.

descriptions.name: caramel ii
descriptions.description_en: Caramel II is an ultra-processed caramel coloring produced with sulfites and linked to controversial by-products. These by-products raise concerns about its health impact.

descriptions.name: caramel iii
descriptions.description_en: Caramel III is an ultra-processed caramel coloring produced with ammonia and contains 4-MEI, classified as possibly carcinogenic (IARC Group 2B). Consumption may involve cancer risk concerns.

descriptions.name: caramel iv
descriptions.description_en: Caramel IV is an ultra-processed coloring made by heating sugars with ammonia and sulfites, containing 4-MEI (IARC Group 2B, possibly carcinogenic). It is commonly found in colas and poses potential cancer risks.

descriptions.name: caramel sulfite caustique
descriptions.description_en: Caramel sulfite caustique is an ultra-processed caramel coloring produced with sulfites, which may generate controversial by-products.

descriptions.name: carbonate d ammonium
descriptions.description_en: Carbonate d ammonium is an industrial raising agent that releases carbon dioxide and ammonia during baking, used in dry biscuits and crackers. Poorly baked or heavily dosed products may retain ammonia odor and cause irritation, but normal use is not a major health risk.

descriptions.name: carbonate de calcium
descriptions.description_en: Calcium carbonate is a natural source of dietary calcium essential for bone health.

descriptions.name: Carbonate de magnésium
descriptions.description_en: Magnesium carbonate supplies magnesium, supporting muscle and nerve function.

descriptions.name: carbonate de sodium
descriptions.description_en: Sodium carbonate (E500), an acidity regulator and raising agent used in noodles, baked goods and cocoa. It is neutralised in the finished food but contributes sodium and marks industrial processing.

descriptions.name: carotenes
descriptions.description_en: Carotenes act as antioxidants and convert to vitamin A, supporting vision and immunity.

descriptions.name: carotte
descriptions.description_en: Carrots provide beta-carotene for vitamin A and fiber, aiding vision and digestion.

descriptions.name: carraghenane
descriptions.description_en: A seaweed-derived thickener (E407) used in dairy, plant milks and processed meat. Food-grade carrageenan is authorised, but studies link it to gut inflammation and it is banned in EU infant formula.

descriptions.name: carraghenane degrade
descriptions.description_en: Degraded carrageenan, also called poligeenan, is the low-molecular-weight form and is classified IARC Group 2B, possibly carcinogenic. It has no authorised use as a food additive.

descriptions.name: caseinate
descriptions.description_en: Milk protein extracted with alkali and isolated from the rest of the dairy matrix. It is a purely technical ingredient used to bind and emulsify, and marks an industrially assembled recipe.

descriptions.name: cashew
descriptions.description_en: Rich in magnesium, zinc and healthy fats that support heart and immune health.

descriptions.name: catechin
descriptions.description_en: The main catechin in green tea, a well-studied antioxidant. Drunk as an infusion it raises no concern. As a concentrated extract it is a different matter: EFSA found in 2018 that 800 mg of EGCG per day or more from supplements raises liver enzymes, and the EU now requires warning labelling on green tea extracts. Read it as a good sign in tea, a caution in a supplement.

Read it as a good sign in tea, a caution in a supplement.

descriptions.name: caustic sulfite caramel
descriptions.description_en: Caustic sulfite caramel is an ultra-processed caramel coloring produced with sulfites and associated with controversial by-products. Its safety remains debated due to these by-products.

descriptions.name: caviar
descriptions.description_en: Fish roe is rich in omega-3 EPA and DHA, vitamin B12 and vitamin D. It is also salted heavily to preserve it, which makes it one of the saltiest foods on a table - it works as a delicacy in small spoonfuls, not as a portion.

descriptions.name: céleri
descriptions.description_en: Rich in fibre and potassium, which support digestion and heart health.

descriptions.name: celery juice
descriptions.description_en: Celery stalk or celeriac, simply dried and ground - harmless as a seasoning. Worth knowing, though, that the meat industry uses celery powder and celery juice as a natural nitrate source to cure meat labelled "no nitrites added": the body converts that nitrate to nitrite and the same nitroso-compounds form. On a charcuterie label it is a curing agent, not a vegetable.

descriptions.name: celery juice powder
descriptions.description_en: Celery stalk or celeriac, simply dried and ground - harmless as a seasoning. Worth knowing, though, that the meat industry uses celery powder and celery juice as a natural nitrate source to cure meat labelled "no nitrites added": the body converts that nitrate to nitrite and the same nitroso-compounds form. On a charcuterie label it is a curing agent, not a vegetable.

descriptions.name: celery powder
descriptions.description_en: Celery stalk or celeriac, simply dried and ground - harmless as a seasoning. Worth knowing, though, that the meat industry uses celery powder and celery juice as a natural nitrate source to cure meat labelled "no nitrites added": the body converts that nitrate to nitrite and the same nitroso-compounds form. On a charcuterie label it is a curing agent, not a vegetable.

descriptions.name: cellulose
descriptions.description_en: Plant cellulose (E460), used as an anti-caking agent and bulking fibre. It is not digested and behaves as insoluble fibre, but in processed food it usually replaces real ingredients.

descriptions.name: ceramides
descriptions.description_en: Ceramides help restore the skin's protective barrier and reduce water loss, improving skin hydration.

descriptions.name: ceteareth
descriptions.description_en: An ethoxylated emulsifier used to blend oil and water. The ethoxylation process can leave traces of 1,4-dioxane, a possible carcinogen, so manufacturers are expected to purify it out.

descriptions.name: champignon
descriptions.description_en: Mushrooms provide B vitamins, selenium, beta-glucans, and vitamin D, supporting immunity and bone health.

descriptions.name: chaource
descriptions.description_en: Soft ripened cheeses provide calcium, protein and vitamin B12, and develop their character through surface moulds. Because their moisture and low acidity suit listeria, health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid soft ripened cheeses unless they are made from pasteurised milk or have been cooked until steaming hot.

descriptions.name: charbon vegetal
descriptions.description_en: Vegetable carbon (E153), a black colourant made by carbonising plant material. It is authorised in the EU but adds no nutritional value and can bind medicines and nutrients in the gut.

descriptions.name: chataigne
descriptions.description_en: Chestnuts are rich in fiber and vitamin C, aiding digestion and immune defense.

descriptions.name: chaux
descriptions.description_en: Chaux, also known as slaked lime, firms foods, processes corn, and regulates acidity; concentrated forms can irritate mouth or digestion.

descriptions.name: cheddar deshydrate
descriptions.description_en: Cheese powder used to coat crisps and season mixes. It is very high in sodium and often blended with flavour enhancers and anti-caking agents rather than being simply dried cheese.

descriptions.name: chevre frais
descriptions.description_en: Fresh goat cheese provides protein and is lower in fat, often better tolerated than cow milk cheeses.

descriptions.name: chinook
descriptions.description_en: Chinook provides omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: chlorella
descriptions.description_en: A freshwater microalga dried into powder or tablets, rich in protein, iron and chlorophyll. Because it absorbs what its growing water contains, the quality of sourcing decides whether it also carries heavy metals - certified production matters more here than for most foods.

descriptions.name: chlorophylle
descriptions.description_en: Green plant pigments (E140/E141) used as colouring. The natural form is benign; the copper-stabilised version used for brighter colour adds a small amount of copper to the diet.

descriptions.name: chlorpyrifos
descriptions.description_en: An organophosphate insecticide banned across the EU since 2020. EFSA could not establish a safe exposure level, citing genotoxicity concerns and evidence of harm to brain development in children.

descriptions.name: chlorure de calcium
descriptions.description_en: Chlorure de calcium is a refined calcium salt used to firm vegetables, set cheese, and stabilize texture. High concentrations may irritate the digestive tract and taste bitter, but normal use is not a major health concern.

descriptions.name: chlorure de magnesium
descriptions.description_en: Chlorure de magnesium is a refined magnesium salt used in tofu, mineral fortification, and texture control. Large amounts may cause diarrhea, nausea, or abdominal cramping, especially with reduced kidney function.

descriptions.name: chocolat 100
descriptions.description_en: Pure 100% cocoa chocolate is rich in antioxidants, magnesium, and fiber, promoting overall nutrition.

descriptions.name: chocolat 100 cacao
descriptions.description_en: Pure 100% cocoa chocolate is rich in antioxidants, magnesium, and fiber, promoting overall nutrition.

descriptions.name: chocolat 70
descriptions.description_en: Dark chocolate is rich in heart-friendly flavonoids and magnesium, supporting cardiovascular health.

descriptions.name: chocolat 85
descriptions.description_en: Dark chocolate is rich in heart-friendly flavonoids and magnesium, supporting cardiovascular health.

descriptions.name: chocolat a patisser
descriptions.description_en: Pure cocoa mass chocolate supports heart health with antioxidants, magnesium, and fiber.

descriptions.name: chocolat noir
descriptions.description_en: Dark chocolate with high cocoa content supplies flavanols and minerals that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: chocolat noir 100
descriptions.description_en: Pure 100% cocoa chocolate is rich in antioxidants, magnesium, and fiber, promoting overall nutrition.

descriptions.name: chocolat non sucre
descriptions.description_en: Unsweetened chocolate is rich in flavanols, magnesium, and fiber, which benefit heart and digestive health.

descriptions.name: chocolat pur cacao
descriptions.description_en: Pure cocoa mass chocolate supports heart health with antioxidants, magnesium, and fiber.

descriptions.name: chocolat sans sucre
descriptions.description_en: Pure 100% cocoa chocolate is rich in antioxidants, magnesium, and fiber, promoting overall nutrition.

descriptions.name: chocolat sans sucre ajoute
descriptions.description_en: Pure 100% cocoa chocolate is rich in antioxidants, magnesium, and fiber, promoting overall nutrition.

descriptions.name: chocolate 100
descriptions.description_en: Chocolate 100 is pure 100% cocoa chocolate rich in antioxidants, magnesium, and fiber, promoting overall nutrition.

descriptions.name: chorizo
descriptions.description_en: A cured, paprika-spiced sausage. As a processed meat it falls under the IARC Group 1 classification: the curing and smoking process generates compounds tied to colorectal cancer.

descriptions.name: chou
descriptions.description_en: Cabbage is high in vitamins C and K and fiber, supporting immune function and gut health.

descriptions.name: chou-fleur
descriptions.description_en: Cruciferous vegetables provide fiber, vitamin C, and glucosinolates, aiding digestion and antioxidant protection.

descriptions.name: Chrome hexavalent (Cr VI)
descriptions.description_en: Chromium(VI) compounds are IARC Group 1 human carcinogens, causally linked to lung and nasal cancer. An industrial contaminant, notably from tanning and plating, with no legitimate use in consumer products.

descriptions.name: chum salmon
descriptions.description_en: Chum salmon is a wild fish rich in omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: cinq epices
descriptions.description_en: Five-spice powder provides natural antioxidants and essential nutrients from dried herbs and spices.

descriptions.name: cire d abeille
descriptions.description_en: Beeswax is a natural coating agent that is not absorbed by the body and is safe for consumption.

descriptions.name: cire de candelilla
descriptions.description_en: Candelilla wax is a plant-based coating that is not absorbed and serves as a vegan alternative to beeswax.

descriptions.name: cire de carnauba
descriptions.description_en: A plant wax from the leaves of the Brazilian carnauba palm, used to glaze sweets, chewing gum, coffee beans and coated tablets. EFSA re-evaluated it in 2012 and found no genotoxicity concern and sufficient margins of safety at authorised uses. It is practically not absorbed by the gut - the same conclusion reached for candelilla wax (E902).

descriptions.name: cire microcristalline
descriptions.description_en: A petroleum-derived wax (E905) used as a glazing and release agent. It is not absorbed by the body, but it originates from mineral oil refining rather than from a plant or animal source.

descriptions.name: citrate de sodium
descriptions.description_en: Citrate de sodium is an acidity-regulating salt made industrially, considered benign but indicative of ultra-processed foods.

descriptions.name: citrate de triethyle
descriptions.description_en: Citrate de triethyle is a manufactured citrate ester used as a carrier, solvent, or plasticizer for flavors and coatings. No major specific harm is established at authorized levels; total exposure should remain within the acceptable daily intake.

descriptions.name: citrate triammonique
descriptions.description_en: Triammonium citrate is an industrial ammonium salt with limited toxicological data available.

descriptions.name: citrem
descriptions.description_en: Citrem (E472c) is citric acid esters of mono- and diglycerides used to emulsify and prevent oxidation, an industrial recipe with no EFSA safety concern.

descriptions.name: citric acid
descriptions.description_en: The acid that gives citrus fruit its sharpness - though the E330 on a label is produced industrially by fermenting sugar with Aspergillus niger, not extracted from lemons. It is one of the most benign additives there is, used to adjust acidity and protect colour. Its only real drawback is that it erodes tooth enamel in acidic drinks.

descriptions.name: citron vert
descriptions.description_en: Lime supplies vitamin C and antioxidants that promote immune defense and skin vitality.

descriptions.name: citronnelle
descriptions.description_en: Citronnelle aids digestion and offers antioxidant benefits.

descriptions.name: clam
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: clams
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: clarified butter
descriptions.description_en: Clarified butter supplies healthy fats that help the body absorb fat-soluble vitamins.

descriptions.name: clementine
descriptions.description_en: Clementine is a citrus fruit rich in vitamin C, supporting immune function.

descriptions.name: cmc
descriptions.description_en: Carboxymethylcellulose (E466), a synthetic thickener made from cellulose. A controlled human trial found it altered the gut microbiome and intestinal lining, and it is a strong marker of ultra-processed food.

descriptions.name: coal tar
descriptions.description_en: A by-product of coal processing, historically used in anti-dandruff and psoriasis treatments and in dyes. Coal tars are IARC Group 1 human carcinogens; untreated preparations are restricted in EU cosmetics.

descriptions.name: cochenille
descriptions.description_en: Carmine (E120), a red colour made from crushed cochineal insects. It is natural rather than synthetic, but it is a recognised allergen that has caused severe reactions, and it is not vegetarian.

descriptions.name: cockle
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: coconut cream
descriptions.description_en: Coconut cream offers beneficial fats that contribute to heart and brain function.

descriptions.name: coeur
descriptions.description_en: Exceptionally rich in vitamin A, B12, iron and copper - one of the most nutrient-dense foods there is. Its preformed vitamin A is so concentrated that health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid liver and liver products entirely, and a single weekly portion is enough for everyone else.

descriptions.name: coho
descriptions.description_en: Coho is a wild fish rich in omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: coing
descriptions.description_en: Quince, mirabelle, greengage and morello cherry are stone or pome fruits eaten cooked or fresh, supplying fibre, potassium and polyphenols. Quince is always cooked, being too astringent raw.

descriptions.name: cold pressed coconut oil
descriptions.description_en: Cold pressed coconut oil is a basic culinary fat rich in medium-chain saturated fats that performs well in cooking and baking.

descriptions.name: collagene
descriptions.description_en: Collagen moisturizes and softens the skin surface without penetrating, helping to maintain skin hydration.

descriptions.name: colorant caramel
descriptions.description_en: Colorant caramel is an industrial caramel coloring often produced chemically, potentially containing carcinogenic 4-MEI (IARC Group 2B).

descriptions.name: Colorants azoïques textiles
descriptions.description_en: Textile azo dyes that can break down on the skin into benzidine and related aromatic amines, IARC Group 1 human carcinogens. Banned in the EU in textiles designed for prolonged skin contact.

descriptions.name: combava
descriptions.description_en: Aromatic leaves and rhizomes used fresh in South-East Asian cooking - kaffir lime leaf, lemongrass, galangal, fresh turmeric, ginger root and curry leaf. They are whole plant parts, used in small amounts, and carry the essential oils and antioxidants of the fresh plant.

descriptions.name: concentre de fruits
descriptions.description_en: Fruit or vegetable juice boiled down to concentrate its sugars. Manufacturers use it to sweeten products while keeping a natural-sounding label; the fibre is gone and the sugar behaves like added sugar.

descriptions.name: coque
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: coqueret
descriptions.description_en: Small tart fruits eaten fresh - physalis, tamarillo and feijoa. They are low in sugar and supply vitamin C, fibre and carotenoids.

descriptions.name: coquille saint jacques
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: cordyceps
descriptions.description_en: Medicinal mushrooms sold as dried powder or concentrated extract. They supply beta-glucans and are well tolerated as a food. As a supplement, reishi has been associated with rare cases of liver injury - the NIH LiverTox database describes clinically apparent injury as extremely rare, and reported cases mostly involve the unextracted powdered form, alcohol use or existing liver disease. It can also interact with anticoagulants. Treat it as a supplement with its own precautions, not as an ordinary mushroom.

descriptions.name: coriandre
descriptions.description_en: Concentrated antioxidants and essential oils in fresh herbs support overall health without added salt or sugar.

descriptions.name: corn starch modified
descriptions.description_en: A generic label covering any starch altered chemically or physically to thicken and stabilise industrial food, without saying which one. EFSA considers modified starches safe with no numerical ADI needed, but they are refined carbohydrates with no nutrients and one of the clearest markers of ultra-processing.

descriptions.name: cornichon naturel
descriptions.description_en: Vegetables preserved by lacto-fermentation in brine rather than vinegar. Live bacteria and organic acids survive in the jar as long as it has not been pasteurised, which supports gut flora. The salt in the brine is the only thing to keep an eye on.

descriptions.name: coulommiers
descriptions.description_en: Soft ripened cheeses provide calcium, protein and vitamin B12, and develop their character through surface moulds. Because their moisture and low acidity suit listeria, health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid soft ripened cheeses unless they are made from pasteurised milk or have been cooked until steaming hot.

descriptions.name: couscous complet
descriptions.description_en: Whole grains provide fibre and minerals for sustained energy and digestive health.

descriptions.name: crab
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: crabe
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: cranberries sechees
descriptions.description_en: Dried cranberries supply vitamins and antioxidants that help maintain urinary tract health.

descriptions.name: cranberry sechee
descriptions.description_en: Dried cranberry offers antioxidants and vitamins that promote immune system function.

descriptions.name: crayfish
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: creme
descriptions.description_en: Dairy fat in cream offers energy but should be consumed in moderation due to saturated fat.

descriptions.name: creme de coco
descriptions.description_en: Coconut cream contains healthy fats that help maintain skin and brain health.

descriptions.name: crevette
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: crevettes
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: criniere de lion
