descriptions.description_en: Medicinal mushrooms sold as dried powder or concentrated extract. They supply beta-glucans and are well tolerated as a food. As a supplement, reishi has been associated with rare cases of liver injury - the NIH LiverTox database describes clinically apparent injury as extremely rare, and reported cases mostly involve the unextracted powdered form, alcohol use or existing liver disease. It can also interact with anticoagulants. Treat it as a supplement with its own precautions, not as an ordinary mushroom.

descriptions.name: crottin
descriptions.description_en: Crottin goat cheese is lower in fat and easier to digest, benefiting those sensitive to cow milk.

descriptions.name: curcuma
descriptions.description_en: Curcumin in turmeric helps reduce inflammation when absorbed properly with fat and black pepper.

descriptions.name: curcuma frais
descriptions.description_en: Fresh turmeric (curcuma frais) contains curcumin, which supports anti-inflammatory processes.

descriptions.name: curcumin
descriptions.description_en: The yellow pigment of turmeric (E100), used as a natural colouring. It is a plant-derived alternative to synthetic yellow dyes and raises no safety concern at food levels. The anti-inflammatory effects attributed to curcumin come from concentrated supplement doses, not from the trace amount used to colour a food.

descriptions.name: curcumine
descriptions.description_en: The yellow pigment of turmeric (E100), used as a natural colouring. It is a plant-derived alternative to synthetic yellow dyes and raises no safety concern at food levels. The anti-inflammatory effects attributed to curcumin come from concentrated supplement doses, not from the trace amount used to colour a food.

descriptions.name: curry
descriptions.description_en: Curry benefits the body by supplying curcumin, which has anti-inflammatory properties.

descriptions.name: curry leaf
descriptions.description_en: Curry leaf promotes antioxidant activity and supports digestive health.

descriptions.name: cuttlefish
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: cyanocobalamine
descriptions.description_en: A stable added form of vitamin B12, widely used in fortified foods and supplements and important for anyone eating little animal produce. Safe at normal intake; it marks a fortified rather than naturally rich product.

descriptions.name: cyclamate
descriptions.description_en: An artificial sweetener (E952) still permitted in the EU but banned in the US since 1969 after bladder tumours appeared in rats. It has one of the lowest acceptable daily intakes of any sweetener.

descriptions.name: Cyclopentasiloxane D5
descriptions.description_en: A silicone that gives cosmetics a smooth, fast-drying feel. It is classified as very persistent and very bioaccumulative under EU chemical law, and its use in cosmetics is restricted in Europe.

descriptions.name: cyclosiloxane
descriptions.description_en: Cyclic silicones (cyclomethicone, D4, D5, D6) used for silky texture in hair and skin products. They are persistent in the environment and are progressively being restricted in EU cosmetics.

descriptions.name: Cyclotétrasiloxane D4
descriptions.description_en: A cyclic silicone classified in the EU as toxic to reproduction and as persistent and bioaccumulative. Its use in cosmetics is restricted in Europe, starting with rinse-off products.

descriptions.name: d allulose
descriptions.description_en: A rare sugar that sweetens with almost no calories and no effect on blood glucose. It is authorised in the United States, Canada, Japan and Korea, but not in the European Union or the UK, where it is still going through novel food assessment. Large amounts cause bloating and digestive upset.

descriptions.name: d-alpha tocopherol
descriptions.description_en: The natural RRR form of vitamin E, the one with the highest vitamin activity in the body. It protects cells and dietary fats from oxidation. EFSA re-evaluated the tocopherol family (E306-E309) in 2015 and found no safety concern at the levels used in food.

descriptions.name: dachine
descriptions.description_en: Starchy tropical roots that must always be cooked. Raw taro and raw yam contain calcium oxalate crystals and other compounds that irritate the mouth and digestive tract; cooking destroys them. Once cooked they are a good source of complex carbohydrate, potassium and fibre.

descriptions.name: daikon
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: dark chocolate 70
descriptions.description_en: Dark chocolate is rich in heart-friendly flavonoids and magnesium, supporting cardiovascular health.

descriptions.name: dark chocolate 85
descriptions.description_en: Dark chocolate 85 is rich in heart-friendly flavonoids and magnesium, supporting cardiovascular health.

descriptions.name: datem
descriptions.description_en: DATEM (E472e), a dough strengthener in industrial bread. EFSA found no safety concern in 2020, but laboratory work links it to gut microbiome disruption and a large French cohort tied higher intake to slightly raised type 2 diabetes risk.

descriptions.name: dates
descriptions.description_en: Rich in fibre, potassium and natural sugars — a nutritious energy source in moderation.

descriptions.name: datte
descriptions.description_en: Rich in fibre, potassium and natural sugars — a nutritious energy source in moderation.

descriptions.name: datte medjool
descriptions.description_en: Datte medjool contains natural sugars and fiber that help sustain energy and digestive health.

descriptions.name: dattes
descriptions.description_en: Dattes provide natural sugars and fiber that boost energy and support digestion.

descriptions.name: dattes medjool
descriptions.description_en: Medjool dates provide essential nutrients and natural energy to support overall health.

descriptions.name: DEA (Diéthanolamine)
descriptions.description_en: A foaming and pH-adjusting agent that can react with nitrites to form nitrosamines. Diethanolamine is prohibited in cosmetics in the European Union.

descriptions.name: defatted soy flour
descriptions.description_en: Soy flour with the oil removed by industrial solvent extraction, then used as a cheap protein filler. It is a highly processed commodity ingredient with little resemblance to whole soy.

descriptions.name: deglet nour
descriptions.description_en: Deglet Nour dates supply vital vitamins and minerals that promote bodily functions.

descriptions.name: delta-tocopherol
descriptions.description_en: Vitamin E from delta-tocopherol protects cells and oils from damage and supports nutrition.

descriptions.name: dextrine
descriptions.description_en: A partially broken-down starch used as a thickener, binder and bulking agent. It is a refined carbohydrate with a high glycemic response and no nutrients.

descriptions.name: dextrose
descriptions.description_en: Industrially refined pure glucose, usually from corn starch. Absorbed very rapidly, it causes sharp blood-sugar and insulin spikes with no nutritional benefit.

descriptions.name: diacetate de glyceryle
descriptions.description_en: Diacetate de glyceryle is a manufactured glycerol ester used to carry flavors, retain moisture, and improve processing. It is broken down into glycerol and acetic acid, and no major risk is established at permitted use.

descriptions.name: diacetate de sodium
descriptions.description_en: Diacetate de sodium (E262) is a preservative that adds salt-and-vinegar flavor to foods. It is well tolerated but adds sodium to the diet.

descriptions.name: diacetine
descriptions.description_en: Diacetine is a manufactured glycerol ester used to carry flavors, retain moisture, and improve processing. It is broken down into glycerol and acetic acid, and no major risk is established at permitted use.

descriptions.name: diazolidinyl urea
descriptions.description_en: A cosmetic preservative that works by slowly releasing formaldehyde, an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen. It is a known contact allergen and its use is capped under EU cosmetics rules.

descriptions.name: diglutamate de calcium
descriptions.description_en: A flavour enhancer (E623) used as a lower-sodium alternative to MSG. Considered safe at food levels, but it signals a product engineered on additives rather than ingredients.

descriptions.name: diglutamate de magnesium
descriptions.description_en: A flavour enhancer (E625) from the glutamate family, used to boost savoury taste in processed foods. Safe at normal intake, but characteristic of heavily seasoned industrial products.

descriptions.name: Diméthylformamide (DMF)
descriptions.description_en: An industrial solvent used in synthetic leather and coatings. It is classified as toxic to reproduction in the EU and is restricted under REACH, with strict limits on residues in consumer articles.

descriptions.name: dimethylpolysiloxane
descriptions.description_en: A silicone anti-foaming agent (E900) used mainly in frying oils and industrial cooking. It is inert and poorly absorbed, but it is a synthetic silicone typical of large-scale food production.

descriptions.name: dioxines
descriptions.description_en: Persistent industrial by-products that accumulate in animal fat and reach us mainly through meat, dairy and fish. TCDD is an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen, and EFSA cut the tolerable weekly intake sevenfold in 2018.

descriptions.name: dioxyde de carbone
descriptions.description_en: Carbon dioxide is inert in foods and drinks, posing no nutritional effect or residue.

descriptions.name: dioxyde de soufre
descriptions.description_en: A preservative and antioxidant (E220) common in wine, dried fruit and processed potato. It must be declared as an allergen in the EU above 10 mg/kg because it can trigger asthma attacks in sensitive people.

descriptions.name: dioxyde de titane
descriptions.description_en: A white colouring (E171) used in sweets, sauces and supplements. The EU banned it as a food additive in August 2022 after EFSA concluded that a concern for genotoxicity could not be ruled out and that no safe daily intake could be set. It remains permitted in the United States and in cosmetics.

descriptions.name: diphosphate
descriptions.description_en: Diphosphates (E450) used as raising agents and to retain water in meat and seafood. They add to total phosphate intake, which EFSA capped in 2019 over cardiovascular and kidney concerns.

descriptions.name: dmdm hydantoin
descriptions.description_en: One of the most common formaldehyde-releasing preservatives in shampoos and lotions. The formaldehyde it emits is an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen; EU rules restrict its level and require warning labelling.

descriptions.name: doogh
descriptions.description_en: Doogh supports hydration and provides beneficial probiotics for digestive health.

descriptions.name: doubanjiang
descriptions.description_en: Doubanjiang benefits the body by providing fermented vegetables that support digestive health.

descriptions.name: dried cranberries
descriptions.description_en: Dried berries rich in antioxidants and polyphenols that help protect the urinary tract.

descriptions.name: dried cranberry
descriptions.description_en: A dried berry rich in antioxidants and polyphenols that help protect the urinary tract.

descriptions.name: dukkah
descriptions.description_en: Dukkah benefits the body by providing natural antioxidants and essential nutrients from dried herbs and spices.

descriptions.name: dulse
descriptions.description_en: Seaweed provides iodine, iron, magnesium and soluble fibre, supporting thyroid function and overall nutrition. Nori and wakame are moderate, but kombu is by far the most iodine-dense food known and can disturb thyroid function if eaten regularly - health agencies advise limiting it, and using it for stock rather than eating it.

descriptions.name: e100
descriptions.description_en: The yellow pigment of turmeric (E100), used as a natural colouring. It is a plant-derived alternative to synthetic yellow dyes and raises no safety concern at food levels. The anti-inflammatory effects attributed to curcumin come from concentrated supplement doses, not from the trace amount used to colour a food.

descriptions.name: e131
descriptions.description_en: E131 is a synthetic blue dye used only to change appearance and provide no nutritional value. People with a history of reactions to synthetic dyes should be cautious due to possible hypersensitivity.

descriptions.name: e1404
descriptions.description_en: Starch chemically oxidised (E1404) to improve thickening, clarity and processing performance. EFSA's 2017 re-evaluation of the whole modified-starch family found no safety concern and no genotoxic concern. Its role is purely technological: a refined carbohydrate that signals an industrially engineered texture.

descriptions.name: e1413
descriptions.description_en: A cross-linked and phosphorylated starch (E1413) designed to resist heat, acid and mechanical processing. EFSA found no safety concern for the modified-starch family, but the additive brings no nutrition and marks a heavily formulated product.

descriptions.name: e1440
descriptions.description_en: A chemically modified starch (E1440) that stays stable through freezing, heating and storage. EFSA's 2017 opinion raised no safety or genotoxicity concern, but it is a refined carbohydrate whose only purpose is texture in industrial recipes.

descriptions.name: e1442
descriptions.description_en: One of the most common modified starches (E1442), used in sauces, desserts and ready meals to hold texture through heating and freezing. EFSA's 2017 re-evaluation found no safety concern and set no numerical ADI, but it is a purely technical refined carbohydrate and a clear marker of ultra-processed food.

descriptions.name: e1450
descriptions.description_en: Starch modified with octenyl succinic anhydride (E1450) to act as an emulsifier and encapsulating agent in drinks, dressings and powdered flavourings. EFSA's 2017 re-evaluation of modified starches found no safety concern and no need for a numerical ADI, but it remains a refined carbohydrate with no nutrients and a marker of industrial formulation.

descriptions.name: e1451
descriptions.description_en: A starch both oxidised and acetylated (E1451) to improve stability, clarity and texture. EFSA found no safety concern for the modified-starch family, but the double chemical treatment leaves a refined carbohydrate used purely as a structural ingredient.

descriptions.name: e150
descriptions.description_en: E150 is an industrial caramel coloring usually made by chemical processes involving ammonia or sulfites, generating possibly carcinogenic 4-MEI (IARC Group 2B). Its consumption may carry cancer risk concerns.

descriptions.name: e1505
descriptions.description_en: E1505 is a manufactured citrate ester used as a carrier, solvent, or plasticizer for flavors and coatings. No major specific harm is established at authorized levels; total exposure should remain within the acceptable daily intake.

descriptions.name: e150b
descriptions.description_en: E150b is an ultra-processed caramel coloring produced with sulfites and associated with controversial by-products. The health implications of these by-products are uncertain.

descriptions.name: e150c
descriptions.description_en: E150c is an ultra-processed caramel coloring produced with ammonia and contains 4-MEI, classified as possibly carcinogenic (IARC Group 2B). Health considerations include potential carcinogenic effects.

descriptions.name: e151
descriptions.description_en: E151 is a synthetic black dye used in confectionery, sauces, and decorations. Frequent consumption can increase exposure beyond intended daily use, especially in children.

descriptions.name: e1517
descriptions.description_en: E1517 is a manufactured glycerol ester used to carry flavors, retain moisture, and improve processing. It is broken down into glycerol and acetic acid, and no major risk is established at permitted use.

descriptions.name: e1519
descriptions.description_en: E1519 is an aromatic alcohol used mainly as a solvent or carrier in flavorings. Large systemic doses can depress the nervous system and disturb metabolism; newborns are particularly vulnerable to high medicinal exposure, although food amounts are far lower.

descriptions.name: e155
descriptions.description_en: E155 is a synthetic brown dye used in bakery, dessert, and confectionery products. Repeated high intake from multiple colored products is a health concern, especially for children.

descriptions.name: e160a
descriptions.description_en: Beta carotene (E160a) is an orange plant pigment converted to vitamin A and acts as an antioxidant.

descriptions.name: e160c
descriptions.description_en: E160c is a concentrated red-orange color extracted from paprika and standardized for pigment strength. Quality control is important for solvent residues and purity; rare allergic reactions may occur in sensitive individuals.

descriptions.name: e160d
descriptions.description_en: Lycopene (E160d) is the red pigment of tomatoes and a well-studied dietary antioxidant.

descriptions.name: e161b
descriptions.description_en: Lutein (E161b) is a yellow carotenoid from marigold and greens that supports eye health.

descriptions.name: e170
descriptions.description_en: E170 is a natural source of calcium, an essential mineral beneficial for the body and safe at usual doses.

descriptions.name: e171
descriptions.description_en: A white colouring (E171) used in sweets, sauces and supplements. The EU banned it as a food additive in August 2022 after EFSA concluded that a concern for genotoxicity could not be ruled out and that no safe daily intake could be set. It remains permitted in the United States and in cosmetics.

descriptions.name: e174
descriptions.description_en: Silver (E174), used as a decorative coating on confectionery. EFSA could not conclude on its safety in 2016, and its 2025 follow-up confirmed that the data on nanoparticle content, silver-ion release and genotoxicity are still inadequate. Nearly a decade on, its safety as a food additive remains officially unresolved.

descriptions.name: e175
descriptions.description_en: Gold leaf (E175) used to decorate confectionery and drinks. EFSA re-evaluated it in 2016 and concluded that, given the very low solubility of elemental gold, systemic absorption and systemic effects are not expected. It passes through the body unchanged and adds nothing nutritionally - purely decorative.

descriptions.name: e203
descriptions.description_en: A preservative deleted from the EU list of authorised food additives in 2018 because no company ever supplied the genotoxicity data EFSA had asked for - a data gap, not a proven toxicity. EFSA had already excluded it from the group ADI shared by sorbic acid (E200) and potassium sorbate (E202), partly because the related sodium salt tested positive for genotoxicity. It is no longer permitted in EU food.

descriptions.name: e213
descriptions.description_en: E213 is a synthetic preservative that releases benzoate to slow microbial growth in acidic foods and drinks. Sensitive individuals may experience hives or asthma-like reactions, and high exposure should stay below the acceptable daily intake.

descriptions.name: e214
descriptions.description_en: E214 is a synthetic paraben preservative used to prevent mold and bacterial growth, with weak hormone-like activity studied experimentally. No cancer claim is justified at authorized levels, but repeated combined exposure to parabens is a concern.

descriptions.name: e215
descriptions.description_en: E215 is the water-soluble sodium form of ethyl paraben, contributing to the combined paraben exposure limit. The main concern is cumulative exposure to parabens rather than immediate toxicity at permitted levels.

descriptions.name: e216
descriptions.description_en: A paraben preservative removed from the EU list of authorised food additives in 2006, after EFSA judged that the presumed safe intake was no longer valid because of effects on sex hormones and male reproductive organs in young rats. No food ADI has been accepted since. It is still permitted in US food, and was banned from foods in California in 2023.

descriptions.name: e217
descriptions.description_en: E217 is the sodium form of propyl paraben, no longer authorized in the EU due to uncertain reproductive toxicity safety. It should be avoided as a declared additive where unauthorized, especially due to repeated exposure concerns.

descriptions.name: e219
descriptions.description_en: E219 is the sodium salt of methyl paraben, a synthetic preservative that dissolves easily in water. Repeated exposure from multiple sources is more relevant than a single food serving for health considerations.

descriptions.name: e251
descriptions.description_en: A curing salt (E251) that the body converts to nitrite, which can then form nitrosamines. IARC rates ingested nitrate under conditions leading to endogenous nitrosation as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic. The confirmed Group 1 classification applies to processed meat as a food, not to the additive on its own.

descriptions.name: e260
descriptions.description_en: Vinegar acid (E260) helps preserve food and slightly lowers blood sugar response when taken with meals.

descriptions.name: e290
descriptions.description_en: Carbon dioxide (E290) benefits the body by being inert and leaving no residues after use in food and drinks.

descriptions.name: e296
descriptions.description_en: E296 is an industrially synthesized compound rarely extracted from fruit. Its occasional use reflects its synthetic origin in food processing.

descriptions.name: e300
descriptions.description_en: E300, known as ascorbic acid, helps protect cells from oxidative damage and supports immune health.

descriptions.name: e301
descriptions.description_en: Sodium ascorbate (E301) supports antioxidant activity and helps maintain healthy vitamin C levels in the body.

descriptions.name: e302
descriptions.description_en: Calcium ascorbate (E302) provides vitamin C and calcium, supporting immune function and bone health.

descriptions.name: e306
descriptions.description_en: A natural vitamin E mixture extracted from vegetable oils (E306), used to stop fats going rancid. EFSA's 2015 re-evaluation of the tocopherol family found no safety concern at dietary exposures. It is one of the most benign antioxidants available, and a better sign on a label than synthetic BHA or BHT.

descriptions.name: e307a
descriptions.description_en: The natural RRR form of vitamin E, the one with the highest vitamin activity in the body. It protects cells and dietary fats from oxidation. EFSA re-evaluated the tocopherol family (E306-E309) in 2015 and found no safety concern at the levels used in food.

descriptions.name: e308
descriptions.description_en: E308 is a natural form of vitamin E (gamma-tocopherol) from vegetable oils that acts as an antioxidant.

descriptions.name: e309
descriptions.description_en: E309 is a natural form of vitamin E (delta-tocopherol) from vegetable oils that acts as an antioxidant.

descriptions.name: e311
descriptions.description_en: Propyl, octyl and dodecyl gallate (E310–E312) are synthetic antioxidants preventing fat rancidity. They may cause contact allergy and are limited in infant foods.

descriptions.name: e330
descriptions.description_en: The acid that gives citrus fruit its sharpness - though the E330 on a label is produced industrially by fermenting sugar with Aspergillus niger, not extracted from lemons. It is one of the most benign additives there is, used to adjust acidity and protect colour. Its only real drawback is that it erodes tooth enamel in acidic drinks.

descriptions.name: e331
descriptions.description_en: E331 is an acidity-regulating salt made industrially from citric acid and sodium hydroxide with no natural food form; it is a benign additive but indicates ultra-processing.

descriptions.name: e363
descriptions.description_en: E363 is an industrial acidifier with limited long-term research available. Its health effects are not fully understood, so use is occasional.

descriptions.name: e380
descriptions.description_en: E380 is an industrial ammonium salt with limited toxicological data available. Its safety profile is not well established, so consumption should be occasional.

descriptions.name: e406
descriptions.description_en: E406, agar-agar, supports digestive health as a source of dietary fiber.

descriptions.name: e412
descriptions.description_en: E412 is an industrial gelling agent that may cause bloating and digestive discomfort. It is used to thicken and stabilize foods.

descriptions.name: e415
descriptions.description_en: E415 is an additive that may disrupt digestion in sensitive people. It can cause digestive issues for some individuals.

descriptions.name: e425
descriptions.description_en: E425 is an additive that carries a risk of intestinal blockage. Care should be taken when consuming products containing it.

descriptions.name: e426
descriptions.description_en: E426 is a processed fiber fraction from soybeans used to thicken and stabilize food products. Residual soy proteins may affect people with severe soy allergies despite low toxicity of the additive.

descriptions.name: e440
descriptions.description_en: E440, or pectin, benefits digestive health by promoting gut flora balance and regularity.

descriptions.name: e441
descriptions.description_en: Collagen extracted from animal skin and bone by acid or alkali treatment (E441). It is a safe, protein-based gelling agent, though of animal origin and low in nutritional value. Not suitable for vegetarians, or for halal and kosher diets unless certified.

descriptions.name: e471
descriptions.description_en: Mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids (E471), used to blend fat and water. Widely permitted, but they can contain traces of trans fats depending on the source oil, and they mark an industrial recipe.

descriptions.name: e472d
descriptions.description_en: E472d are chemically modified fats used to strengthen dough and control texture in processed foods. No major disease risk is established at authorized levels, but cumulative intake and impurities are concerns.

descriptions.name: e472f
descriptions.description_en: E472f is a complex emulsifier made by chemically esterifying mono- and diglycerides, enhancing dough and shelf life. Purity, tartaric-acid exposure, and frequent consumption of processed foods are health considerations.

descriptions.name: e482
descriptions.description_en: E482 is sodium stearoyl lactylate (E481), a dough conditioner that improves volume and shelf life in industrial bread. It is authorized at limited levels but unnecessary in traditional bread.

descriptions.name: e492
descriptions.description_en: E492 is a sorbitan emulsifier used to stabilise fats in baked goods and confectionery, under study for gut lining effects.

descriptions.name: e493
descriptions.description_en: E493 is a sorbitan emulsifier used to stabilise fats in baked goods and confectionery, under study for gut lining effects.

descriptions.name: e494
descriptions.description_en: E494 is a sorbitan emulsifier used to stabilise fats in baked goods and confectionery, under study for gut lining effects.

descriptions.name: e503
descriptions.description_en: E503 is an industrial raising agent releasing carbon dioxide and ammonia during baking, common in dry biscuits and crackers. Poorly baked or heavily dosed products may retain ammonia odor and cause irritation, but normal use is not a major health risk.

descriptions.name: e504
descriptions.description_en: E504 are refined magnesium salts used to prevent clumping and regulate acidity in foods. Large doses can cause diarrhea and abdominal cramping, but typical additive amounts are much lower.

descriptions.name: e509
descriptions.description_en: E509 is a refined calcium salt used to firm vegetables, set cheese, and stabilize texture. High concentrations may irritate the digestive tract and taste bitter, but normal use is not a major health concern.

descriptions.name: e511
descriptions.description_en: E511 is a refined magnesium salt used in tofu, mineral fortification, and texture control. Large amounts may cause diarrhea, nausea, or abdominal cramping, especially with reduced kidney function.

descriptions.name: e514
descriptions.description_en: E514 consists of refined sulfate salts used for processing and acidity control; large doses can cause diarrhea by drawing water into the intestine. Sodium-containing forms also contribute to total sodium intake.

descriptions.name: e515
descriptions.description_en: E515 is a refined potassium salt used to regulate acidity or support processing; people with kidney disease must avoid excessive potassium intake. Excess potassium can disturb heart rhythm in sensitive individuals.

descriptions.name: e518
descriptions.description_en: E518 is an industrial laxative at high doses that can disrupt electrolyte balance. Excessive intake may cause health issues.

descriptions.name: e520
descriptions.description_en: E520 is an aluminum-containing processing salt used in limited applications that contributes to total dietary aluminum exposure. Aluminum can accumulate, so repeated exposure may exceed tolerable weekly levels, especially in those with reduced kidney function.

descriptions.name: e521
descriptions.description_en: E521 is an aluminum- and sodium-containing industrial salt used in baking powders and processing applications. Frequent consumption raises concerns due to cumulative aluminum and sodium exposure.

descriptions.name: e522
descriptions.description_en: Potassium alum (E522) is a firming or processing agent that adds aluminum to the diet. Health concerns focus on cumulative aluminum exposure, not immediate effects.

descriptions.name: e523
descriptions.description_en: E523 is an aluminum-containing industrial salt used for firming or processing in limited foods. Repeated intake contributes to total aluminum exposure, which can accumulate in the body.

descriptions.name: e528
descriptions.description_en: E528 is a refined magnesium compound used to regulate acidity and acts as a laxative at medicinal doses. Too much can cause diarrhea, cramping, and magnesium accumulation in people with kidney impairment.

descriptions.name: e530
descriptions.description_en: E530 is a refined magnesium compound used to prevent clumping or regulate acidity. Large doses may cause diarrhea or magnesium accumulation, particularly in people with impaired kidney function.

descriptions.name: e541
descriptions.description_en: E541 is an acidic aluminum salt used in baking powders to control gas release; it adds aluminum and sodium, increasing exposure risks if heavily consumed.

descriptions.name: e542
descriptions.description_en: Bone phosphate (E542), a calcium phosphate obtained by degreasing and calcining animal bones, used in small amounts to keep powders free-flowing. It is of animal origin, so it does not suit vegetarian, vegan, halal or kosher diets unless specifically certified, and it adds to total phosphate intake, which EFSA already considers high in European diets. Its use in food today is marginal.

descriptions.name: e553b
descriptions.description_en: Food-grade talc (E553b) used to stop powders sticking and clumping. IARC reclassified talc as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic to humans, in 2024, on limited evidence in humans, sufficient evidence in animals and strong mechanistic evidence. A separate and older concern is contamination with asbestos, which occurs naturally alongside talc deposits and is a confirmed Group 1 carcinogen.

descriptions.name: e572
descriptions.description_en: E572 is an industrial lubricating agent that may reduce nutrient absorption. Its use should be occasional to minimize potential effects.

descriptions.name: e576
descriptions.description_en: E576 is a refined sodium salt used to bind metals, stabilize products, and control acidity. Its main nutritional concern is added sodium rather than specific toxicity.

descriptions.name: e577
descriptions.description_en: E577 is a potassium salt used for mineral fortification and product stability. Excess potassium can be dangerous for people with kidney disease or medicines that impair potassium removal.

descriptions.name: e578
descriptions.description_en: E578 is a calcium salt used for firming, fortification, and stabilization. Very high calcium intake can cause constipation and may be unsuitable for people with certain kidney or calcium-balance disorders.

descriptions.name: e626
descriptions.description_en: E626, guanylic acid, is an umami flavor enhancer that boosts MSG effects and is not advised for people with gout due to purines.

descriptions.name: e627
descriptions.description_en: E627, disodium guanylate, is an umami enhancer in instant soups that multiplies MSG effects and is not advised for gout sufferers.

descriptions.name: e630
descriptions.description_en: E630, inosinic acid, is an umami enhancer from bacterial fermentation that boosts MSG taste and is not advised for people with gout.

descriptions.name: e633
descriptions.description_en: E633, calcium inosinate, is a rare umami enhancer from ribonucleotides and is not advised for people with gout.

descriptions.name: e634
descriptions.description_en: E634, calcium ribonucleotides, is a blend of calcium salts of inosinic and guanylic acids used as an umami enhancer and not advised for gout.

descriptions.name: e902
descriptions.description_en: E902 is a plant wax from a Mexican shrub that provides a vegan alternative to beeswax and shellac.

descriptions.name: e903
descriptions.description_en: A plant wax from the leaves of the Brazilian carnauba palm, used to glaze sweets, chewing gum, coffee beans and coated tablets. EFSA re-evaluated it in 2012 and found no genotoxicity concern and sufficient margins of safety at authorised uses. It is practically not absorbed by the gut - the same conclusion reached for candelilla wax (E902).

descriptions.name: e967
descriptions.description_en: A polyol sweetener used in sugar-free gum, sweets and drinks. It is dose-dependently laxative, and a 2024 European Heart Journal study linked circulating xylitol to major cardiovascular events and showed heightened platelet reactivity in every volunteer after ingestion. The evidence is associative plus mechanistic rather than causal, but it places xylitol alongside erythritol rather than with the other polyols.

descriptions.name: e968
descriptions.description_en: A polyol sweetener produced by fermentation. EFSA re-evaluated it in 2023 and, for the first time ever, set an ADI based on an immediate effect - diarrhoea - at 0.5 g/kg body weight per day, then concluded that both acute and chronic intake exceed that ADI in every age group. Separate Cleveland Clinic work links circulating erythritol to platelet reactivity and cardiovascular events; that is association plus mechanism rather than proof, but it is enough to set it apart from older polyols.

descriptions.name: eau
descriptions.description_en: Water hydrates the body without calories or additives, supporting all bodily functions.

descriptions.name: eau de coco
descriptions.description_en: Eau de coco hydrates the body with natural electrolytes and supports fluid balance.

descriptions.name: Eau de Javel (hypochlorite)
descriptions.description_en: Sodium hypochlorite bleach, an effective disinfectant that is corrosive to skin, eyes and airways. Mixed with ammonia or acidic cleaners it releases toxic gases, and it should never be combined with other products.

descriptions.name: ecrevisse
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: edam
descriptions.description_en: Edam cheese provides essential nutrients from milk with no additives in traditional recipes.

descriptions.name: edible bone phosphate
descriptions.description_en: Bone phosphate (E542), a calcium phosphate obtained by degreasing and calcining animal bones, used in small amounts to keep powders free-flowing. It is of animal origin, so it does not suit vegetarian, vegan, halal or kosher diets unless specifically certified, and it adds to total phosphate intake, which EFSA already considers high in European diets. Its use in food today is marginal.

descriptions.name: edta
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic chelator (E385) that traps metal ions to stop fats going rancid and colours fading. Authorised at limited levels, it can also bind minerals the body needs and does not occur in nature.

descriptions.name: egcg
descriptions.description_en: The main catechin in green tea, a well-studied antioxidant. Drunk as an infusion it raises no concern. As a concentrated extract it is a different matter: EFSA found in 2018 that 800 mg of EGCG per day or more from supplements raises liver enzymes, and the EU now requires warning labelling on green tea extracts. Read it as a good sign in tea, a caution in a supplement.

descriptions.name: emulsifiant
descriptions.description_en: Emulsifiant is an additive that may contain hidden trans fats. Consumption of trans fats can negatively affect heart health.

descriptions.name: emulsifiants
descriptions.description_en: Emulsifiants are additives that may contain hidden trans fats. Consumption of trans fats can negatively affect heart health.

descriptions.name: emulsifier
descriptions.description_en: An emulsifier is an additive that may contain hidden trans fats. Consumption of trans fats can negatively affect heart health.

descriptions.name: emulsifiers
descriptions.description_en: Emulsifiers are additives that may contain hidden trans fats. Consumption of trans fats can negatively affect heart health.

descriptions.name: encornet
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: epeautre
descriptions.description_en: Higher protein and minerals in spelt support muscle and bone health and may aid digestion.

descriptions.name: epigallocatechin
descriptions.description_en: The main catechin in green tea, a well-studied antioxidant. Drunk as an infusion it raises no concern. As a concentrated extract it is a different matter: EFSA found in 2018 that 800 mg of EGCG per day or more from supplements raises liver enzymes, and the EU now requires warning labelling on green tea extracts. Read it as a good sign in tea, a caution in a supplement.

descriptions.name: epigallocatechin gallate
descriptions.description_en: The main catechin in green tea, a well-studied antioxidant. Drunk as an infusion it raises no concern. As a concentrated extract it is a different matter: EFSA found in 2018 that 800 mg of EGCG per day or more from supplements raises liver enzymes, and the EU now requires warning labelling on green tea extracts. Read it as a good sign in tea, a caution in a supplement.

descriptions.name: epigallocatechine
descriptions.description_en: The main catechin in green tea, a well-studied antioxidant. Drunk as an infusion it raises no concern. As a concentrated extract it is a different matter: EFSA found in 2018 that 800 mg of EGCG per day or more from supplements raises liver enzymes, and the EU now requires warning labelling on green tea extracts. Read it as a good sign in tea, a caution in a supplement.

descriptions.name: epinard
descriptions.description_en: Folate, vitamin K, magnesium, and iron in spinach support blood health and vision.

descriptions.name: epoisses
descriptions.description_en: Epoisses offers protein and essential fats, but its high fat and salt content should be consumed in moderation.

descriptions.name: erythorbate de sodium
descriptions.description_en: An antioxidant (E316) that is a mirror-image form of vitamin C, used to keep cured meat pink and fats fresh. It is safe, but it has no vitamin activity and appears mostly in processed meat.

descriptions.name: erythritol
descriptions.description_en: A polyol sweetener produced by fermentation. EFSA re-evaluated it in 2023 and, for the first time ever, set an ADI based on an immediate effect - diarrhoea - at 0.5 g/kg body weight per day, then concluded that both acute and chronic intake exceed that ADI in every age group. Separate Cleveland Clinic work links circulating erythritol to platelet reactivity and cardiovascular events; that is association plus mechanism rather than proof, but it is enough to set it apart from older polyols.

descriptions.name: espadon
descriptions.description_en: Long-lived top predators that concentrate the most methylmercury of any commercial fish. The FDA and EPA place swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel, bigeye tuna, orange roughy and Gulf tilefish on the Choices to Avoid list: pregnant women, breastfeeding women and children should not eat them at all, and other adults only rarely.

descriptions.name: esters acetiques
descriptions.description_en: Acetic acid esters of mono- and diglycerides (E472a), an emulsifier used to stabilise fats in industrial baking and desserts. EFSA raised no safety concern, but it is a purely technical ingredient.

descriptions.name: esters acetiques et tartriques de mono et diglycerides
descriptions.description_en: Esters acetiques et tartriques de mono et diglycerides improve dough performance, volume, and shelf stability in industrial foods. Frequent consumption and purity levels should be considered for health.

descriptions.name: esters citriques
descriptions.description_en: Citric acid esters of mono- and diglycerides (E472c), used to emulsify and prevent oxidation. EFSA found no safety concern, though it marks an industrially assembled recipe.

descriptions.name: esters de propylene glycol
descriptions.description_en: Propylene glycol esters of fatty acids (E477), used to aerate whipped toppings and cake mixes. Permitted at capped levels, and characteristic of ultra-processed desserts.

descriptions.name: esters de sucrose
descriptions.description_en: Sucrose esters of fatty acids (E473), synthetic emulsifiers built from sugar and fat. They are authorised at limited levels but belong to the emulsifier family under study for effects on the gut lining.

descriptions.name: esters lactiques
descriptions.description_en: Lactic acid esters of mono- and diglycerides (E472b), used to aerate whipped and baked products. Considered safe by EFSA, it is a chemically modified fat with no nutritional role.

descriptions.name: esters mono et diacetyltartriques
descriptions.description_en: Esters mono et diacetyltartriques (DATEM, E472e) strengthen dough in industrial bread but may disrupt gut microbiome and slightly raise diabetes risk.

descriptions.name: esters monoacetyltartriques
descriptions.description_en: Esters monoacetyltartriques (DATEM, E472e) strengthen dough in industrial bread but may disrupt gut microbiome and slightly raise diabetes risk.

descriptions.name: esters polyglyceriques
descriptions.description_en: Polyglycerol esters of fatty acids (E475), used to emulsify cakes, ice cream and spreads. Permitted at capped levels, and a clear marker of ultra-processed formulation.

descriptions.name: esters tartriques
descriptions.description_en: Esters tartriques are chemically modified fats used to strengthen dough and control texture in processed foods. No major disease risk is established at authorized levels, but cumulative intake and impurities are concerns.

descriptions.name: esters tartriques de mono et diglycerides
descriptions.description_en: Esters tartriques de mono et diglycerides are chemically modified fats used to strengthen dough and control texture in processed foods. No major disease risk is established at authorized levels, but cumulative intake and impurities are concerns.

descriptions.name: ethyl paraben
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic paraben preservative used to prevent mold and bacterial growth. Experimental research has examined weak hormone-like activity, so exposure is controlled through a combined acceptable daily intake. Health: No cancer claim is justified at authorized food levels. The relevant concern is repeated combined exposure to several parabens.

descriptions.name: ethylcellulose
descriptions.description_en: A modified cellulose (E462) used as a binder and film former. It is indigestible and considered safe, serving a purely technical role in manufacturing.

descriptions.name: ethylparaben
descriptions.description_en: A preservative (E214/E215) permitted in a narrow range of EU foods. Parabens have weak oestrogen-like activity in laboratory studies; the ethyl form is among the least potent of the family.

descriptions.name: ethylparabene
descriptions.description_en: Ethylparabene is a synthetic paraben preservative used to prevent mold and bacterial growth, with weak hormone-like activity studied experimentally. No cancer claim is justified at authorized levels, but repeated combined exposure to parabens is a concern.

descriptions.name: ethylparabene sodique
descriptions.description_en: Ethylparabene sodique is the water-soluble sodium form of ethyl paraben, contributing to the combined paraben exposure limit. The main concern is cumulative exposure to parabens rather than immediate toxicity at permitted levels.

descriptions.name: eucheuma transforme
descriptions.description_en: Processed eucheuma seaweed (E407a), a cheaper, less purified relative of carrageenan. It shares carrageenan's concerns about gut inflammation and is banned in EU infant formula.

descriptions.name: extra virgin coconut oil
descriptions.description_en: Extra virgin coconut oil is a basic culinary fat rich in medium-chain saturated fats that performs well in cooking and baking.

descriptions.name: extra virgin olive oil
descriptions.description_en: Extra virgin olive oil is a basic culinary fat rich in monounsaturated fatty acids and antioxidant polyphenols.

descriptions.name: extrait d'epices
descriptions.description_en: Spice extract is obtained by industrial solvent extraction, differing significantly from whole spices. Its processing may reduce natural benefits and alter health effects.

descriptions.name: extrait de fruit du moine
descriptions.description_en: A sweetener from the luo han guo fruit, with no calories and no effect on blood sugar. It has a long history of use in Asia and is widely permitted in North America. In the EU only an aqueous decoction of the fruit has been authorised, while purified mogroside V - the form used in most imported products - is still awaiting authorisation.

descriptions.name: extrait de ginseng
descriptions.description_en: An Asian root traditionally used against fatigue, sold today mostly as a concentrated extract. It is not inert: it interacts with anticoagulants and diabetes medication, can disturb sleep at higher doses, and is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

descriptions.name: extrait de levure
descriptions.description_en: Yeast broken down to release its natural glutamate, giving a savoury boost without an “MSG” label. It is safe, but it plays the same role as a flavour enhancer while sounding more natural.

descriptions.name: extrait de paprika
descriptions.description_en: Capsanthin and carotenoids in paprika extract provide antioxidant support for cells.

descriptions.name: extrait de paprika standardise
descriptions.description_en: Extrait de paprika standardise is a concentrated red-orange color extracted from paprika and standardized for pigment strength. Quality control is important for solvent residues and purity; rare allergic reactions may occur in sensitive individuals.

descriptions.name: Extrait de romarin
descriptions.description_en: Rosemary extract's polyphenols protect cells by reducing oxidative stress.

descriptions.name: extrait de spiruline
descriptions.description_en: A cyanobacterium dried into powder, dense in plant protein, iron and antioxidants. One caveat matters: the B12 it contains is pseudo-B12, inactive in humans, so it cannot be counted as a B12 source on a plant-based diet. Sourcing also matters, since poorly controlled production can carry microcystin contamination.

descriptions.name: extrait de the vert concentre
descriptions.description_en: The main catechin in green tea, a well-studied antioxidant. Drunk as an infusion it raises no concern. As a concentrated extract it is a different matter: EFSA found in 2018 that 800 mg of EGCG per day or more from supplements raises liver enzymes, and the EU now requires warning labelling on green tea extracts. Read it as a good sign in tea, a caution in a supplement.

descriptions.name: extrait riche en tocopherols
descriptions.description_en: A natural vitamin E mixture extracted from vegetable oils (E306), used to stop fats going rancid. EFSA's 2015 re-evaluation of the tocopherol family found no safety concern at dietary exposures. It is one of the most benign antioxidants available, and a better sign on a label than synthetic BHA or BHT.

descriptions.name: faba bean protein
descriptions.description_en: Fava bean protein is extracted by dry milling and air classification, rich in lysine and allergen-free but still a protein concentrate; it is acceptable as a supplement but not as the sole protein source.

descriptions.name: farine de ble blanche
descriptions.description_en: Wheat flour with the bran and germ milled out. It keeps the starch and part of the protein but loses most of the fibre, magnesium and B vitamins of the grain, and raises blood sugar faster. Wholemeal flour is the same ingredient with its nutrition intact.

descriptions.name: farine de ble enrichie
descriptions.description_en: White flour with a few vitamins and iron added back after refining stripped them out. The fortification helps, but the fibre and most micronutrients of the whole grain are gone for good.

descriptions.name: farine de maïs
descriptions.description_en: Corn milled into flour or semolina. Unlike cornstarch it keeps part of the grain's protein and fibre, but its glycemic index stays high once cooked. Naturally gluten-free.

descriptions.name: farine de pois
descriptions.description_en: Dried yellow peas simply milled into flour, with no chemical extraction. Unlike a protein isolate it keeps the whole pea's fibre and starch, making it one of the least processed plant-protein ingredients.

descriptions.name: farine de pois chiche
descriptions.description_en: Flour from chickpeas is a plant-based protein source rich in fiber and iron, obtained by milling and water separation. It is useful as a supplement but less complete than whole chickpeas.

descriptions.name: farine de pomme de terre
descriptions.description_en: Potato starch extracted industrially. Gluten-free and thickening, but a refined carbohydrate stripped of the potato’s fibre and potassium.

descriptions.name: farine de riz
descriptions.description_en: Milled white rice, naturally gluten-free and easy to digest. With the bran and germ removed it behaves like a fast sugar in the body, so wholegrain rice flour is the better option.

descriptions.name: farine de soja degraissee
descriptions.description_en: Defatted soy flour is soy flour with most fat removed, often from genetically modified soy; it marks ultra-processed foods.

descriptions.name: farmed atlantic salmon
descriptions.description_en: Farmed Atlantic salmon is intensively farmed with industrial feed, antibiotics, synthetic colorants, and possible contaminants like PCBs and dioxins. Consumption should be occasional due to these potential contaminants and additives.

descriptions.name: fatty acids
descriptions.description_en: Refined fatty acids used as processing aids, glazing agents, or anti-caking agents. The E-number does not identify a single harmful fat. Health: Health impact depends more on the source and overall fat profile of the food than on this additive function.

descriptions.name: fecula modifiee
descriptions.description_en: A generic label covering any starch altered chemically or physically to thicken and stabilise industrial food, without saying which one. EFSA considers modified starches safe with no numerical ADI needed, but they are refined carbohydrates with no nutrients and one of the clearest markers of ultra-processing.

descriptions.name: fécule de maïs
descriptions.description_en: Cornstarch extracted industrially, often from GM corn outside the EU. A refined carbohydrate with a high glycemic index and no fibre, vitamins or minerals.

descriptions.name: fécule de pomme de terre
descriptions.description_en: Potato starch extracted industrially. Gluten-free and thickening, but a refined carbohydrate stripped of the potato’s fibre and potassium.

descriptions.name: fecule de pomme de terre modifiee
descriptions.description_en: Modified potato starch is an industrially acetylated starch with a high glycemic index; it can affect blood sugar control and metabolic health.

descriptions.name: fécule de tapioca
descriptions.description_en: Starch extracted from the cassava root. It is naturally gluten-free and useful as a thickener, but like every isolated starch it is a refined carbohydrate with a high glycemic response and none of the fibre or minerals of the root.

descriptions.name: fecule modifiee
descriptions.description_en: A generic label covering any starch altered chemically or physically to thicken and stabilise industrial food, without saying which one. EFSA considers modified starches safe with no numerical ADI needed, but they are refined carbohydrates with no nutrients and one of the clearest markers of ultra-processing.

descriptions.name: fecule modifiee de pomme de terre
descriptions.description_en: Modified potato starch is an industrially acetylated starch with a high glycemic index as an ultra-processed carbohydrate.

descriptions.name: feijoa
descriptions.description_en: Feijoa is a good source of vitamins and antioxidants that support immune function and digestive health.

descriptions.name: fermented chili paste
descriptions.description_en: A Korean fermented paste of chilli, glutinous rice and soybeans. The traditional version is a genuine ferment; most supermarket jars list glucose-fructose syrup among the main ingredients, which puts them closer to a sweet sauce than to a ferment. The ingredient list decides which one you have.

descriptions.name: ferments lactiques
descriptions.description_en: Lactic acid bacteria improve digestion and support a balanced gut microbiome.

descriptions.name: ferrocyanure de potassium
descriptions.description_en: An anti-caking agent (E536) added to salt to keep it free-flowing. Despite the name, the cyanide is locked in a stable complex and EFSA considers it safe at permitted levels.

descriptions.name: ferrocyanure de sodium
descriptions.description_en: An anti-caking agent (E535) added to table salt to keep it free-flowing. Despite the alarming name, the cyanide is locked in a stable complex and EFSA considers it safe at permitted levels.

descriptions.name: ferrous gluconate
descriptions.description_en: An iron salt used to darken olives and provide iron. It can significantly increase iron exposure in concentrated products. Health: Excess iron can cause nausea, constipation, abdominal pain, and oxidative injury. It is especially dangerous in large accidental doses to children.

descriptions.name: ferrous lactate
descriptions.description_en: An iron salt used mainly to stabilize the dark color of olives and other foods. Health: Too much iron may cause digestive symptoms and is unsuitable for people with iron-overload disorders.

descriptions.name: feta
descriptions.description_en: Protein and calcium in feta support muscle function and bone strength.

descriptions.name: feuille de curry
descriptions.description_en: Curry leaf promotes antioxidant activity and supports digestive health.

descriptions.name: feuille de kaffir
descriptions.description_en: Aromatic leaves and rhizomes used fresh in South-East Asian cooking - kaffir lime leaf, lemongrass, galangal, fresh turmeric, ginger root and curry leaf. They are whole plant parts, used in small amounts, and carry the essential oils and antioxidants of the fresh plant.

descriptions.name: feuilles de stevia
descriptions.description_en: Stevia leaves provide a natural, calorie-free sweetener that can help reduce sugar intake.

descriptions.name: fibre de racine de manioc
descriptions.description_en: Cassava root fiber feeds beneficial gut bacteria and supports digestive health.

descriptions.name: figue
descriptions.description_en: Dried figs provide fiber and minerals that support digestion and heart health.

descriptions.name: figues sechees
descriptions.description_en: Dried figs provide fiber and antioxidants that support digestive health and reduce inflammation.

descriptions.name: five spice
descriptions.description_en: Five spice benefits the body by providing natural antioxidants and essential nutrients from dried herbs and spices.

descriptions.name: fletan
descriptions.description_en: A large flatfish with firm white flesh and a good omega-3 content. Being a big predator it accumulates more methylmercury than small white fish, which puts it on the FDA and EPA Good Choices list: one serving a week rather than the two to three allowed for lean white fish. Sturgeon falls in the same group.

descriptions.name: foie
descriptions.description_en: Exceptionally rich in vitamin A, B12, iron and copper - one of the most nutrient-dense foods there is. Its preformed vitamin A is so concentrated that health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid liver and liver products entirely, and a single weekly portion is enough for everyone else.

descriptions.name: foie de volaille
descriptions.description_en: Exceptionally rich in vitamin A, B12, iron and copper - one of the most nutrient-dense foods there is. Its preformed vitamin A is so concentrated that health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid liver and liver products entirely, and a single weekly portion is enough for everyone else.

descriptions.name: food gelatine
descriptions.description_en: Gelatine (E441) is a protein-based gelling agent derived from animal collagen with minimal nutritional value.

descriptions.name: formaldehyde
descriptions.description_en: A preservative and disinfectant classified IARC Group 1 human carcinogen, causally linked to nasopharyngeal cancer and leukaemia. Banned as a direct food additive and prohibited in EU cosmetics.

descriptions.name: fourme d ambert
descriptions.description_en: Blue cheeses concentrate calcium, protein and B12, and their moulds give them their character. They are among the saltiest cheeses there are, and health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid blue-veined cheese unless it has been cooked until steaming hot.

descriptions.name: fragrance
descriptions.description_en: A single word hiding a mixture that can contain dozens of undisclosed compounds. EU law requires 26 known fragrance allergens to be named separately, which is why perfumed products are a leading cause of contact allergy.

descriptions.name: fraise
descriptions.description_en: High in vitamin C and antioxidants, berries help protect cells and support immune health.

descriptions.name: fresh turmeric
descriptions.description_en: Fresh turmeric supports the body's anti-inflammatory processes and promotes overall health.

descriptions.name: fromage
descriptions.description_en: Concentrated protein and calcium in cheese support muscle and bone strength when eaten in moderation.

descriptions.name: fromage allege
descriptions.description_en: Reduced-fat cheese. Lower in calories, but manufacturers often compensate with added salt, starch or stabilisers, and the texture depends on more processing than full-fat cheese.

descriptions.name: fromage fondu
descriptions.description_en: Processed cheese made by melting cheese scraps with emulsifying salts, usually phosphates. It is high in sodium and phosphate additives and bears little resemblance to traditionally made cheese.

descriptions.name: fructose
descriptions.description_en: Isolated fructose, very different from the fructose inside whole fruit, which comes with fibre and nutrients. It is metabolised by the liver and, in isolated form, promotes fat accumulation there.

descriptions.name: Fructose ajouté
descriptions.description_en: Fructose added in isolated form, without the fibre and nutrients of whole fruit. It is processed almost entirely by the liver, and regular intake is linked to fat accumulation there.

descriptions.name: fruit
descriptions.description_en: Whole fruits and vegetables provide fiber, vitamins, and antioxidants that promote overall health.

descriptions.name: fruit du moine
descriptions.description_en: A sweetener from the luo han guo fruit, with no calories and no effect on blood sugar. It has a long history of use in Asia and is widely permitted in North America. In the EU only an aqueous decoction of the fruit has been authorised, while purified mogroside V - the form used in most imported products - is still awaiting authorisation.

descriptions.name: Fruit du moine / Monk fruit
descriptions.description_en: Monk fruit extract offers a calorie-free sweetening option without affecting blood sugar.

descriptions.name: fruit du moine en poudre
descriptions.description_en: A sweetener from the luo han guo fruit, with no calories and no effect on blood sugar. It has a long history of use in Asia and is widely permitted in North America. In the EU only an aqueous decoction of the fruit has been authorised, while purified mogroside V - the form used in most imported products - is still awaiting authorisation.

descriptions.name: fumee naturelle
descriptions.description_en: Smoke flavouring produced by condensing wood smoke. It can carry polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, which is why EFSA has re-evaluated smoke flavourings and the EU has restricted several of them.

descriptions.name: galanga
descriptions.description_en: Galanga contains compounds that support digestion and reduce inflammation.

descriptions.name: galangal
descriptions.description_en: Galangal supports digestion and has anti-inflammatory properties.

descriptions.name: gallate d epigallocatechine
descriptions.description_en: The main catechin in green tea, a well-studied antioxidant. Drunk as an infusion it raises no concern. As a concentrated extract it is a different matter: EFSA found in 2018 that 800 mg of EGCG per day or more from supplements raises liver enzymes, and the EU now requires warning labelling on green tea extracts. Read it as a good sign in tea, a caution in a supplement.

descriptions.name: gallates
descriptions.description_en: Propyl, octyl and dodecyl gallate (E310–E312), synthetic antioxidants that stop fats going rancid. They are permitted at low levels but can trigger contact allergy and are restricted in foods for infants.

descriptions.name: gambas
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: gamma-tocopherol
descriptions.description_en: Vitamin E as gamma-tocopherol acts as an antioxidant protecting cells from damage.

descriptions.name: ganjang
descriptions.description_en: Traditionally brewed soy sauce is fermented for months and carries the depth that comes with it. Two things are worth checking on the label: it is extremely salty, so a few tablespoons cover a large share of the daily sodium limit; and cheaper versions are made by acid hydrolysis rather than brewing, a process that can generate 3-MCPD, which the EU caps by law.

descriptions.name: ganoderma
descriptions.description_en: Medicinal mushrooms sold as dried powder or concentrated extract. They supply beta-glucans and are well tolerated as a food. As a supplement, reishi has been associated with rare cases of liver injury - the NIH LiverTox database describes clinically apparent injury as extremely rare, and reported cases mostly involve the unextracted powdered form, alcohol use or existing liver disease. It can also interact with anticoagulants. Treat it as a supplement with its own precautions, not as an ordinary mushroom.

descriptions.name: garam masala
descriptions.description_en: Garam masala benefits the body by providing natural antioxidants and essential nutrients from dried herbs and spices.

descriptions.name: garlic
descriptions.description_en: Garlic contains allicin, which supports heart health and has antibacterial properties.

descriptions.name: gaz carbonique
descriptions.description_en: Carbon dioxide (E290) benefits the body by being inert and leaving no residues after use in food and drinks.

descriptions.name: gelatine
descriptions.description_en: Collagen extracted from animal skin and bone by acid or alkali treatment (E441). It is a safe, protein-based gelling agent, though of animal origin and low in nutritional value. Not suitable for vegetarians, or for halal and kosher diets unless certified.

descriptions.name: gelatine alimentaire
descriptions.description_en: Gelatine (E441) is a protein-based gelling agent derived from animal collagen with minimal nutritional value.

descriptions.name: gelée royale
descriptions.description_en: Bee products carrying enzymes, amino acids and antibacterial compounds. They are also documented allergens: royal jelly and propolis have caused severe allergic reactions including anaphylaxis, rare but well recorded, and are best avoided by people with asthma or a known allergy to bee products. Pollen can trigger reactions in people allergic to the source plants.

descriptions.name: germe de blé
descriptions.description_en: Wheat germ is the embryo of the wheat grain, rich in vitamin E, magnesium, zinc, and B vitamins.

descriptions.name: germes de soja
descriptions.description_en: Bamboo shoots are low in calories and a good source of fibre and potassium, but fresh shoots contain cyanogenic glycosides and must be boiled before eating - canned shoots are already processed and safe. Bean sprouts and lotus root, often sold alongside them, raise no such issue.

descriptions.name: ghee
descriptions.description_en: Ghee is a stable cooking fat that is lactose-free and provides energy from saturated fat.

descriptions.name: gingembre
descriptions.description_en: Anti-inflammatory gingerols in ginger help reduce nausea and support digestive health.

descriptions.name: ginger root
descriptions.description_en: Ginger root aids digestion and helps reduce nausea and inflammation.

descriptions.name: ginseng
descriptions.description_en: An Asian root traditionally used against fatigue, sold today mostly as a concentrated extract. It is not inert: it interacts with anticoagulants and diabetes medication, can disturb sleep at higher doses, and is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

descriptions.name: ginseng extract
descriptions.description_en: An Asian root traditionally used against fatigue, sold today mostly as a concentrated extract. It is not inert: it interacts with anticoagulants and diabetes medication, can disturb sleep at higher doses, and is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

descriptions.name: ginseng rouge
descriptions.description_en: An Asian root traditionally used against fatigue, sold today mostly as a concentrated extract. It is not inert: it interacts with anticoagulants and diabetes medication, can disturb sleep at higher doses, and is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

descriptions.name: gluconic acid
descriptions.description_en: An organic acid produced from glucose and used to regulate acidity or bind minerals. Health: It has low toxicity, although concentrated or high amounts may irritate the digestive system.

descriptions.name: glucono-delta-lactone
descriptions.description_en: A glucose-derived compound that slowly releases gluconic acid, helping set tofu, cure foods, and control acidity. Health: Large amounts may cause bloating, gas, or digestive discomfort.

descriptions.name: glucose
descriptions.description_en: Added glucose in isolated form, absorbed almost instantly. It raises blood sugar faster than table sugar and carries no nutritional value beyond calories.

descriptions.name: glucose fructose syrup
descriptions.description_en: Glucose fructose syrup is an industrial sweetener extracted from corn, often GMO. It is strongly linked to obesity, type 2 diabetes, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, and metabolic syndrome, so it should be avoided.

descriptions.name: glutamate monoammonique
descriptions.description_en: A glutamate flavour enhancer (E624) that intensifies umami in industrial seasonings. It performs the same role as MSG under a different name.

descriptions.name: glutamate monopotassique
descriptions.description_en: A flavour enhancer (E622) from the glutamate family, used like MSG to build savoury taste with less real ingredient. It is a reliable marker of ultra-processed food.

descriptions.name: glyceryl diacetate (diacetin)
descriptions.description_en: A manufactured glycerol ester used to carry flavors, retain moisture, and improve processing. Health: It is broken down into glycerol and acetic acid. Modern long-term data are less extensive than for some common additives, but no major risk is established at permitted use.

descriptions.name: glycine
descriptions.description_en: An amino acid (E640) used as a mild sweetener and flavour modifier. The body makes its own supply, and it is safe at the small amounts used in food.

descriptions.name: glyphosate
descriptions.description_en: The world's most used herbicide, found as a residue in cereals and legumes. IARC classified it Group 2A, probably carcinogenic to humans, in 2015, though EFSA reached a different conclusion.

descriptions.name: goat milk
descriptions.description_en: Smaller fat globules in goat, sheep and buffalo milk may make them easier to digest for some people. Nutritionally they are close to cow's milk, with slightly more medium-chain fats.

descriptions.name: gochujang
descriptions.description_en: A Korean fermented paste of chilli, glutinous rice and soybeans. The traditional version is a genuine ferment; most supermarket jars list glucose-fructose syrup among the main ingredients, which puts them closer to a sweet sauce than to a ferment. The ingredient list decides which one you have.

descriptions.name: gold
descriptions.description_en: Gold leaf (E175) used to decorate confectionery and drinks. EFSA re-evaluated it in 2016 and concluded that, given the very low solubility of elemental gold, systemic absorption and systemic effects are not expected. It passes through the body unchanged and adds nothing nutritionally - purely decorative.

descriptions.name: golden raisin
descriptions.description_en: Golden raisins deliver antioxidants and natural sugars that benefit energy and wellness.

descriptions.name: golden raisins
descriptions.description_en: Golden raisins provide antioxidants and essential nutrients that support overall health and energy.

descriptions.name: gombo
descriptions.description_en: Okra provides soluble fibre that helps regulate blood sugar and cholesterol, with very few calories. Its mucilage is what thickens stews and gumbo.

descriptions.name: gomme adragante
descriptions.description_en: A plant gum (E413) from the astragalus shrub, used as a thickener and stabiliser. It behaves as soluble fibre and is well tolerated, though it can cause bloating in quantity.

descriptions.name: gomme arabique
descriptions.description_en: Acacia gum acts as a prebiotic fiber that nourishes beneficial gut bacteria.

descriptions.name: gomme cassia
descriptions.description_en: A thickener (E427) from cassia tree seeds, authorised in the EU with strict purity limits because the raw seed contains natural anthraquinones. Purified food grade is considered safe.

descriptions.name: gomme guar
descriptions.description_en: Guar gum is an industrial gelling agent that may cause bloating and digestive discomfort.

descriptions.name: gomme konjac
descriptions.description_en: Konjac gum is a thickener with a risk of intestinal blockage.

descriptions.name: gomme xanthane
descriptions.description_en: Xanthan gum is a thickening agent that may disrupt digestion in sensitive people.

descriptions.name: gorgonzola
descriptions.description_en: Blue cheeses concentrate calcium, protein and B12, and their moulds give them their character. They are among the saltiest cheeses there are, and health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid blue-veined cheese unless it has been cooked until steaming hot.

descriptions.name: gouda
descriptions.description_en: Gouda cheese delivers protein and calcium, essential for bone strength and muscle repair.

descriptions.name: goudron de houille
descriptions.description_en: Coal tar is a coal derivative used in some shampoos and dyes. It is a confirmed human carcinogen (IARC Group 1).

descriptions.name: Goudron de houille (coal tar)
descriptions.description_en: A thick residue from coal distillation used in some medicated shampoos and dyes. Coal tars are IARC Group 1 human carcinogens; untreated forms are restricted in EU cosmetic products.

descriptions.name: graines
descriptions.description_en: Mixed seeds provide plant protein, fiber, minerals, and healthy fats for nutrition.

descriptions.name: graines de chia
descriptions.description_en: Chia seeds offer soluble fiber and omega-3 ALA to aid digestion and fullness.

descriptions.name: graines de courge
descriptions.description_en: Pumpkin and other seeds supply minerals, protein, and healthy fats for body functions.

descriptions.name: graines de lin
descriptions.description_en: Flax seeds are rich in omega-3 ALA and lignans that support heart and hormonal health.

descriptions.name: graines de sesame
descriptions.description_en: Sesame seeds provide calcium, magnesium, and lignans that promote bone and heart health.

descriptions.name: graines de tournesol
descriptions.description_en: Sunflower seeds deliver vitamin E, magnesium, and selenium to support antioxidant defenses.

descriptions.name: graisse de coco
descriptions.description_en: Coconut fat is a basic culinary fat rich in medium-chain saturated fats that performs well in cooking and baking.

descriptions.name: graisse hydrogenee
descriptions.description_en: Hydrogenated fats are processed fats containing trans fats. Trans fats can negatively affect heart health.

descriptions.name: graisse interesterifiee
descriptions.description_en: Fat rearranged chemically or enzymatically to replace trans fats and mimic their texture. It avoids trans fats but remains a laboratory-restructured fat, and its long-term metabolic effects are still debated.

descriptions.name: grana padano
descriptions.description_en: Grana Padano cheese supplies valuable nutrients like calcium and protein for maintaining strong bones and muscles.

descriptions.name: grapefruit
descriptions.description_en: Grapefruit provides vitamin C and antioxidants that support immune function and skin health.

descriptions.name: gras trans
descriptions.description_en: Trans fatty acids raise bad cholesterol while lowering the good kind, directly increasing cardiovascular risk. The WHO has called for their global elimination and there is no safe level of intake.

descriptions.name: greek yogurt
descriptions.description_en: Greek yogurt provides protein and probiotics that support muscle maintenance and digestion.

descriptions.name: green s
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic green food dye used to create or intensify color. It has an acceptable daily intake, and high consumption of several colored products can increase total exposure. Health: The concern is unnecessary cumulative exposure and possible intolerance in sensitive individuals, not proven carcinogenicity.

descriptions.name: green tea extract
descriptions.description_en: The main catechin in green tea, a well-studied antioxidant. Drunk as an infusion it raises no concern. As a concentrated extract it is a different matter: EFSA found in 2018 that 800 mg of EGCG per day or more from supplements raises liver enzymes, and the EU now requires warning labelling on green tea extracts. Read it as a good sign in tea, a caution in a supplement.

descriptions.name: grenade
descriptions.description_en: Pomegranate seeds are dense in punicalagins and anthocyanins, among the most concentrated antioxidants in any fruit, along with fibre and vitamin K.

descriptions.name: griotte
descriptions.description_en: Griotte cherries contain antioxidants and vitamins that help reduce inflammation and support heart health.

descriptions.name: guacamole
descriptions.description_en: Guacamole benefits the body by providing healthy fats and vitamins from avocados.

descriptions.name: guanylate
descriptions.description_en: Guanylate, disodium ribonucleotides (E635), is a ribonucleotide flavor enhancer combining E627 and E631, often used with MSG.

descriptions.name: guanylate de calcium
descriptions.description_en: Calcium guanylate (E629) is a ribonucleotide flavor enhancer that boosts savory taste; not advised for people with gout due to purines.

descriptions.name: guanylate dipotassique
descriptions.description_en: Dipotassium guanylate (E628) is a potassium variant umami enhancer not advised for people with gout.

descriptions.name: guanylate disodique
descriptions.description_en: Disodium guanylate is an umami enhancer in instant soups and snacks, not advised for people with gout due to purines.

descriptions.name: guarana
descriptions.description_en: Natural caffeine in guarana provides sustained energy without rapid spikes.

descriptions.name: halloumi
descriptions.description_en: Halloumi supplies important proteins and minerals that aid in maintaining healthy bones.

descriptions.name: haricots
descriptions.description_en: Rich in plant protein and fiber, haricots support stable blood sugar levels.

descriptions.name: heart
descriptions.description_en: Exceptionally rich in vitamin A, B12, iron and copper - one of the most nutrient-dense foods there is. Its preformed vitamin A is so concentrated that health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid liver and liver products entirely, and a single weekly portion is enough for everyone else.

descriptions.name: helium
