descriptions.description_en: An inert gas used in specialized packaging or processing. It leaves no meaningful chemical residue in food. Health: Food use is not considered a safety concern. Inhalation of pressurized helium is a separate non-food hazard.

descriptions.name: hemicellulose de soja
descriptions.description_en: Hemicellulose de soja is a processed fiber fraction from soybeans used to thicken and stabilize food products. Residual soy proteins may affect people with severe soy allergies despite low toxicity of the additive.

descriptions.name: hericium
descriptions.description_en: Medicinal mushrooms sold as dried powder or concentrated extract. They supply beta-glucans and are well tolerated as a food. As a supplement, reishi has been associated with rare cases of liver injury - the NIH LiverTox database describes clinically apparent injury as extremely rare, and reported cases mostly involve the unextracted powdered form, alcohol use or existing liver disease. It can also interact with anticoagulants. Treat it as a supplement with its own precautions, not as an ordinary mushroom.

descriptions.name: hfcs
descriptions.description_en: HFCS is an industrial sweetener extracted from corn, often GMO. It is strongly linked to obesity, type 2 diabetes, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, and metabolic syndrome, so it should be avoided.

descriptions.name: hijiki
descriptions.description_en: A brown seaweed that accumulates inorganic arsenic, an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen, at levels far above any other edible seaweed. The food agencies of the UK, Canada and Ireland do not merely advise moderation: they advise not eating it at all, and choosing another seaweed instead.

descriptions.name: homard
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: honey
descriptions.description_en: Raw honey brings antioxidants, enzymes and antibacterial compounds that refined sugar does not have. It is still around 80% sugar, and the WHO counts it as a free sugar exactly like table sugar - a better sweetener, not a free one. Never give honey to a baby under one year old, because of the risk of infant botulism.

descriptions.name: hoplostete orange
descriptions.description_en: Long-lived top predators that concentrate the most methylmercury of any commercial fish. The FDA and EPA place swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel, bigeye tuna, orange roughy and Gulf tilefish on the Choices to Avoid list: pregnant women, breastfeeding women and children should not eat them at all, and other adults only rarely.

descriptions.name: horseradish
descriptions.description_en: Horseradish root supports respiratory health and aids digestion.

descriptions.name: huile d'avocat
descriptions.description_en: Avocado oil is a simple culinary fat rich in monounsaturated fatty acids and vitamin E, stable for cooking due to its high smoke point.

descriptions.name: huile d'olive
descriptions.description_en: Olive oil is a basic culinary fat rich in monounsaturated fatty acids and antioxidant polyphenols, benefiting cardiovascular health.

descriptions.name: Huile de canola / colza raffinée
descriptions.description_en: Refined rapeseed oil with a favourable fatty acid profile on paper. High-heat refining degrades its omega-3 content and generates process contaminants; cold-pressed versions are better.

descriptions.name: huile de coco
descriptions.description_en: Medium-chain fats in coconut oil provide a stable cooking fat source when used moderately.

descriptions.name: huile de coco fractionnee
descriptions.description_en: Fractionated coconut oil is an ultra-processed fat made by industrial processes like hydrogenation and fractionation; it indicates ultra-processed food and should be consumed cautiously.

descriptions.name: huile de coco hydrogenee
descriptions.description_en: Hydrogenated coconut oil is an ultra-processed fat produced by industrial hydrogenation and fractionation; it signals ultra-processed food and requires cautious consumption.

descriptions.name: huile de coco interesterifiee
descriptions.description_en: Interesterified coconut oil is an ultra-processed fat created by industrial hydrogenation and fractionation; it marks ultra-processed food and should be consumed with caution.

descriptions.name: huile de coco modifiee
descriptions.description_en: Coconut oil that has been hydrogenated, fractionated or interesterified to change its melting point. These industrial treatments alter the fat structure and mark a heavily engineered product.

descriptions.name: huile de colza
descriptions.description_en: Rapeseed (canola) oil, favourable in fatty acid profile but industrially refined at high heat, which degrades its omega-3 content and forms process contaminants. Cold-pressed versions are a better choice.

descriptions.name: huile de coton
descriptions.description_en: Cottonseed oil, extracted from a non-food crop that is heavily treated with pesticides. It is very high in omega-6 fats and requires intensive refining to remove natural toxins such as gossypol.

descriptions.name: huile de lin
descriptions.description_en: Flaxseed oil offers omega-3 ALA that supports heart and brain health when used raw.

descriptions.name: huile de mais
descriptions.description_en: Corn oil, an industrially refined oil very high in omega-6 fatty acids. An unbalanced omega-6 to omega-3 ratio is associated with chronic inflammation when consumed regularly.

descriptions.name: huile de noix
descriptions.description_en: Walnut oil supplies omega-3 ALA and polyphenols that support cardiovascular health.

descriptions.name: huile de palme
descriptions.description_en: A cheap refined fat used across industrial food. High-temperature refining forms 3-MCPD and glycidyl esters — glycidol is rated IARC Group 2A, probably carcinogenic — and EFSA set very low tolerable intakes. Also a major driver of deforestation.

descriptions.name: huile de pepin de raisin
descriptions.description_en: Grapeseed oil, extracted from winemaking residue and usually solvent-refined. It is very high in omega-6 fats, which tilts the diet away from omega-3 balance when used regularly.

descriptions.name: huile de sesame
descriptions.description_en: Sesame oil contains antioxidants that protect cells and remain stable during cooking.

descriptions.name: huile de soja
descriptions.description_en: The most widely used oil in industrial food, refined at high heat and dominated by omega-6 fats. It is often derived from GM crops outside the EU and contributes to an inflammatory fatty acid balance.

descriptions.name: huile de tournesol
descriptions.description_en: Sunflower oil, usually refined and very high in omega-6 fats. It oxidises readily when heated, generating harmful compounds, and its regular use tilts the diet away from omega-3 balance.

descriptions.name: huile hydrogenee
descriptions.description_en: Hydrogenated oils are processed fats containing trans fats. Trans fats can negatively affect heart health.

descriptions.name: Huile hydrogénée / Gras trans
descriptions.description_en: Partially hydrogenated oil, the main industrial source of trans fats. Trans fats raise LDL cholesterol and lower HDL; the WHO calls for their elimination and the EU caps them at 2% of total fat.

descriptions.name: huile minerale
descriptions.description_en: Mineral oil is petroleum-derived; untreated or mildly treated forms are confirmed human carcinogens due to MOAH and should be avoided.

descriptions.name: Huile minérale (paraffinum, petrolatum)
descriptions.description_en: Petroleum-derived oils used in creams, balms and lubricants. Untreated and mildly treated mineral oils are IARC Group 1 human carcinogens; refined cosmetic grades are safer but can still carry aromatic hydrocarbon (MOAH) residues.

descriptions.name: huile vegetale
descriptions.description_en: An unspecified blend, most often refined palm or rapeseed. The label hides which fat is actually used, and heavy industrial refining is typical of ultra-processed food that whole ingredients never require.

descriptions.name: Huile végétale (non spécifiée)
descriptions.description_en: An undisclosed blend of refined oils, most often palm or rapeseed. The label hides which fat is actually used, which alone makes it worth limiting.

descriptions.name: huile vegetale bromee
descriptions.description_en: Brominated vegetable oil, used to keep citrus flavours suspended in soft drinks. The FDA revoked its authorisation in 2024 after evidence of thyroid harm and bromine build-up in body fat. Long banned in the EU, UK and Japan.

descriptions.name: huiles minerales
descriptions.description_en: Huiles minerales are petroleum-derived mineral oils; untreated or mildly treated forms are confirmed human carcinogens (IARC Group 1) due to MOAH and should be avoided.

descriptions.name: huitre
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: hummus
descriptions.description_en: Hummus benefits the body by supplying plant-based protein and fiber for digestive and muscle health.

descriptions.name: humus maison
descriptions.description_en: Cooked chickpeas blended with tahini, olive oil, lemon and garlic - plant protein, fibre, unsaturated fat and calcium in one spread. Homemade versions contain nothing else; industrial tubs often add preservatives and cheaper oils.

descriptions.name: hydrochloric acid
descriptions.description_en: A strong processing acid used in controlled amounts to adjust pH or manufacture ingredients. It is neutralized or highly diluted in the finished food. Health: The concentrated industrial chemical is corrosive, but that hazard should not be confused with properly controlled residues in food.

descriptions.name: hydrogen
descriptions.description_en: A gas used in limited food-processing applications. It is highly flammable during industrial handling but does not remain as a toxic food residue. Health: The main hazard is fire or explosion during manufacturing, not consumption of properly processed food.

descriptions.name: hydrogenated
descriptions.description_en: Oil hardened by adding hydrogen to extend shelf life. Partial hydrogenation creates trans fats, which are strongly linked to heart disease and are now restricted in the EU and banned in the US.

descriptions.name: hydroquinone
descriptions.description_en: A powerful skin-lightening agent. Banned in EU cosmetics except for limited professional nail products, because it causes irreversible skin discolouration (ochronosis) and carries genotoxicity concerns.

descriptions.name: hydroxyde de calcium
descriptions.description_en: Calcium hydroxide (E526), or slaked lime, used to treat corn (nixtamalisation) and adjust acidity. Harmless in the finished food, but corrosive in raw form and a sign of industrial processing.

descriptions.name: hydroxyde de magnesium
descriptions.description_en: Hydroxyde de magnesium is a refined magnesium compound used to regulate acidity and acts as a laxative at medicinal doses. Too much can cause diarrhea, cramping, and magnesium accumulation in people with kidney impairment.

descriptions.name: hydroxyde de potassium
descriptions.description_en: Potassium hydroxide (E525), a strongly alkaline processing aid used to adjust acidity and treat cocoa. It is neutralised in the final product but marks a chemically processed recipe.

descriptions.name: hydroxyde de sodium
descriptions.description_en: Sodium hydroxide (E524), caustic soda, used to adjust pH and to peel or treat foods such as pretzels and olives. Corrosive in concentrated form; its presence indicates industrial processing.

descriptions.name: hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate
descriptions.description_en: One of the most common modified starches (E1442), used in sauces, desserts and ready meals to hold texture through heating and freezing. EFSA's 2017 re-evaluation found no safety concern and set no numerical ADI, but it is a purely technical refined carbohydrate and a clear marker of ultra-processed food.

descriptions.name: igname
descriptions.description_en: Starchy tropical roots that must always be cooked. Raw taro and raw yam contain calcium oxalate crystals and other compounds that irritate the mouth and digestive tract; cooking destroys them. Once cooked they are a good source of complex carbohydrate, potassium and fibre.

descriptions.name: imidazolidinyl urea
descriptions.description_en: A widely used cosmetic preservative that releases formaldehyde, an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen. It is a recognised contact allergen and is restricted under EU cosmetics regulation.

descriptions.name: imitation mozzarella
descriptions.description_en: A cheese substitute built from vegetable oil, starch and milk proteins rather than curdled milk. It is engineered for melt and cost, and delivers none of the qualities of real cheese.

descriptions.name: inosinate
descriptions.description_en: Inosinate (E635) is a flavor enhancer combining E627 and E631, often used with MSG. It should be consumed occasionally due to its additive nature.

descriptions.name: inosinate de calcium
descriptions.description_en: Calcium inosinate is a rare ribonucleotide umami enhancer; like others, it is not advised for people with gout due to purines.

descriptions.name: inosinate dipotassique
descriptions.description_en: Dipotassium inosinate (E632) is a potassium-based ribonucleotide flavor enhancer used in reduced-sodium recipes; not advised for people with gout.

descriptions.name: inositol
descriptions.description_en: A sugar-like compound found naturally in fruits, beans and grains, and also produced by the body. Added to energy drinks and supplements, it is well tolerated, but the added form is more marketing than nutritional need.

descriptions.name: inuline
descriptions.description_en: A prebiotic fibre from chicory root or agave that feeds beneficial gut bacteria. It is genuinely useful, but it is also one of the most fermentable fibres there is: added to industrial products to boost the fibre figure on the label, it commonly causes bloating and gas, and it is poorly tolerated in irritable bowel syndrome.

descriptions.name: irradiation
descriptions.description_en: Treatment with ionising radiation to kill microbes and extend shelf life. It leaves no radioactivity and is authorised in the EU for a narrow list of foods, which must carry an "irradiated" label; it does degrade some vitamins.

descriptions.name: isobutylparaben
descriptions.description_en: A family of preservatives with weak hormone-like activity in laboratory tests. The EU banned five of them from cosmetics in 2014 for lack of safety data (isopropyl-, isobutyl-, phenyl-, benzyl- and pentylparaben) and capped propyl- and butylparaben at 0.14%, with an additional ban on the nappy area of children under three. The 2004 study that detected parabens in breast tissue established no causal link; the real issue is cumulative exposure across food, cosmetics and medicines.

descriptions.name: isolat de proteines
descriptions.description_en: Protein stripped from its original food by industrial extraction, leaving no fibre, fat or micronutrients. Useful for boosting protein figures on a label, but a marker of a reconstructed product.

descriptions.name: Isolat de protéines (whey, soja, lait)
descriptions.description_en: Protein separated from its original food by industrial processing, leaving no fibre, fat or micronutrients. Effective for raising protein figures, but a marker of a reconstructed product.

descriptions.name: isomalt
descriptions.description_en: A polyol (E953) made from sucrose, common in sugar-free sweets. It does not feed tooth decay and has a low glycemic impact, but it causes digestive upset in larger amounts.

descriptions.name: isopropyl myristate
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic emollient that gives creams a light, fast-absorbing feel. It is not toxic, but it is highly comedogenic and a common trigger of clogged pores in acne-prone skin.

descriptions.name: isopropylparaben
descriptions.description_en: A family of preservatives with weak hormone-like activity in laboratory tests. The EU banned five of them from cosmetics in 2014 for lack of safety data (isopropyl-, isobutyl-, phenyl-, benzyl- and pentylparaben) and capped propyl- and butylparaben at 0.14%, with an additional ban on the nappy area of children under three. The 2004 study that detected parabens in breast tissue established no causal link; the real issue is cumulative exposure across food, cosmetics and medicines.

descriptions.name: Isothiazolinones (MIT, CMIT)
descriptions.description_en: Preservatives in cosmetics, paints and household products, and among the strongest contact allergens known. Methylisothiazolinone has been banned from leave-on cosmetics in the EU since 2017 after a wave of skin reactions.

descriptions.name: jambon
descriptions.description_en: Cured or cooked pork leg. As a processed meat it falls under the IARC Group 1 classification (2015): salting and nitrite curing generate compounds that raise colorectal cancer risk with regular intake.

descriptions.name: jasmine rice
descriptions.description_en: Jasmine rice is a fragrant long-grain rice that supplies energy through carbohydrates.

descriptions.name: jaune 6
descriptions.description_en: Sunset Yellow (E110), a synthetic azo dye. EU law requires a warning that it may affect children's activity and attention, and the FDA is phasing it out of US foods.

descriptions.name: jaune de quinoléine
descriptions.description_en: Quinoline Yellow (E104), a synthetic dye carrying the mandatory EU warning about effects on children's activity and attention. It is not authorised as a food colour in the United States.

descriptions.name: jeotgal
descriptions.description_en: Seafood salted and fermented for months, used as a seasoning and as a base for kimchi. It is a genuine traditional ferment, and it is also preserved in enough salt to make it one of the highest-sodium foods in any cuisine - a condiment by the spoonful, never a portion.

descriptions.name: jerky
descriptions.description_en: Salted and dried strips of beef. It counts as processed meat, an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen, and is also very high in sodium. Best kept as an occasional snack.

descriptions.name: jerusalem artichoke
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: jus concentre
descriptions.description_en: Juice boiled down to concentrate its sugars, then used to sweeten products while keeping a natural-sounding label. The fibre is gone and the sugar behaves like added sugar.

descriptions.name: jus de celeri
descriptions.description_en: Celery stalk or celeriac, simply dried and ground - harmless as a seasoning. Worth knowing, though, that the meat industry uses celery powder and celery juice as a natural nitrate source to cure meat labelled "no nitrites added": the body converts that nitrate to nitrite and the same nitroso-compounds form. On a charcuterie label it is a curing agent, not a vegetable.

descriptions.name: jus de fruits frais
descriptions.description_en: Freshly pressed juice keeps the vitamins and polyphenols of the fruit, but pressing removes the fibre that slows sugar absorption. The WHO counts fruit juice as a free sugar for that reason, and a glass concentrates the sugar of several pieces of fruit. Whole fruit is always the better version; vegetable-based juices avoid most of the issue.

descriptions.name: jus de pommes concentre
descriptions.description_en: Concentrated apple juice, one of the most common "natural" sweeteners in industrial food. Nutritionally it is close to added sugar, with the fibre and most vitamins removed.

descriptions.name: jus de raisin concentre
descriptions.description_en: Concentrated grape juice used to sweeten products without declaring added sugar. It is rich in fructose and behaves metabolically much like a syrup.

descriptions.name: kaffir lime leaf
descriptions.description_en: Kaffir lime leaf provides antioxidants and supports digestion.

descriptions.name: kamut
descriptions.description_en: Kamut is an ancient durum wheat variety richer in protein and selenium than modern wheat, but contains gluten.

descriptions.name: kashkaval
descriptions.description_en: Kashkaval supplies proteins and calcium important for maintaining healthy bones and muscles.

descriptions.name: kefalotyri
descriptions.description_en: Kefalotyri provides essential nutrients that support overall body health and muscle function.

descriptions.name: kefir
descriptions.description_en: Fermented dairy like kefir delivers live cultures and protein for gut and muscle health.

descriptions.name: keratine
descriptions.description_en: The structural protein of hair, added to products to smooth and coat the strand. The protein itself is harmless, but some professional keratin straightening treatments release formaldehyde when heated.

descriptions.name: keta
descriptions.description_en: Keta is a wild fish rich in omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: khorasan
descriptions.description_en: Khorasan wheat provides more protein and selenium than modern wheat, supporting muscle and antioxidant functions.

descriptions.name: kidney
descriptions.description_en: Exceptionally rich in vitamin A, B12, iron and copper - one of the most nutrient-dense foods there is. Its preformed vitamin A is so concentrated that health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid liver and liver products entirely, and a single weekly portion is enough for everyone else.

descriptions.name: kimchi
descriptions.description_en: Lacto-fermented vegetables rich in live lactic bacteria, fibre, vitamin C and beta-carotene - one of the best-studied traditional ferments there is. Its one drawback is salt: kimchi is brined, and diets very high in salted foods are an established risk factor for stomach cancer, so it works best as a side dish rather than a main portion.

descriptions.name: king mackerel
descriptions.description_en: Long-lived top predators that concentrate the most methylmercury of any commercial fish. The FDA and EPA place swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel, bigeye tuna, orange roughy and Gulf tilefish on the Choices to Avoid list: pregnant women, breastfeeding women and children should not eat them at all, and other adults only rarely.

descriptions.name: king salmon
descriptions.description_en: King salmon provides omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: kiwi
descriptions.description_en: One of the richest fruits in vitamin C, alongside fibre, potassium and actinidin, an enzyme that helps break down protein and eases digestion.

descriptions.name: klamath
descriptions.description_en: A wild-harvested cyanobacterium (Aphanizomenon flos-aquae) sold as a supplement. Because it is gathered from an open lake rather than cultivated, batches can be contaminated with microcystins, liver toxins produced by other cyanobacteria growing alongside it. Health agencies have repeatedly flagged this, and it is not recommended for children or during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: kombu
descriptions.description_en: Seaweed provides iodine, iron, magnesium and soluble fibre, supporting thyroid function and overall nutrition. Nori and wakame are moderate, but kombu is by far the most iodine-dense food known and can disturb thyroid function if eaten regularly - health agencies advise limiting it, and using it for stock rather than eating it.

descriptions.name: kombucha
descriptions.description_en: Sweetened tea fermented by a culture of bacteria and yeast. The fermentation consumes part of the sugar and produces organic acids and live cultures, but commercial bottles are usually sweetened again afterwards and can carry as much sugar as a soft drink. The nutrition label settles it, not the health framing.

descriptions.name: koumis
descriptions.description_en: Koumis contains probiotics that enhance digestion and strengthen the immune system.

descriptions.name: kumis
descriptions.description_en: Kumis offers probiotics that aid digestion and support immune function.

descriptions.name: kumquat
descriptions.description_en: Kumquat contains vitamin C and fiber, supporting immune health and digestive function.

descriptions.name: l-cysteine
descriptions.description_en: An amino acid (E920) used as a dough conditioner to speed up industrial bread making. Modern production is by bacterial fermentation, though it was historically extracted from feathers and hair.

descriptions.name: l-theanine
descriptions.description_en: L-theanine promotes calm alertness and reduces caffeine-induced jitteriness.

descriptions.name: labneh
descriptions.description_en: Labneh offers proteins and probiotics that support digestive health and bone strength.

descriptions.name: lactate de calcium
descriptions.description_en: A firming agent and acidity regulator (E327) that also supplies calcium. It is well tolerated and one of the more benign mineral salts used in food.

descriptions.name: lactate de potassium
descriptions.description_en: A preservative and acidity regulator (E326) often used to reduce sodium in processed meat. It is considered safe, though people with kidney disease should limit added potassium salts.

descriptions.name: lactate de sodium
descriptions.description_en: The sodium salt of lactic acid (E325), used to preserve and retain moisture in meat and baked goods. It is well tolerated but adds sodium to an already salty product category.

descriptions.name: lactic acid
descriptions.description_en: Lactic acid is a compound often produced by industrial fermentation or chemical synthesis, not naturally derived from milk. It should be consumed occasionally due to its industrial origin and processing.

descriptions.name: lactitol
descriptions.description_en: A polyol (E966) derived from lactose, poorly absorbed and used in sugar-free products. It reaches the colon largely intact, which is why it carries a laxative warning above 10%.

descriptions.name: lacto fermented vegetables
descriptions.description_en: Lacto fermented vegetables are traditional probiotic fermented foods that enhance digestive function.

descriptions.name: lactoserum
descriptions.description_en: Whey is a natural cheese byproduct rich in protein that supports muscle repair and growth.

descriptions.name: lactoserum modifie
descriptions.description_en: Lactoserum modifie is whey protein industrially modified by chemical or enzymatic processes. It is a marker of ultra-processing and is denatured compared to natural whey.

descriptions.name: lait
descriptions.description_en: Complete protein, calcium, iodine, and B12 in milk support bone health and energy metabolism.

descriptions.name: lait cru
descriptions.description_en: Milk that has not been pasteurised. It keeps enzymes and flavour that heat destroys, but it can carry listeria, salmonella and E. coli, which is why health agencies advise against it for pregnant women, young children, older adults and anyone immunocompromised. Its sale for direct consumption is prohibited in Canada.

descriptions.name: lait d amande
descriptions.description_en: Plant drinks are a good dairy alternative when the ingredient list is short: water, the nut or grain, and nothing else. Most supermarket versions add sugar, oils, gums and emulsifiers, and many contain only 2 to 3% almond, which leaves a drink with almost no protein. Choose unsweetened and fortified with calcium.

descriptions.name: lait de brebis
descriptions.description_en: Smaller fat globules in goat, sheep and buffalo milk may make them easier to digest for some people. Nutritionally they are close to cow's milk, with slightly more medium-chain fats.

descriptions.name: lait de bufflonne
descriptions.description_en: Smaller fat globules in goat, sheep and buffalo milk may make them easier to digest for some people. Nutritionally they are close to cow's milk, with slightly more medium-chain fats.

descriptions.name: lait de chevre
descriptions.description_en: Smaller fat globules in goat, sheep and buffalo milk may make them easier to digest for some people. Nutritionally they are close to cow's milk, with slightly more medium-chain fats.

descriptions.name: lait ecreme
descriptions.description_en: Skimmed milk provides protein, calcium, and B vitamins while reducing fat intake.

descriptions.name: lait en poudre
descriptions.description_en: Milk dried at high temperature for shelf life. It keeps most nutrients, though heat processing can oxidise some cholesterol and degrade certain vitamins compared with fresh milk.

descriptions.name: lait non pasteurise
descriptions.description_en: Milk that has not been pasteurised. It keeps enzymes and flavour that heat destroys, but it can carry listeria, salmonella and E. coli, which is why health agencies advise against it for pregnant women, young children, older adults and anyone immunocompromised. Its sale for direct consumption is prohibited in Canada.

descriptions.name: langouste
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: langoustine
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: langue
descriptions.description_en: Exceptionally rich in vitamin A, B12, iron and copper - one of the most nutrient-dense foods there is. Its preformed vitamin A is so concentrated that health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid liver and liver products entirely, and a single weekly portion is enough for everyone else.

descriptions.name: lanoline
descriptions.description_en: A wax from sheep's wool that is highly effective at sealing moisture into dry skin and lips. Purified grades are safe, but it is a known contact allergen and lower grades can carry pesticide residues.

descriptions.name: lassi
descriptions.description_en: Lassi is a yogurt-based drink that aids hydration and digestion.

descriptions.name: leben
descriptions.description_en: Leben supplies essential nutrients and promotes a healthy gut flora.

descriptions.name: lecithine de soja
descriptions.description_en: A natural emulsifier extracted from soybeans or sunflower seeds, used to blend fat and water. It is well tolerated and one of the most benign emulsifiers, though soy versions are often solvent-extracted and may be GM.

descriptions.name: lecithine de tournesol
descriptions.description_en: A natural emulsifier pressed from sunflower seeds, used to blend fat and water. Unlike soy lecithin it is obtained mechanically rather than with solvents, involves no GM crop and carries no soy allergen - which makes it the cleanest emulsifier commonly found on a label.

descriptions.name: legumes lacto fermentes
descriptions.description_en: Lacto-fermented vegetables are traditional probiotic fermented foods that support a balanced gut flora.

descriptions.name: lemongrass
descriptions.description_en: Lemongrass helps reduce inflammation and supports digestion.

descriptions.name: lentilles
descriptions.description_en: Lentils provide plant protein, iron, folate, and fiber, supporting blood and digestive health.

descriptions.name: levain
descriptions.description_en: A natural starter of wild yeasts and lactic bacteria. Long sourdough fermentation breaks down part of the gluten and the phytates that block mineral absorption, which makes sourdough bread more digestible and its magnesium, zinc and iron more available than in yeasted bread.

descriptions.name: levure
descriptions.description_en: Baker's yeast adds B vitamins and protein while naturally raising dough without chemicals.

descriptions.name: lilial
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic floral fragrance (butylphenyl methylpropional) banned in EU cosmetics since March 2022. It was classified toxic to reproduction (CMR 1B) after animal studies showed effects on fertility and foetal development, and it is also a contact allergen.

descriptions.name: lime
descriptions.description_en: Lime offers vitamin C and antioxidants that help protect cells and improve skin health.

descriptions.name: lion s mane
descriptions.description_en: Medicinal mushrooms sold as dried powder or concentrated extract. They supply beta-glucans and are well tolerated as a food. As a supplement, reishi has been associated with rare cases of liver injury - the NIH LiverTox database describes clinically apparent injury as extremely rare, and reported cases mostly involve the unextracted powdered form, alcohol use or existing liver disease. It can also interact with anticoagulants. Treat it as a supplement with its own precautions, not as an ordinary mushroom.

descriptions.name: liver
descriptions.description_en: Exceptionally rich in vitamin A, B12, iron and copper - one of the most nutrient-dense foods there is. Its preformed vitamin A is so concentrated that health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid liver and liver products entirely, and a single weekly portion is enough for everyone else.

descriptions.name: lobster
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: lotus root
descriptions.description_en: Bamboo shoots are low in calories and a good source of fibre and potassium, but fresh shoots contain cyanogenic glycosides and must be boiled before eating - canned shoots are already processed and safe. Bean sprouts and lotus root, often sold alongside them, raise no such issue.

descriptions.name: luo han guo
descriptions.description_en: A sweetener from the luo han guo fruit, with no calories and no effect on blood sugar. It has a long history of use in Asia and is widely permitted in North America. In the EU only an aqueous decoction of the fruit has been authorised, while purified mogroside V - the form used in most imported products - is still awaiting authorisation.

descriptions.name: luteine
descriptions.description_en: Lutein accumulates in the retina and supports eye health as a natural carotenoid.

descriptions.name: lycopene
descriptions.description_en: Lycopene is a dietary antioxidant from tomatoes that supports cellular health.

descriptions.name: maasdam
descriptions.description_en: Maasdam cheese provides essential nutrients from milk with no additives in traditional recipes.

descriptions.name: mackerel
descriptions.description_en: Mackerel provides essential omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: magnesium carbonates
descriptions.description_en: Refined magnesium salts used to prevent clumping, regulate acidity, or improve powder flow. Health: Large magnesium doses can cause diarrhea and abdominal cramping; food-additive quantities are usually much lower.

descriptions.name: magnesium chloride
descriptions.description_en: A refined magnesium salt used in tofu, mineral fortification, and texture control. Health: Large amounts may cause diarrhea, nausea, or abdominal cramping, especially in people with reduced kidney function.

descriptions.name: magnesium hydroxide
descriptions.description_en: A refined magnesium compound used to regulate acidity. At larger medicinal doses it also acts as a laxative. Health: Too much can cause diarrhea, cramping, and magnesium accumulation in people with kidney impairment.

descriptions.name: magnesium oxide
descriptions.description_en: A refined magnesium compound used to prevent clumping or regulate acidity. Health: Large doses may cause diarrhea or magnesium accumulation, particularly in people with impaired kidney function.

descriptions.name: magnesium silicate
descriptions.description_en: A processed mineral used to keep powders dry and free-flowing. The available modern data are limited for a complete long-term assessment. Health: Use should remain controlled because chronic exposure has not been characterized as thoroughly as for better-studied additives.

descriptions.name: magnesium trisilicate
descriptions.description_en: A mineral anti-caking compound used in powdered foods. Its long-term safety database is incomplete. Health: The concern is uncertainty from limited chronic and reproductive data, rather than confirmed toxicity from normal food use.

descriptions.name: mais déshydraté
descriptions.description_en: Whole dried corn supplies fiber, B vitamins, and carotenoids, promoting digestion and nutrition.

descriptions.name: makaire
descriptions.description_en: Long-lived top predators that concentrate the most methylmercury of any commercial fish. The FDA and EPA place swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel, bigeye tuna, orange roughy and Gulf tilefish on the Choices to Avoid list: pregnant women, breastfeeding women and children should not eat them at all, and other adults only rarely.

descriptions.name: malanga
descriptions.description_en: Starchy tropical roots that must always be cooked. Raw taro and raw yam contain calcium oxalate crystals and other compounds that irritate the mouth and digestive tract; cooking destroys them. Once cooked they are a good source of complex carbohydrate, potassium and fibre.

descriptions.name: maltitol
descriptions.description_en: A polyol (E965) widely used in sugar-free chocolate. It still raises blood sugar noticeably — more than other polyols — and is one of the most likely to cause bloating and laxative effects.

descriptions.name: maltodextrine
descriptions.description_en: An ultra-processed carbohydrate made by industrial hydrolysis of starch, often from corn. Its glycemic index reaches around 110, higher than table sugar, and studies link it to disrupted gut bacteria.

descriptions.name: manchego
descriptions.description_en: Manchego delivers beneficial nutrients that promote strong bones and muscle health.

descriptions.name: mandarin
descriptions.description_en: Mandarin is a citrus fruit rich in vitamin C, supporting immune function.

descriptions.name: mandarine
descriptions.description_en: Mandarine is a citrus fruit rich in vitamin C, supporting immune function.

descriptions.name: mangue
descriptions.description_en: Vitamins A and C and digestive enzymes in mango support immune health and digestion while fiber balances natural sugars.

descriptions.name: mannitol
descriptions.description_en: A polyol sweetener and anti-caking agent (E421) with roughly half the calories of sugar. Like all polyols it is poorly absorbed and carries a mandatory laxative warning above 10%.

descriptions.name: maquereau
descriptions.description_en: Maquereau provides omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: maquereau roi
descriptions.description_en: Long-lived top predators that concentrate the most methylmercury of any commercial fish. The FDA and EPA place swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel, bigeye tuna, orange roughy and Gulf tilefish on the Choices to Avoid list: pregnant women, breastfeeding women and children should not eat them at all, and other adults only rarely.

descriptions.name: marlin
descriptions.description_en: Long-lived top predators that concentrate the most methylmercury of any commercial fish. The FDA and EPA place swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel, bigeye tuna, orange roughy and Gulf tilefish on the Choices to Avoid list: pregnant women, breastfeeding women and children should not eat them at all, and other adults only rarely.

descriptions.name: maroilles
descriptions.description_en: Maroilles offers protein and essential fats, but its high fat and salt content should be consumed in moderation.

descriptions.name: masala
descriptions.description_en: Masala benefits the body by delivering curcumin with studied anti-inflammatory properties from dried spices.

descriptions.name: mascarpone
descriptions.description_en: Mascarpone cheese offers beneficial fats and proteins that contribute to energy and tissue repair.

descriptions.name: massala
descriptions.description_en: Massala benefits the body by delivering curcumin with studied anti-inflammatory properties from dried spices.

descriptions.name: matiere grasse de coco
descriptions.description_en: Coconut fat provides medium-chain saturated fats that support energy metabolism and cooking versatility.

descriptions.name: matiere grasse de coco modifiee
descriptions.description_en: Modified coconut fat is an ultra-processed fat created by industrial processes like hydrogenation and fractionation. It is a marker of ultra-processed food (NOVA 4) and should be consumed with caution.

descriptions.name: medjool
descriptions.description_en: Medjool dates offer essential nutrients and fiber that aid in maintaining healthy digestion.

descriptions.name: Mélamine
descriptions.description_en: An industrial resin chemical with no place in food. It was illegally added to milk products to fake protein readings, causing kidney failure in infants in 2008. IARC classifies it Group 2B, possibly carcinogenic.

descriptions.name: Mélamine (vaisselle)
descriptions.description_en: A resin used in unbreakable tableware. It is stable at normal temperatures but can migrate into food when heated, which is why melamine dishes should never go in a microwave or hold very hot food.

descriptions.name: melon
descriptions.description_en: Melons and watermelon are more than 90% water, which makes them low in calories while supplying potassium, vitamin C and, in the orange and red varieties, beta-carotene and lycopene. Their sugar is diluted enough that a generous portion stays modest.

descriptions.name: menthol
descriptions.description_en: A cooling compound from mint, used in balms, toothpaste and scalp products. The cooling sensation is not an active benefit, and at higher concentrations it irritates skin and mucous membranes.

descriptions.name: mercure
descriptions.description_en: A heavy metal that is strongly neurotoxic, especially for the developing brain. Banned in EU cosmetics and tightly capped in fish and seafood. It accumulates in the body and is never safe at any deliberate dose.

descriptions.name: Mercure / Thimérosal
descriptions.description_en: Mercury and its preservative form thimerosal. Mercury is a potent neurotoxin that accumulates in the nervous system and kidneys; it is banned in EU cosmetics and strictly limited in food.

descriptions.name: metabisulfite de potassium
descriptions.description_en: A sulfite preservative (E224) common in winemaking and dried fruit. It must be declared as an allergen above 10 mg/kg and can cause asthma symptoms in sensitive people.

descriptions.name: metabisulfite de sodium
descriptions.description_en: One of the most widely used sulfites (E223), found in wine, dried fruit and seafood. It destroys some thiamine (vitamin B1) and is a declarable allergen above 10 mg/kg in the EU.

descriptions.name: methyl paraben
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic preservative used against molds and bacteria. It has weak biological activity in laboratory testing, but food use is regulated under a combined acceptable daily intake with ethyl paraben. Health: The practical concern is cumulative exposure from food, medicines, and personal-care products, not proven cancer from permitted food levels.

descriptions.name: methylcellulose
descriptions.description_en: A chemically modified cellulose (E461) used to thicken and bind, notably in plant-based meat substitutes. It is not absorbed and passes through as fibre, but it is a laboratory-modified ingredient.

descriptions.name: methylparaben
descriptions.description_en: A preservative (E218/E219) still permitted in limited EU food uses and widely used in cosmetics. It is the least potent paraben, though the family as a whole is under scrutiny for endocrine activity.

descriptions.name: methylparabene sodique
descriptions.description_en: Methylparabene sodique is a synthetic preservative that dissolves easily in water and preserves food safety. Repeated exposure from multiple sources is more relevant than a single food serving for health considerations.

descriptions.name: Mica contaminé
descriptions.description_en: A mineral that gives cosmetics their shimmer. Natural mica can carry heavy metal impurities, and much of the global supply is linked to child labour in unregulated mines.

descriptions.name: Microplastiques / Microbilles
descriptions.description_en: Tiny plastic particles added to scrubs, toothpaste and cosmetics. The EU began banning intentionally added microplastics in 2023 because they pass through water treatment and accumulate in the environment.

descriptions.name: miel
descriptions.description_en: Raw honey brings antioxidants, enzymes and antibacterial compounds that refined sugar does not have. It is still around 80% sugar, and the WHO counts it as a free sugar exactly like table sugar - a better sweetener, not a free one. Never give honey to a baby under one year old, because of the risk of infant botulism.

descriptions.name: mimolette
descriptions.description_en: Mimolette provides calcium and protein, supporting bone health and muscle maintenance.

descriptions.name: mirabelle
descriptions.description_en: Mirabelle provides vitamins and antioxidants that help protect cells and support overall wellness.

descriptions.name: miso
descriptions.description_en: Soybeans fermented with koji over months, eaten as a paste. Unpasteurised miso, natto and tempeh carry live cultures and enzymes that support digestion, along with complete plant protein. Miso is salty enough to count as a seasoning rather than an ingredient.

descriptions.name: mixed acetic and tartaric acid esters of mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
descriptions.description_en: A complex emulsifier made by chemically esterifying mono- and diglycerides. It improves dough performance, volume, and shelf stability in industrial foods. Health: No carcinogenic classification applies. Purity, total tartaric-acid exposure, and frequent consumption of heavily formulated foods are the main considerations.

descriptions.name: moah
descriptions.description_en: Mineral oil aromatic hydrocarbons, contaminants from packaging inks, machine lubricants and processing aids. EFSA considers those with three or more aromatic rings genotoxic and carcinogenic, and found their presence in infant formula to be of health concern.

descriptions.name: modified coconut fat
descriptions.description_en: Modified coconut fat is an ultra-processed fat created by industrial processes like hydrogenation and fractionation. It is a marker of ultra-processed food (NOVA 4) and should be consumed with caution.

descriptions.name: modified coconut oil
descriptions.description_en: Modified coconut oil is an ultra-processed fat created by industrial processes like hydrogenation and fractionation. It is a marker of ultra-processed food (NOVA 4) and should be consumed with caution.

descriptions.name: modified corn starch
descriptions.description_en: A generic label covering any starch altered chemically or physically to thicken and stabilise industrial food, without saying which one. EFSA considers modified starches safe with no numerical ADI needed, but they are refined carbohydrates with no nutrients and one of the clearest markers of ultra-processing.

descriptions.name: modified cornstarch
descriptions.description_en: A generic label covering any starch altered chemically or physically to thicken and stabilise industrial food, without saying which one. EFSA considers modified starches safe with no numerical ADI needed, but they are refined carbohydrates with no nutrients and one of the clearest markers of ultra-processing.

descriptions.name: modified potato starch
descriptions.description_en: Modified potato starch is an industrially acetylated starch with a high glycemic index as an ultra-processed carbohydrate.

descriptions.name: modified rice starch
descriptions.description_en: A generic label covering any starch altered chemically or physically to thicken and stabilise industrial food, without saying which one. EFSA considers modified starches safe with no numerical ADI needed, but they are refined carbohydrates with no nutrients and one of the clearest markers of ultra-processing.

descriptions.name: modified starch
descriptions.description_en: A generic label covering any starch altered chemically or physically to thicken and stabilise industrial food, without saying which one. EFSA considers modified starches safe with no numerical ADI needed, but they are refined carbohydrates with no nutrients and one of the clearest markers of ultra-processing.

descriptions.name: modified tapioca starch

EFSA considers modified starches safe with no numerical ADI needed, but they are refined carbohydrates with no nutrients and one of the clearest markers of ultra-processing.

descriptions.name: modified wheat starch
descriptions.description_en: A generic label covering any starch altered chemically or physically to thicken and stabilise industrial food, without saying which one. EFSA considers modified starches safe with no numerical ADI needed, but they are refined carbohydrates with no nutrients and one of the clearest markers of ultra-processing.

descriptions.name: modified whey
descriptions.description_en: Whey that has been chemically or enzymatically altered for texture and shelf life. It is far removed from the original dairy ingredient and is characteristic of ultra-processed formulation.

descriptions.name: mogroside
descriptions.description_en: A sweetener from the luo han guo fruit, with no calories and no effect on blood sugar. It has a long history of use in Asia and is widely permitted in North America. In the EU only an aqueous decoction of the fruit has been authorised, while purified mogroside V - the form used in most imported products - is still awaiting authorisation.

descriptions.name: mogrosides
descriptions.description_en: A sweetener from the luo han guo fruit, with no calories and no effect on blood sugar. It has a long history of use in Asia and is widely permitted in North America. In the EU only an aqueous decoction of the fruit has been authorised, while purified mogroside V - the form used in most imported products - is still awaiting authorisation.

descriptions.name: monk fruit
descriptions.description_en: A sweetener from the luo han guo fruit, with no calories and no effect on blood sugar. It has a long history of use in Asia and is widely permitted in North America. In the EU only an aqueous decoction of the fruit has been authorised, while purified mogroside V - the form used in most imported products - is still awaiting authorisation.

descriptions.name: monk fruit extract
descriptions.description_en: A sweetener from the luo han guo fruit, with no calories and no effect on blood sugar. It has a long history of use in Asia and is widely permitted in North America. In the EU only an aqueous decoction of the fruit has been authorised, while purified mogroside V - the form used in most imported products - is still awaiting authorisation.

descriptions.name: mono and diacetyltartaric acid esters
descriptions.description_en: Mono and diacetyltartaric acid esters (DATEM, E472e) are dough strengtheners used in industrial bread production. They may disrupt the gut microbiome and are linked to a slightly increased risk of type 2 diabetes.

descriptions.name: monoammonium glutamate
descriptions.description_en: Monoammonium glutamate (E624) is a glutamate flavour enhancer that intensifies umami in industrial seasonings. It performs the same role as MSG under a different name.

descriptions.name: monopotassium glutamate
descriptions.description_en: Monopotassium glutamate (E622) is a flavour enhancer from the glutamate family used to build savoury taste with less real ingredient. It is a reliable marker of ultra-processed food.

descriptions.name: monostearate de sorbitane
descriptions.description_en: Sorbitan emulsifiers (E491–E495) stabilise fats in baked goods and are synthetic emulsifiers under study for gut lining effects.

descriptions.name: morbier
descriptions.description_en: Morbier offers protein and essential fats, but its high fat and salt content should be consumed in moderation.

descriptions.name: moringa
descriptions.description_en: Moringa leaves provide concentrated protein, calcium, iron, and vitamin A, supporting overall nutritional health.

descriptions.name: mortadelle
descriptions.description_en: An emulsified, cured pork sausage. As a processed meat it falls under the IARC Group 1 classification, with regular consumption linked to a higher colorectal cancer risk.

descriptions.name: mosh
descriptions.description_en: Mineral oil saturated hydrocarbons, which migrate into food from packaging and machinery. EFSA concluded in 2023 that current dietary exposure raises no health concern, though they accumulate in the liver and lymphatic tissue and long-term effects remain uncertain.

descriptions.name: moule
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: moules
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: moutarde
descriptions.description_en: Mustard is simply crushed mustard seed with vinegar and salt. It adds flavour for almost no calories and keeps the antioxidant compounds of the seed. Dijon and wholegrain versions contain little beyond seed, vinegar, water and salt.

descriptions.name: mouton
descriptions.description_en: Mutton and similar unprocessed meats provide complete protein, iron, and B vitamins, and are generally leaner.

descriptions.name: mozzarella
descriptions.description_en: Mozzarella delivers calcium and protein that strengthen bones and muscles.

descriptions.name: msg
descriptions.description_en: Monosodium glutamate (E621), a flavour enhancer that makes processed food taste richer. Regulators consider it safe at normal intake, but it is a reliable marker of ultra-processed food and can encourage overeating.

descriptions.name: munster
descriptions.description_en: Munster offers protein and essential fats, but its high fat and salt content should be consumed in moderation.

descriptions.name: mure
descriptions.description_en: Anthocyanins in dark berries support heart health and cognitive function.

descriptions.name: mussel
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: mussels
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: natamycine
descriptions.description_en: An antifungal (E235) applied to the surface of cheese and cured sausage. It is not absorbed through the gut wall, but it is an antibiotic-class compound, raising questions about resistance.

descriptions.name: navet
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: neohesperidine dc
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic sweetener (E959) derived from bitter orange peel, several hundred times sweeter than sugar. It is authorised in the EU but not in the United States, and is used mainly to mask bitterness in industrial products.

descriptions.name: neotame
descriptions.description_en: An artificial sweetener (E961) built from aspartame, up to 13,000 times sweeter than sugar. EFSA re-evaluated it in 2025 and found no safety concern at permitted levels, though the WHO advises against sweeteners for weight control.

descriptions.name: niacinamide
descriptions.description_en: Vitamin B3 in its added form, used to fortify flours, cereals and drinks. The vitamin itself is beneficial and well tolerated; its presence mainly signals a refined product whose nutrients were added back after processing.

descriptions.name: nigari
descriptions.description_en: Nigari is a refined magnesium salt used in tofu, mineral fortification, and texture control. Large amounts may cause diarrhea, nausea, or abdominal cramping, especially with reduced kidney function.

descriptions.name: nisine
descriptions.description_en: A natural antibacterial peptide (E234) produced by lactic bacteria, used in cheese and canned foods. It is digested like any protein and is one of the most benign preservatives available.

descriptions.name: nitrate de potassium
descriptions.description_en: A curing salt (E252) used in charcuterie and cheese. In the body it converts to nitrite and forms nitrosamines: IARC classifies ingested nitrate under conditions leading to nitrosation as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic.

descriptions.name: nitrate de sodium
descriptions.description_en: A curing salt (E251) that the body converts to nitrite, which can then form nitrosamines. IARC rates ingested nitrate under conditions leading to endogenous nitrosation as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic. The confirmed Group 1 classification applies to processed meat as a food, not to the additive on its own.

descriptions.name: nitrite de potassium
descriptions.description_en: A curing agent (E249) that fixes the pink colour of cured meats and blocks botulism. It forms nitrosamines during curing and cooking; IARC rates ingested nitrite leading to nitrosation as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic.

descriptions.name: nitrite de sodium
descriptions.description_en: A curing agent (E250) that fixes the pink colour of cured meat and blocks botulism. During curing and cooking it forms nitrosamines; IARC rates ingested nitrite leading to nitrosation as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic.

descriptions.name: nitrosamine
descriptions.description_en: Compounds formed when nitrites react with proteins in cured meat or under high-heat cooking. Several nitrosamines, including NDMA, are rated IARC Group 2A and are a main reason processed meat is classified Group 1.

descriptions.name: noir brillant bn
descriptions.description_en: Brilliant Black BN (E151) is a synthetic black dye used in confectionery, sauces and decorations. Frequent consumption of several dyed products can push intake beyond the level intended for daily use.

descriptions.name: Noir de carbone
descriptions.description_en: Carbon black, a pigment used in cosmetics, inks and tyres. IARC classifies it Group 2B, possibly carcinogenic, based on inhalation exposure; the risk in finished cosmetics is far lower.

descriptions.name: noir pn
descriptions.description_en: Brilliant Black PN (E151) is a synthetic black dye used in confectionery, sauces and decorations. Frequent consumption of several dyed products can push intake beyond the level intended for daily use.

descriptions.name: noisette
descriptions.description_en: Vitamin E, monounsaturated fat, and manganese in hazelnuts support skin health and metabolism.

descriptions.name: noix
descriptions.description_en: Source of omega-3 ALA, protein and minerals that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: noix de cajou
descriptions.description_en: Rich in magnesium, zinc and healthy fats that support heart and immune health.

descriptions.name: noix de coco
descriptions.description_en: Medium-chain saturated fats in coconut provide energy and support metabolism when consumed in moderation.

descriptions.name: noix de macadamia
descriptions.description_en: Macadamia nuts supply monounsaturated fats that help maintain healthy cholesterol levels.

descriptions.name: noix de muscade
descriptions.description_en: Nutmeg is a spice used in small amounts that adds flavor without nutritional risk at culinary doses.

descriptions.name: noix de pecan
descriptions.description_en: Pecan nuts provide healthy fats and antioxidants that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: noix de pili
descriptions.description_en: A buttery tree nut rich in magnesium and healthy fats that support heart health.

descriptions.name: noix du bresil
descriptions.description_en: The richest natural source of selenium on the planet, which supports thyroid function and antioxidant defences. One or two nuts already cover a full day's requirement, and eating them by the handful every day can exceed the tolerable upper intake - a rare case where a whole food needs a portion limit.

descriptions.name: Nonylphénols éthoxylés (NPE)
descriptions.description_en: Detergent surfactants that degrade into nonylphenol, an endocrine disruptor and a priority hazardous substance in EU water law. Their use in consumer products is heavily restricted in Europe.

descriptions.name: nori
descriptions.description_en: Seaweed provides iodine, iron, magnesium and soluble fibre, supporting thyroid function and overall nutrition. Nori and wakame are moderate, but kombu is by far the most iodine-dense food known and can disturb thyroid function if eaten regularly - health agencies advise limiting it, and using it for stock rather than eating it.

descriptions.name: norwegian salmon
descriptions.description_en: Norwegian salmon is intensively farmed with industrial feed, antibiotics, synthetic colorants, and possible contaminants like PCBs and dioxins. Consumption should be occasional due to these potential contaminants and additives.

descriptions.name: octenyl succinic anhydride starch
descriptions.description_en: Starch modified with octenyl succinic anhydride (E1450) to act as an emulsifier and encapsulating agent in drinks, dressings and powdered flavourings. EFSA's 2017 re-evaluation of modified starches found no safety concern and no need for a numerical ADI, but it remains a refined carbohydrate with no nutrients and a marker of industrial formulation.

descriptions.name: octinoxate
descriptions.description_en: A chemical UV filter (with homosalate and octisalate) that penetrates the skin and is detectable in blood. EU scientific committees have cut the permitted levels over endocrine-disruption concerns, and some regions restrict it to protect coral reefs.

descriptions.name: octopus
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: oeuf
descriptions.description_en: High-quality protein, choline, vitamin D, B12, and lutein in eggs support brain, bone, and eye health.

descriptions.name: offal
descriptions.description_en: Exceptionally rich in vitamin A, B12, iron and copper - one of the most nutrient-dense foods there is. Its preformed vitamin A is so concentrated that health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid liver and liver products entirely, and a single weekly portion is enough for everyone else.

descriptions.name: oignon
descriptions.description_en: Quercetin, sulfur compounds, and prebiotic fructans in onion support antioxidant defenses and gut health.

descriptions.name: oignon déshydraté
descriptions.description_en: Keeps part of the onion's antioxidants while seasoning food naturally.

descriptions.name: okra
descriptions.description_en: Okra provides soluble fibre that helps regulate blood sugar and cholesterol, with very few calories. Its mucilage is what thickens stews and gumbo.

descriptions.name: okras
descriptions.description_en: Okra provides soluble fibre that helps regulate blood sugar and cholesterol, with very few calories. Its mucilage is what thickens stews and gumbo.

descriptions.name: oleoresine de paprika
descriptions.description_en: Oleoresine de paprika is a concentrated red-orange color extracted from paprika and standardized for pigment strength. Quality control is important for solvent residues and purity; rare allergic reactions may occur in sensitive individuals.

descriptions.name: oleoresins
descriptions.description_en: Oleoresins are obtained by industrial solvent extraction using hexane and ethanol; they are very different from the whole spice.

descriptions.name: onion
descriptions.description_en: Rich in quercetin and prebiotic fiber, onions support gut bacteria and overall digestive health.

descriptions.name: or
descriptions.description_en: Gold leaf (E175) used to decorate confectionery and drinks. EFSA re-evaluated it in 2016 and concluded that, given the very low solubility of elemental gold, systemic absorption and systemic effects are not expected. It passes through the body unchanged and adds nothing nutritionally - purely decorative.

descriptions.name: orange
descriptions.description_en: Vitamin C, fiber, and flavonoids in whole oranges support immunity and improve iron absorption.

descriptions.name: orange b
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic dye whose only remaining approved use in the US is colouring hot dog and sausage casings. It has never been authorised in the European Union.

descriptions.name: orange roughy
descriptions.description_en: Long-lived top predators that concentrate the most methylmercury of any commercial fish. The FDA and EPA place swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel, bigeye tuna, orange roughy and Gulf tilefish on the Choices to Avoid list: pregnant women, breastfeeding women and children should not eat them at all, and other adults only rarely.

descriptions.name: organic catechins
descriptions.description_en: The main catechin in green tea, a well-studied antioxidant. Drunk as an infusion it raises no concern. As a concentrated extract it is a different matter: EFSA found in 2018 that 800 mg of EGCG per day or more from supplements raises liver enzymes, and the EU now requires warning labelling on green tea extracts. Read it as a good sign in tea, a caution in a supplement.

descriptions.name: orge
descriptions.description_en: Barley’s beta-glucan fiber helps control cholesterol and supports gut health with a low glycemic response.

descriptions.name: osa starch
descriptions.description_en: Starch modified with octenyl succinic anhydride (E1450) to act as an emulsifier and encapsulating agent in drinks, dressings and powdered flavourings. EFSA's 2017 re-evaluation of modified starches found no safety concern and no need for a numerical ADI, but it remains a refined carbohydrate with no nutrients and a marker of industrial formulation.

descriptions.name: oursin
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: oxidized starch
descriptions.description_en: Starch chemically oxidised (E1404) to improve thickening, clarity and processing performance. EFSA's 2017 re-evaluation of the whole modified-starch family found no safety concern and no genotoxic concern. Its role is purely technological: a refined carbohydrate that signals an industrially engineered texture.

descriptions.name: oxybenzone
descriptions.description_en: A chemical UV filter absorbed through the skin and repeatedly flagged for hormonal activity. Its permitted concentration has been reduced in the EU, and it is banned in Hawaii and Palau for coral reef damage.

descriptions.name: oxyde d ethylene
descriptions.description_en: A fumigant banned in EU food production and classified as mutagenic, carcinogenic and reprotoxic, with no safe level established. Its detection in imported sesame and locust bean gum triggered the largest food recall operation in EU history from 2020.

descriptions.name: oxyde de magnesium
descriptions.description_en: Oxyde de magnesium is a refined magnesium compound used to prevent clumping or regulate acidity. Large doses may cause diarrhea or magnesium accumulation, particularly in people with impaired kidney function.

descriptions.name: oxydes de fer
descriptions.description_en: Mineral pigments (E172) used to colour coatings, sweets and cosmetics. They pass through the body largely unabsorbed and EFSA considers them safe, but they add no nutritional value.

descriptions.name: oxygen
descriptions.description_en: A natural gas used in controlled-atmosphere packaging and processing. Health: It is not toxic at food-packaging exposure. It can accelerate oxidation, rancidity, and vitamin loss in some foods.

descriptions.name: oyster
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: oysters
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: p hydroxybenzoate d ethyle
descriptions.description_en: P hydroxybenzoate d ethyle is a synthetic paraben preservative used to prevent mold and bacterial growth, with weak hormone-like activity studied experimentally. No cancer claim is justified at authorized levels, but repeated combined exposure to parabens is a concern.

descriptions.name: pain blanc
descriptions.description_en: Bread made from refined flour, with the bran and germ removed. It raises blood sugar quickly and delivers little fibre; wholemeal or sourdough versions are substantially better.

descriptions.name: pain complet
descriptions.description_en: Whole grain breads provide high fiber and help maintain stable blood sugar levels.

descriptions.name: pain plat
descriptions.description_en: Flatbreads such as pita, naan, chapati, roti, lavash and tortilla. Made with wholemeal flour they are a good bread; made with refined white flour, which is the usual case, they behave like white bread, and industrial versions add oils, sugar and preservatives on top.

descriptions.name: palmitate d ascorbyle
descriptions.description_en: A fat-soluble form of vitamin C (E304) used to keep oils from going rancid. It is broken down into vitamin C and palmitic acid in the body, and is considered safe at permitted levels.

descriptions.name: palourde
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: pamplemousse
descriptions.description_en: Pamplemousse is a citrus fruit rich in vitamin C, supporting immune function.

descriptions.name: panais
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: panax ginseng
descriptions.description_en: An Asian root traditionally used against fatigue, sold today mostly as a concentrated extract. It is not inert: it interacts with anticoagulants and diabetes medication, can disturb sleep at higher doses, and is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

descriptions.name: paneer
descriptions.description_en: Paneer provides proteins and calcium essential for healthy bones and muscle function.

descriptions.name: pantothenate de calcium
descriptions.description_en: Vitamin B5 in its added form, used to enrich foods, drinks and supplements. Harmless and genuinely useful, but it usually appears in products that lost their natural nutrients during refining.

descriptions.name: paprika extract, capsanthin and capsorubin
descriptions.description_en: A concentrated red-orange color extracted from paprika and processed to standardize pigment strength. It is not considered a high-risk additive at permitted levels. Health: Quality control is important for solvent residues and purity. Rare paprika-related allergic reactions may occur in sensitive people.

descriptions.name: paraben
descriptions.description_en: A family of preservatives with weak hormone-like activity in laboratory tests. The EU banned five of them from cosmetics in 2014 for lack of safety data (isopropyl-, isobutyl-, phenyl-, benzyl- and pentylparaben) and capped propyl- and butylparaben at 0.14%, with an additional ban on the nappy area of children under three. The 2004 study that detected parabens in breast tissue established no causal link; the real issue is cumulative exposure across food, cosmetics and medicines.

descriptions.name: parabene
descriptions.description_en: A family of preservatives with weak hormone-like activity in laboratory tests. The EU banned five of them from cosmetics in 2014 for lack of safety data (isopropyl-, isobutyl-, phenyl-, benzyl- and pentylparaben) and capped propyl- and butylparaben at 0.14%, with an additional ban on the nappy area of children under three. The 2004 study that detected parabens in breast tissue established no causal link; the real issue is cumulative exposure across food, cosmetics and medicines.

descriptions.name: parabenes
descriptions.description_en: Parabenes are preservatives detected in breast tumors, raising concerns about their safety in cosmetics and foods.

descriptions.name: Parabènes (méthyl, éthyl, propyl, butyl)
descriptions.description_en: Parabens (methyl, ethyl, propyl, butyl) are cosmetic preservatives that disrupt hormones and mimic estrogen. They are suspected of breast cancer links and are known allergens, so prolonged contact should be avoided.

descriptions.name: parabens
descriptions.description_en: A family of preservatives with weak hormone-like activity in laboratory tests. The EU banned five of them from cosmetics in 2014 for lack of safety data (isopropyl-, isobutyl-, phenyl-, benzyl- and pentylparaben) and capped propyl- and butylparaben at 0.14%, with an additional ban on the nappy area of children under three. The 2004 study that detected parabens in breast tissue established no causal link; the real issue is cumulative exposure across food, cosmetics and medicines.

descriptions.name: paraffinum liquidum
descriptions.description_en: Liquid petroleum oil used as an emollient in cosmetics. Untreated and mildly treated mineral oils are IARC Group 1 human carcinogens; pharmaceutical-grade refining lowers the risk but MOAH residues remain a concern.

descriptions.name: paraquat
descriptions.description_en: A herbicide banned in the EU since 2007 because of its extreme acute toxicity — a small ingested dose can be fatal with no antidote. Epidemiological studies also associate exposure with a raised risk of Parkinson's disease.

descriptions.name: parmesan
descriptions.description_en: Parmesan contains high-quality protein and calcium that support bone density.

descriptions.name: parmigiano
descriptions.description_en: Parmigiano provides essential nutrients like calcium and protein for strong bones.

descriptions.name: parsnip
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: partiellement hydrogene
descriptions.description_en: Partially hydrogenated oils are processed fats containing trans fats. Trans fats can negatively affect heart health.

descriptions.name: pastrami
descriptions.description_en: Brined, smoked and spiced beef. It falls under processed meat, an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen, and carries a heavy salt load. Regular intake is linked to colorectal cancer.

descriptions.name: patate
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable.
