Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: patate douce
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: pate de cacao
descriptions.description_en: Cocoa mass retains flavanols, fiber, and minerals that support heart health and antioxidant protection.

descriptions.name: pâte de curry
descriptions.description_en: Pâte de curry benefits the body by delivering fresh crushed plants rich in natural compounds.

descriptions.name: pate de piment fermentee coreenne
descriptions.description_en: A Korean fermented paste of chilli, glutinous rice and soybeans. The traditional version is a genuine ferment; most supermarket jars list glucose-fructose syrup among the main ingredients, which puts them closer to a sweet sauce than to a ferment. The ingredient list decides which one you have.

descriptions.name: patent blue v
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic blue dye used only to change appearance and provide no nutritional value. Current authorized uses have not been shown to create a general safety concern, but rare hypersensitivity reactions are possible. Health: People with a history of reactions to synthetic dyes should be cautious. The additive mainly signals a highly formulated product.

descriptions.name: pates completes
descriptions.description_en: Whole grain pasta offers fiber and minerals while lowering blood sugar spikes when cooked al dente.

descriptions.name: pcb
descriptions.description_en: Polychlorinated biphenyls, banned industrial oils that persist for decades in the environment and concentrate in fatty fish. IARC classifies them Group 1 human carcinogens, and they are also linked to hormonal and developmental effects.

descriptions.name: peanut
descriptions.description_en: A good source of plant protein, fibre and heart-healthy fats.

descriptions.name: peche
descriptions.description_en: Stone fruits supply fiber, potassium, carotenoids, and anti-inflammatory compounds for overall health.

descriptions.name: pecorino
descriptions.description_en: Pecorino cheese provides essential proteins and calcium that support bone health and muscle function.

descriptions.name: pectine
descriptions.description_en: Soluble fiber pectin helps lower cholesterol and supports digestive health naturally.

descriptions.name: peg-
descriptions.description_en: PEG- are ethoxylated ingredients that may contain traces of 1,4-dioxane, a possible carcinogen (IARC Group 2B). Their quality depends on purification; limit use.

descriptions.name: pentylparaben
descriptions.description_en: A family of preservatives with weak hormone-like activity in laboratory tests. The EU banned five of them from cosmetics in 2014 for lack of safety data (isopropyl-, isobutyl-, phenyl-, benzyl- and pentylparaben) and capped propyl- and butylparaben at 0.14%, with an additional ban on the nappy area of children under three. The 2004 study that detected parabens in breast tissue established no causal link; the real issue is cumulative exposure across food, cosmetics and medicines.

descriptions.name: pepperoni
descriptions.description_en: A cured, fermented pork and beef sausage preserved with nitrites. It is a processed meat, high in sodium and saturated fat, and regular intake is linked to colorectal cancer risk.

descriptions.name: peptides
descriptions.description_en: Peptides signal skin repair processes and are generally well tolerated without irritation.

descriptions.name: Perchloréthylène
descriptions.description_en: The classic dry-cleaning solvent. IARC classifies it Group 2A, probably carcinogenic to humans, and it is being phased out or tightly controlled in many countries because it lingers on treated fabrics.

descriptions.name: perfluoro
descriptions.description_en: Perfluorinated compounds (PFAS) are near-indestructible "forever chemicals"; PFOA is a confirmed human carcinogen (IARC Group 1, 2023). PFOS is possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B); avoid exposure.

descriptions.name: peroxyde de benzoyle
descriptions.description_en: An effective antibacterial acne treatment that kills the bacteria driving breakouts. It is drying and irritating at higher strengths, and it permanently bleaches fabric and hair on contact.

descriptions.name: pes
descriptions.description_en: Processed eucheuma seaweed (E407a) is a less purified carrageenan variant linked to gut inflammation and banned in EU infant formula.

descriptions.name: pesto
descriptions.description_en: Pesto benefits the body by combining whole foods like basil, pine nuts, and olive oil for nutrients.

descriptions.name: petit lait
descriptions.description_en: Whey is a natural cheese byproduct rich in protein that supports muscle repair and growth.

descriptions.name: petit-lait en poudre
descriptions.description_en: Whey dried by high-temperature spray-drying, then used as a cheap source of protein, lactose and texture. It keeps most of whey's nutrients, but it is a dried, fractioned dairy ingredient and is high in lactose.

descriptions.name: petits pois
descriptions.description_en: Pulses provide plant protein, fiber, and slow carbohydrates that improve blood sugar and cholesterol levels.

descriptions.name: petrolatum
descriptions.description_en: Petrolatum consists of petroleum-derived mineral oils; untreated forms are confirmed human carcinogens (IARC Group 1) due to MOAH content and should be avoided.

descriptions.name: pfas
descriptions.description_en: PFAS are chemicals found in grease-resistant food packaging; PFOA is an IARC Group 1 carcinogen since 2023. Prolonged contact should be avoided due to cancer risk.

descriptions.name: PFAS / PFC dans textiles
descriptions.description_en: Water- and stain-repellent "forever chemicals" applied to textiles and packaging. PFOA was classified IARC Group 1 human carcinogen in 2023; PFAS accumulate in the body and do not break down in the environment.

descriptions.name: PFAS / Polluants éternels
descriptions.description_en: PFAS are chemicals found in grease-resistant food packaging; PFOA is an IARC Group 1 carcinogen since 2023. Prolonged contact should be avoided due to cancer risk.

descriptions.name: PFOA / PTFE (Teflon)
descriptions.description_en: Non-stick coating and the chemicals used to make it. PTFE itself is inert, but PFOA — historically used in its manufacture — was classified an IARC Group 1 carcinogen in 2023. Scratched or overheated pans are the real concern.

descriptions.name: pgpr
descriptions.description_en: Polyglycerol polyricinoleate (E476), a synthetic emulsifier from castor oil used to cut cocoa butter costs in chocolate. Authorised in the EU, it signals a cheaper, more industrial formulation.

descriptions.name: phenoxyethanol
descriptions.description_en: A widely used preservative, permitted in the EU up to 1% in cosmetics. It is generally well tolerated, though France's health agency advised against using it on the nappy area of children under three.

descriptions.name: phenylparaben
descriptions.description_en: A family of preservatives with weak hormone-like activity in laboratory tests. The EU banned five of them from cosmetics in 2014 for lack of safety data (isopropyl-, isobutyl-, phenyl-, benzyl- and pentylparaben) and capped propyl- and butylparaben at 0.14%, with an additional ban on the nappy area of children under three. The 2004 study that detected parabens in breast tissue established no causal link; the real issue is cumulative exposure across food, cosmetics and medicines.

descriptions.name: phosphate acide d aluminium et de sodium
descriptions.description_en: Phosphate acide d aluminium et de sodium is an acidic aluminum salt used in baking powders and bakery products to control gas release. It adds aluminum and sodium, increasing exposure risks if heavily consumed.

descriptions.name: phosphate aluminium sodium
descriptions.description_en: Phosphate aluminium sodium is an acidic aluminum salt used in baking powders and bakery products to control gas release. It adds aluminum and sodium, increasing exposure risks if heavily consumed.

descriptions.name: phosphate d aluminium et de sodium acide
descriptions.description_en: Phosphate d aluminium et de sodium acide is an acidic aluminum salt used in baking powders to control gas release; it adds aluminum and sodium, increasing exposure risks if heavily consumed.

descriptions.name: phosphate d'os
descriptions.description_en: Bone phosphate (E542), a calcium phosphate obtained by degreasing and calcining animal bones, used in small amounts to keep powders free-flowing. It is of animal origin, so it does not suit vegetarian, vegan, halal or kosher diets unless specifically certified, and it adds to total phosphate intake, which EFSA already considers high in European diets. Its use in food today is marginal.

descriptions.name: phosphate de calcium
descriptions.description_en: A phosphate salt (E341) used as an anti-caking agent and firming agent, and to fortify foods with calcium. It falls under EFSA's combined phosphate limit, which many diets already approach.

descriptions.name: phosphate de diamidon
descriptions.description_en: Distarch phosphate (E1412), a cross-linked modified starch used to hold texture through heating and freezing. Safe by EFSA standards, but purely technical and typical of ultra-processed products.

descriptions.name: phosphate de diamidon acetyle
descriptions.description_en: Acetylated distarch phosphate (E1422), a doubly modified starch used in sauces, ready meals and desserts. It adds texture and shelf life but no nutritional value, and marks a highly industrial recipe.

descriptions.name: phosphate de diamidon acetyle e1414
descriptions.description_en: A doubly modified starch (E1414) built to survive heating, freezing and acidity. It adds texture and shelf life without nutrition, and signals an industrially engineered recipe.

descriptions.name: phosphate de diamidon hydroxypropyle
descriptions.description_en: One of the most common modified starches (E1442), used in sauces, desserts and ready meals to hold texture through heating and freezing. EFSA's 2017 re-evaluation found no safety concern and set no numerical ADI, but it is a purely technical refined carbohydrate and a clear marker of ultra-processed food.

descriptions.name: phosphate de diamidon hydroxypropyle e1450
descriptions.description_en: Phosphate de diamidon hydroxypropyle E1450 is an industrial starch derivative with a high glycemic index, impacting blood sugar levels.

descriptions.name: phosphate de monoamidon
descriptions.description_en: A modified starch (E1410) used to thicken and stabilise processed food. EFSA considers modified starches safe, but they are refined carbohydrates and a marker of ultra-processing.

descriptions.name: phosphate de potassium
descriptions.description_en: A phosphate salt (E340) used as a buffer and stabiliser. EFSA set a combined limit for all phosphate additives; people with reduced kidney function should keep added phosphates low.

descriptions.name: phosphate de sodium
descriptions.description_en: An added phosphate (E339) used to bind water and hold texture. Added phosphates are absorbed far more readily than natural ones, and EFSA has flagged high total intake as a concern for kidney and heart health.

descriptions.name: phosphated distarch phosphate
descriptions.description_en: A cross-linked and phosphorylated starch (E1413) designed to resist heat, acid and mechanical processing. EFSA found no safety concern for the modified-starch family, but the additive brings no nutrition and marks a heavily formulated product.

descriptions.name: Phosphates (détergents)
descriptions.description_en: Phosphates in detergents soften water and boost cleaning, but they drive algal blooms that suffocate rivers and lakes. The EU has restricted them in household laundry and dishwasher products.

descriptions.name: phosphatides d ammonium
descriptions.description_en: An emulsifier (E442) used almost exclusively in chocolate to control flow during moulding. It is authorised at low levels but is a synthetic phosphate derivative with no place in traditional chocolate.

descriptions.name: phtalate
descriptions.description_en: Plasticisers that soften plastics and fix fragrances. Several are classified as toxic to reproduction and act as endocrine disruptors; the most harmful are banned or authorisation-restricted in the EU.

descriptions.name: Phtalate DBP
descriptions.description_en: Dibutyl phthalate, once common in nail polish. It is classified as toxic to reproduction in the EU, banned from cosmetics, and on the REACH authorisation list because of its endocrine effects.

descriptions.name: Phtalate DEHP
descriptions.description_en: The most widely used plasticiser in soft PVC. It is classified as toxic to reproduction in the EU, banned in cosmetics and in toys, and restricted in food-contact and medical plastics.

descriptions.name: Phtalate DEP
descriptions.description_en: Diethyl phthalate, the phthalate most used to fix fragrances. It is considered less toxic than DEHP or DBP and is still permitted in the EU, but it is absorbed through skin and detected in most people.

descriptions.name: Phtalates (parfums)
descriptions.description_en: Phthalates hidden inside the generic word "fragrance", where they make scent last longer. Because the label discloses nothing, the consumer cannot tell which phthalate is present or at what level.

descriptions.name: physalis
descriptions.description_en: Small tart fruits eaten fresh - physalis, tamarillo and feijoa. They are low in sugar and supply vitamin C, fibre and carotenoids.

descriptions.name: pickle naturel
descriptions.description_en: Pickle naturel is a traditional probiotic fermented food that supports digestive health.

descriptions.name: pieuvre
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: pignon de pin
descriptions.description_en: Pine nuts offer essential fatty acids and vitamins that contribute to energy production and immune function.

descriptions.name: pili nut
descriptions.description_en: A buttery tree nut rich in magnesium and healthy fats that support heart health.

descriptions.name: piment
descriptions.description_en: Chillies contain capsaicin, which has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects at culinary doses.

descriptions.name: pink pepper
descriptions.description_en: Pink pepper berries support the body with their natural antioxidants and mild resinous flavor.

descriptions.name: pink salmon
descriptions.description_en: Pink salmon provides omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: plain yogurt
descriptions.description_en: Plain yogurt offers probiotics and protein that promote digestive and overall health.

descriptions.name: plantain
descriptions.description_en: Plantain is a starchy banana always eaten cooked. Green plantain is high in resistant starch, which feeds gut bacteria and blunts the glycemic response; as it ripens that starch turns to sugar.

descriptions.name: platano
descriptions.description_en: Plantain is a starchy banana always eaten cooked. Green plantain is high in resistant starch, which feeds gut bacteria and blunts the glycemic response; as it ripens that starch turns to sugar.

descriptions.name: plomb
descriptions.description_en: A heavy metal with no safe level of exposure according to the WHO. It is strongly neurotoxic — particularly damaging to children's brain development — and banned in EU cosmetics. Inorganic lead compounds are rated IARC Group 2A.

descriptions.name: Plomb (acétate de plomb)
descriptions.description_en: Lead acetate, once used in hair dyes and cosmetics. Lead is neurotoxic with no safe exposure level per the WHO, damaging brain development in children. It is banned in cosmetics in the EU and the US.

descriptions.name: poireau
descriptions.description_en: Prebiotic fiber and antibacterial sulfur compounds in leeks nourish gut bacteria and help fight infections.

descriptions.name: pois chiches
descriptions.description_en: Protein, fiber, and slow carbs in chickpeas promote fullness and support stable blood sugar levels.

descriptions.name: poivre
descriptions.description_en: Antioxidant-rich spices and herbs enhance flavor while reducing the need for added salt.

descriptions.name: poivre rose
descriptions.description_en: Poivre rose benefits the body as a mild, resinous dried berry with no additives.

descriptions.name: pollen
descriptions.description_en: Bee products carrying enzymes, amino acids and antibacterial compounds. They are also documented allergens: royal jelly and propolis have caused severe allergic reactions including anaphylaxis, rare but well recorded, and are best avoided by people with asthma or a known allergy to bee products. Pollen can trigger reactions in people allergic to the source plants.

descriptions.name: pollen frais
descriptions.description_en: Bee products carrying enzymes, amino acids and antibacterial compounds. They are also documented allergens: royal jelly and propolis have caused severe allergic reactions including anaphylaxis, rare but well recorded, and are best avoided by people with asthma or a known allergy to bee products. Pollen can trigger reactions in people allergic to the source plants.

descriptions.name: Polycarbonate (plastique #7)
descriptions.description_en: A hard, clear plastic made from bisphenol A. BPA leaches out with heat, scratches and age — a real concern now that the EU has banned BPA in food contact materials.

descriptions.name: polydextrose
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic soluble fibre (E1200) made from glucose, used to add bulk and fibre while cutting sugar. It is largely unabsorbed and acts as a prebiotic, but large amounts cause bloating.

descriptions.name: polyfluoro
descriptions.description_en: Perfluorinated compounds (PFAS) are near-indestructible "forever chemicals"; PFOA is a confirmed human carcinogen (IARC Group 1, 2023). PFOS is possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B); avoid exposure.

descriptions.name: polyphosphate
descriptions.description_en: Polyphosphates (E452) used to bind water, emulsify and stabilise processed meat and cheese. They count toward EFSA's combined phosphate limit and are a clear marker of industrial processing.

descriptions.name: polysorbate 20
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic emulsifier (E432) derived from sorbitol and ethylene oxide. Authorised at limited levels, but emulsifiers of this family have been linked in studies to disruption of the gut barrier.

descriptions.name: polysorbate 40
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic emulsifier (E434) used to blend fats and water in industrial food. Permitted at capped levels; animal studies on polysorbates suggest effects on gut bacteria and inflammation.

descriptions.name: polysorbate 60
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic emulsifier (E435) common in whipped toppings and baked goods. It is authorised but purely technical, and its family has been tied to gut microbiome changes in research.

descriptions.name: polysorbate 65
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic emulsifier (E436) used in ice cream and frozen desserts to control texture. Regulated at low levels, it is a clear marker of an industrially engineered product.

descriptions.name: polysorbate 80
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic emulsifier (E433) widely used in ice cream, sauces and dressings. Animal and cell studies link polysorbate 80 to thinning of the protective gut mucus layer and low-grade inflammation.

descriptions.name: Polystyrène (plastique #6)
descriptions.description_en: The plastic of foam trays and disposable cups. Its building block styrene is classified IARC Group 2A, probably carcinogenic, and migration increases with hot or fatty foods.

descriptions.name: polyvinyl alcohol (pva)
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic polymer used in edible films, coatings, and supplement capsules. It is only partly absorbed and is used for a technological purpose. Health: The principal concern is product purity and residual manufacturing chemicals rather than a proven toxic effect at permitted levels.

descriptions.name: polyvinylpolypyrrolidone (pvpp)
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic, insoluble polymer used to clarify beverages or stabilize supplements. It is poorly absorbed from the digestive tract. Health: Safety depends on strict limits for residual monomers and manufacturing impurities.

descriptions.name: pomelo
descriptions.description_en: Pomelo is rich in vitamin C and fiber, aiding digestion and boosting the immune system.

descriptions.name: pomme
descriptions.description_en: Rich in fibre and antioxidants, which slow sugar absorption and support heart health.

descriptions.name: pomme de terre
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: pommes de terre
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium and fibre — a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable.

descriptions.name: ponceau 4r
descriptions.description_en: Cochineal Red A (E124), a synthetic azo dye subject to the EU warning label on children's activity and attention. It is banned from food in the United States, Norway and Finland.

descriptions.name: potassium aluminium silicate
descriptions.description_en: Potassium aluminium silicate is an aluminum-containing mineral used to improve powder flow. Frequent intake may increase total aluminum exposure, especially for vulnerable consumers.

descriptions.name: potassium aluminium sulfate
descriptions.description_en: Potassium aluminium sulfate, also known as potassium alum, is used as a firming or processing agent adding aluminum to the diet. Long-term health concerns relate to cumulative aluminum exposure.

descriptions.name: potassium aluminum silicate
descriptions.description_en: An aluminum-containing mineral used to improve powder flow. It adds to aluminum exposure and has limited modern toxicology data. Health: Frequent intake from several aluminum-containing foods may increase total exposure, especially for vulnerable consumers.

descriptions.name: potassium aluminum sulfate
descriptions.description_en: Also called potassium alum, this compound is used as a firming or processing agent and adds aluminum to the diet. Health: Long-term concern relates to cumulative aluminum exposure, not an immediate poisoning effect from a single serving.

descriptions.name: potassium carbonates
descriptions.description_en: Refined mineral salts used to control acidity, improve dough, or support manufacturing. They are not considered harmful at normal food levels. Health: Very high potassium intake can be dangerous for people with kidney disease or those taking medicines that raise blood potassium.

descriptions.name: potassium chloride
descriptions.description_en: A refined mineral salt used to replace sodium, control flavor, or support texture. Health: Excess potassium can cause dangerous heart-rhythm problems in people with kidney disease or certain medications. Normal consumers usually tolerate food amounts.

descriptions.name: potassium ferrocyanide
descriptions.description_en: A stable anti-caking complex used mainly in salt. It does not normally release dangerous free cyanide during ordinary food use. Health: The additive should still remain within regulatory limits and purity specifications.

descriptions.name: potassium gluconate
descriptions.description_en: A potassium salt used for mineral fortification and product stability. Health: Excess potassium can be dangerous for people with kidney disease or medicines that impair potassium removal.

descriptions.name: potassium hydroxide
descriptions.description_en: A strong alkali used to adjust pH or manufacture other ingredients. It is neutralized or highly diluted during food processing. Health: The raw chemical can cause severe burns, but properly controlled food use should not retain this corrosive effect.

descriptions.name: potassium sulfate
descriptions.description_en: Potassium sulfate is a refined potassium salt used to regulate acidity or support processing; people with kidney disease must avoid excessive potassium intake. Excess potassium can disturb heart rhythm in sensitive individuals.

descriptions.name: potassium sulfates
descriptions.description_en: Refined potassium salts used to regulate acidity or support processing. Health: People with kidney disease must avoid excessive potassium because it can disturb heart rhythm.

descriptions.name: potassium sulphite
descriptions.description_en: Potassium sulphite is a sulfite preservative related to sodium sulfite and can trigger reactions in asthmatics.

descriptions.name: potato
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: poudre a lever
descriptions.description_en: Baking powder, a blend of a carbonate and an acid salt that makes dough rise. It is harmless in itself, though some formulations use aluminium-based acids that add to total aluminium intake.

descriptions.name: poudre de celeri
descriptions.description_en: Celery stalk or celeriac, simply dried and ground - harmless as a seasoning. Worth knowing, though, that the meat industry uses celery powder and celery juice as a natural nitrate source to cure meat labelled "no nitrites added": the body converts that nitrate to nitrite and the same nitroso-compounds form. On a charcuterie label it is a curing agent, not a vegetable.

descriptions.name: poudre de stevia
descriptions.description_en: Stevia powder is derived from whole leaves and serves as a natural, calorie-free sweetener.

descriptions.name: poulet
descriptions.description_en: Lean poultry provides complete protein and B vitamins for muscle repair and energy metabolism.

descriptions.name: poulpe
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: pousses de bambou
descriptions.description_en: Bamboo shoots are low in calories and a good source of fibre and potassium, but fresh shoots contain cyanogenic glycosides and must be boiled before eating - canned shoots are already processed and safe. Bean sprouts and lotus root, often sold alongside them, raise no such issue.

descriptions.name: pousses de haricot mungo
descriptions.description_en: Okra provides soluble fibre that helps regulate blood sugar and cholesterol, with very few calories. Its mucilage is what thickens stews and gumbo.

descriptions.name: ppd
descriptions.description_en: Para-phenylenediamine, the base of most permanent dark hair dyes. A strong skin sensitiser that can trigger severe allergic reactions; it is capped in the EU and illegal in "black henna" temporary tattoos.

descriptions.name: prawn
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: propane 1 2 diol esters
descriptions.description_en: Propylene glycol esters of fatty acids (E477) are used to aerate desserts and are typical in ultra-processed foods, permitted at capped levels.

descriptions.name: propionate de calcium
descriptions.description_en: A mould inhibitor (E282) used mainly in industrial bread. It is considered safe by EFSA and occurs naturally in some cheeses, though its presence signals bread built for long shelf life.

descriptions.name: propionate de potassium
descriptions.description_en: A mould inhibitor (E283) used in packaged bread and baked goods. Considered safe by EFSA, though it is only needed when bread must last far beyond its natural life.

descriptions.name: propionate de sodium
descriptions.description_en: A bread preservative (E281) that blocks mould and rope spoilage. EFSA considers it safe at permitted levels; it marks industrial rather than fresh-baked bread.

descriptions.name: propolis
descriptions.description_en: Bee products carrying enzymes, amino acids and antibacterial compounds. They are also documented allergens: royal jelly and propolis have caused severe allergic reactions including anaphylaxis, rare but well recorded, and are best avoided by people with asthma or a known allergy to bee products. Pollen can trigger reactions in people allergic to the source plants.

descriptions.name: propyl paraben
descriptions.description_en: A paraben preservative removed from the EU list of authorised food additives in 2006, after EFSA judged that the presumed safe intake was no longer valid because of effects on sex hormones and male reproductive organs in young rats. No food ADI has been accepted since. It is still permitted in US food, and was banned from foods in California in 2023.

descriptions.name: Propylène glycol
descriptions.description_en: A synthetic solvent and moisture-retaining agent used in flavors, colors, enzymes, and processed foods. It is not the same substance as toxic ethylene glycol. Health: Very high exposure can cause hyperosmolality, lactic acidosis, nervous-system depression, and kidney stress, especially in infants or people with impaired liver or kidney function.

descriptions.name: propylparaben
descriptions.description_en: A paraben preservative removed from the EU list of authorised food additives in 2006, after EFSA judged that the presumed safe intake was no longer valid because of effects on sex hormones and male reproductive organs in young rats. No food ADI has been accepted since. It is still permitted in US food, and was banned from foods in California in 2023.

descriptions.name: propylparabene sodique
descriptions.description_en: Propylparabene sodique is the sodium form of propyl paraben, no longer authorized in the EU due to uncertain reproductive toxicity safety. It should be avoided as a declared additive where unauthorized, especially due to repeated exposure concerns.

descriptions.name: protéine de blé
descriptions.description_en: Wheat gluten isolated by washing the starch out of the flour, then dried. It is protein-rich but low in lysine, and is used mainly to give industrial breads and meat substitutes their elasticity. Unsuitable in coeliac disease or gluten sensitivity.

descriptions.name: proteine de feve
descriptions.description_en: Protein extracted from fava beans, used to boost protein content in plant-based products. Nutritionally useful, though an isolate rather than a whole food.

descriptions.name: proteine de feverole
descriptions.description_en: Fava bean protein is extracted by dry milling and air classification, rich in lysine and allergen-free but still a protein concentrate; it is acceptable as a supplement but not as the sole protein source.

descriptions.name: proteine de lactoserum
descriptions.description_en: Whey is a natural cheese byproduct rich in protein that supports muscle repair and growth.

descriptions.name: proteine de petit lait
descriptions.description_en: Whey is a natural cheese byproduct rich in protein that supports muscle repair and growth.

descriptions.name: proteine de pois
descriptions.description_en: Protein isolated from yellow peas by industrial extraction. It is a useful plant protein, but stripped of the fibre and micronutrients of the whole pulse.

descriptions.name: protéine de pois chiche
descriptions.description_en: Protein milled and water-separated from chickpeas. It supplies plant protein, fibre and iron with a milder taste than yellow pea protein, but it remains a fractioned ingredient rather than the whole pulse.

descriptions.name: proteine de soja
descriptions.description_en: Soy protein isolated through industrial processing, often with hexane solvent. It is frequently GM-derived outside the EU and is used to bulk up protein content in reconstituted foods.

descriptions.name: proteines de feve
descriptions.description_en: Fava bean protein is extracted by dry milling and air classification, rich in lysine and allergen-free but still a protein concentrate; it is acceptable as a supplement but not as the sole protein source.

descriptions.name: proteines de pois
descriptions.description_en: Yellow-pea protein is made by water separation and drying, providing good iron and lysine but is a fractioned ingredient, not a whole food; it is fine as a supplement but not a replacement for whole-food protein sources.

descriptions.name: proteines de pois chiche
descriptions.description_en: Proteins from chickpeas are plant-based proteins rich in fiber and iron, derived by milling and water separation. They serve as a supplement but are less complete than whole chickpeas.

descriptions.name: proteines de soja
descriptions.description_en: Soy protein is industrially extracted using chemical solvents and is often GMO. It is a marker of ultra-processed food products.

descriptions.name: proteines hydrolysees
descriptions.description_en: Proteins broken down with acid or enzymes, which releases free glutamate and acts as a hidden flavour enhancer. The process can also generate unwanted by-products such as chloropropanols.

descriptions.name: protoxyde d azote
descriptions.description_en: Nitrous oxide (E942), the propellant in aerosol whipped cream. It is inert in food use and leaves no residue, though inhaling it recreationally causes serious neurological harm.

descriptions.name: provolone
descriptions.description_en: Provolone cheese offers essential nutrients that aid in muscle function and bone density.

descriptions.name: psicose
descriptions.description_en: A rare sugar that sweetens with almost no calories and no effect on blood glucose. It is authorised in the United States, Canada, Japan and Korea, but not in the European Union or the UK, where it is still going through novel food assessment. Large amounts cause bloating and digestive upset.

descriptions.name: ptfe
descriptions.description_en: PTFE includes perfluorinated compounds (PFAS), nearly indestructible chemicals; PFOA is a confirmed human carcinogen (IARC Group 1), PFOS possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B). Avoid exposure.

descriptions.name: pullulan
descriptions.description_en: A fermentation-produced carbohydrate polymer used to make edible films, capsules, and coatings. Health: Several grams at once may cause abdominal fullness, gas, bloating, or cramps in some people.

descriptions.name: pulpe de coco
descriptions.description_en: Pulpe de coco provides dietary fiber and healthy fats that support digestion and energy.

descriptions.name: PVC (plastique #3)
descriptions.description_en: A rigid plastic softened with phthalate plasticisers that migrate into fatty foods. Vinyl chloride, its building block, is a confirmed carcinogen, though it is largely bound in the finished material.

descriptions.name: pvp
descriptions.description_en: Polyvinylpyrrolidone (E1201), a synthetic polymer used to clarify drinks and coat tablets. It is not absorbed by the gut and is considered safe, serving a purely technical purpose.

descriptions.name: pyridoxine chlorhydrate
descriptions.description_en: Vitamin B6 in its added form, common in fortified foods and supplements. It is effective and safe at normal levels; very high long-term supplement doses are the only real concern.

descriptions.name: quaternium-15
descriptions.description_en: A formaldehyde-releasing preservative and one of the strongest emitters of the group. Formaldehyde is an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen; quaternium-15 is now prohibited in EU cosmetics.

descriptions.name: queso fresco
descriptions.description_en: Queso fresco contains proteins and calcium that contribute to bone strength and muscle maintenance.

descriptions.name: quince
descriptions.description_en: Quince contains antioxidants and dietary fiber that promote digestive health and reduce inflammation.

descriptions.name: quinoa
descriptions.description_en: Complete amino acids, magnesium, and iron in quinoa support muscle function and oxygen transport.

descriptions.name: racine de gingembre
descriptions.description_en: Ginger root aids digestion and helps reduce nausea and inflammation.

descriptions.name: racine de lotus
descriptions.description_en: Bamboo shoots are low in calories and a good source of fibre and potassium, but fresh shoots contain cyanogenic glycosides and must be boiled before eating - canned shoots are already processed and safe. Bean sprouts and lotus root, often sold alongside them, raise no such issue.

descriptions.name: radis
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: radis noir
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: radish
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: raifort
descriptions.description_en: Horseradish root supports respiratory health and aids digestion.

descriptions.name: raisin
descriptions.description_en: Polyphenols and fiber in grapes help moderate blood sugar and provide antioxidant protection.

descriptions.name: raisin sec
descriptions.description_en: Raisins are rich in antioxidants and fiber, aiding digestion and heart health.

descriptions.name: raisins secs
descriptions.description_en: Raisins contain beneficial compounds that support immune function and provide energy.

descriptions.name: ras el hanout
descriptions.description_en: Ras el hanout is a traditional blend of herbs, seeds, and spices that adds antioxidants and flavor.

descriptions.name: raw butter
descriptions.description_en: Raw butter offers natural fats that contribute to energy and nutrient absorption.

descriptions.name: raw milk
descriptions.description_en: Milk that has not been pasteurised. It keeps enzymes and flavour that heat destroys, but it can carry listeria, salmonella and E. coli, which is why health agencies advise against it for pregnant women, young children, older adults and anyone immunocompromised. Its sale for direct consumption is prohibited in Canada.

descriptions.name: reb a
descriptions.description_en: Reb A is a sweetener from Stevia rebaudiana leaves, industrially purified with zero calories. EFSA set an acceptable daily intake of 4 mg/kg; it signals a processed product.

descriptions.name: rebaudioside
descriptions.description_en: Rebaudioside is a sweetener from Stevia rebaudiana leaves, industrially purified with zero calories. EFSA set an acceptable daily intake of 4 mg/kg; it signals a processed product.

descriptions.name: rebaudioside a
descriptions.description_en: Rebaudioside A is a sweetener from Stevia rebaudiana leaves, industrially purified with zero calories. EFSA set an acceptable daily intake of 4 mg/kg; it signals a processed product.

descriptions.name: rebaudioside m
descriptions.description_en: A steviol glycoside with a cleaner taste than earlier stevia extracts, now often produced by fermentation rather than leaf extraction. It is approved and calorie-free, but industrially manufactured.

descriptions.name: reblochon
descriptions.description_en: Reblochon cheese offers fats and salt that provide energy and support cellular functions when consumed moderately.

descriptions.name: red rice
descriptions.description_en: Red rice provides essential nutrients and antioxidants that support overall health and well-being.

descriptions.name: reine claude
descriptions.description_en: Reine claude plums provide vitamins and antioxidants that support overall health and immune function.

descriptions.name: reishi
descriptions.description_en: Medicinal mushrooms sold as dried powder or concentrated extract. They supply beta-glucans and are well tolerated as a food. As a supplement, reishi has been associated with rare cases of liver injury - the NIH LiverTox database describes clinically apparent injury as extremely rare, and reported cases mostly involve the unextracted powdered form, alcohol use or existing liver disease. It can also interact with anticoagulants. Treat it as a supplement with its own precautions, not as an ordinary mushroom.

descriptions.name: requin
descriptions.description_en: Long-lived top predators that concentrate the most methylmercury of any commercial fish. The FDA and EPA place swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel, bigeye tuna, orange roughy and Gulf tilefish on the Choices to Avoid list: pregnant women, breastfeeding women and children should not eat them at all, and other adults only rarely.

descriptions.name: Résorcinol
descriptions.description_en: A compound used in permanent hair dyes. It is a skin sensitiser and is flagged as a suspected endocrine disruptor affecting thyroid function; its level in cosmetics is capped in the EU.

descriptions.name: rhubarb
descriptions.description_en: Rhubarb stalks are very low in sugar and high in fibre and vitamin K, which makes them one of the few fruits used in desserts that adds almost no sweetness of its own. Only the stalk is edible: the leaves contain enough oxalic acid to be genuinely toxic and must never be eaten.

descriptions.name: rhubarbe
descriptions.description_en: Rhubarb stalks are very low in sugar and high in fibre and vitamin K, which makes them one of the few fruits used in desserts that adds almost no sweetness of its own. Only the stalk is edible: the leaves contain enough oxalic acid to be genuinely toxic and must never be eaten.

descriptions.name: riboflavine
descriptions.description_en: Vitamin B2 is essential for energy production and supports healthy skin and eyes.

descriptions.name: ribonucleotides
descriptions.description_en: Disodium ribonucleotides (E635) are a blend of E627 and E631 that enhance flavor and are often combined with MSG.

descriptions.name: ribonucléotides calciques
descriptions.description_en: Calcium ribonucleotides are calcium salts of inosinic and guanylic acids used as umami enhancers combined with MSG; not advised for people with gout.

descriptions.name: ricotta
descriptions.description_en: Lower fat and salt in ricotta cheese make it a lighter source of calcium and protein.

descriptions.name: riz arborio
descriptions.description_en: Arborio rice is a short-grain rice used in cooking that provides carbohydrates for energy.

descriptions.name: riz basmati
descriptions.description_en: Basmati rice has a lower glycemic index and pigmented varieties add antioxidants and fiber.

descriptions.name: riz blanc
descriptions.description_en: Rice polished to remove the bran and germ. It is easy to digest and keeps well, but the milling takes away most of the fibre, magnesium and B vitamins and leaves a starch with a high glycemic response. Basmati has a lower glycemic index than short-grain white rice.

descriptions.name: riz complet
descriptions.description_en: Brown rice keeps its bran and germ, and with them fibre, B vitamins, magnesium and manganese that support digestion and energy production. White rice is the same grain with those layers polished off, which removes most of the nutrients and raises the glycemic response.

descriptions.name: riz jasmin
descriptions.description_en: Jasmine rice is a fragrant long-grain rice that supplies energy through carbohydrates.

descriptions.name: riz noir
descriptions.description_en: Black rice is a whole grain rich in antioxidants and fiber, supporting heart and digestive health.

descriptions.name: riz précuit
descriptions.description_en: Rice pre-cooked and dried for speed. The processing costs some vitamins and raises the glycemic response compared with regular rice, though parboiled versions retain more nutrients.

descriptions.name: riz rouge
descriptions.description_en: Red rice provides essential nutrients and antioxidants that support overall health and well-being.

descriptions.name: riz sauvage
descriptions.description_en: Wild rice is rich in fiber and protein, promoting digestive health and muscle maintenance.

descriptions.name: riz thai
descriptions.description_en: Thai rice offers carbohydrates and minerals that supply energy and support bodily functions.

descriptions.name: rognon
descriptions.description_en: Exceptionally rich in vitamin A, B12, iron and copper - one of the most nutrient-dense foods there is. Its preformed vitamin A is so concentrated that health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid liver and liver products entirely, and a single weekly portion is enough for everyone else.

descriptions.name: rognons
descriptions.description_en: Exceptionally rich in vitamin A, B12, iron and copper - one of the most nutrient-dense foods there is. Its preformed vitamin A is so concentrated that health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid liver and liver products entirely, and a single weekly portion is enough for everyone else.

descriptions.name: romesco
descriptions.description_en: Romesco benefits the body by offering antioxidants and healthy fats from nuts and roasted peppers.

descriptions.name: roquefort
descriptions.description_en: Blue cheeses concentrate calcium, protein and B12, and their moulds give them their character. They are among the saltiest cheeses there are, and health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid blue-veined cheese unless it has been cooked until steaming hot.

descriptions.name: rouge 3
descriptions.description_en: Erythrosine (E127), a petroleum-based cherry-red dye. The FDA revoked its authorisation in food and ingested drugs in January 2025 after it caused cancer in male rats, with reformulation required by 2027.

descriptions.name: rouge 40
descriptions.description_en: Allura Red (E129), a petroleum-derived synthetic dye. EU law requires a warning label stating it may affect children's activity and attention, and the FDA is phasing it out of the US food supply.

descriptions.name: rouge azo
descriptions.description_en: Red azo is an azo coloring linked to hyperactivity in children and banned in several countries.

descriptions.name: rouge de betterave
descriptions.description_en: Beetroot pigment betanin offers antioxidant activity that helps protect cells from damage.

descriptions.name: royal jelly
descriptions.description_en: Bee products carrying enzymes, amino acids and antibacterial compounds. They are also documented allergens: royal jelly and propolis have caused severe allergic reactions including anaphylaxis, rare but well recorded, and are best avoided by people with asthma or a known allergy to bee products. Pollen can trigger reactions in people allergic to the source plants.

descriptions.name: rutabaga
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: saccharine
descriptions.description_en: One of the oldest artificial sweeteners (E954). Once suspected of causing bladder cancer in rats, it was later cleared for humans and delisted as a carcinogen, but remains a purely synthetic additive.

descriptions.name: safran
descriptions.description_en: Saffron is a natural plant-based coloring and flavoring that does not affect nutrition when used sparingly.

descriptions.name: saint jacques
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: saint nectaire
descriptions.description_en: Saint nectaire provides calcium and protein, supporting bone health and muscle maintenance.

descriptions.name: sainte maure
descriptions.description_en: Sainte Maure goat cheese supports digestion and provides lower fat content compared to hard cheeses.

descriptions.name: salami
descriptions.description_en: A dry fermented and cured sausage. As a processed meat it falls under the IARC Group 1 classification: nitrite curing and fermentation generate compounds tied to colorectal cancer.

descriptions.name: salsa verde
descriptions.description_en: Salsa verde benefits the body by supplying antioxidants and vitamins from fresh herbs and vegetables.

descriptions.name: salt
descriptions.description_en: Sodium chloride, essential for fluid balance and nerve function but present in excess in most processed food. High sodium intake raises blood pressure, and the WHO recommends staying under 5 g of salt a day.

descriptions.name: sambal
descriptions.description_en: Sambal benefits the body by offering fermented or crushed vegetables with natural flavors.

descriptions.name: sardine
descriptions.description_en: Sardine provides omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: sardines
descriptions.description_en: Sardines provide omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: sarrasin
descriptions.description_en: Buckwheat supplies rutin, magnesium, and complete plant protein for blood sugar stability and heart health.

descriptions.name: sauce hoisin
descriptions.description_en: A sweet, thick condiment built mainly on sugar and fermented soybean paste, usually alongside modified starch, caramel colour and flavour enhancers. Oyster sauce is formulated the same way. They are industrial sauces rather than traditional ferments - heavy in both sugar and sodium.

descriptions.name: sauce poisson
descriptions.description_en: Anchovies salted and fermented for months, the backbone of South-East Asian cooking. It is a genuine traditional ferment rich in free amino acids, and it is also one of the saltiest condiments in any kitchen - a teaspoon carries as much sodium as a portion of crisps.

descriptions.name: sauce soja
descriptions.description_en: Traditionally brewed soy sauce is fermented for months and carries the depth that comes with it. Two things are worth checking on the label: it is extremely salty, so a few tablespoons cover a large share of the daily sodium limit; and cheaper versions are made by acid hydrolysis rather than brewing, a process that can generate 3-MCPD, which the EU caps by law.

descriptions.name: saucisse
descriptions.description_en: Sausages, including hot dogs and merguez, are processed meats classified IARC Group 1 human carcinogens (2015). Regular intake raises colorectal cancer risk; they are also high in salt and saturated fat.

descriptions.name: saucisson
descriptions.description_en: A dry-cured sausage preserved with salt and nitrites. It falls under processed meat, an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen, with regular consumption linked to colorectal cancer.

descriptions.name: saumon aquaculture
descriptions.description_en: Farmed salmon is intensively raised with industrial feed, antibiotics, synthetic colorants, and possible contaminants like PCBs and dioxins. Consumption should be occasional due to these potential contaminants and additives.

descriptions.name: saumon coho
descriptions.description_en: Coho salmon is a wild fish rich in omega-3 fatty acids, providing essential nutrients for heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: saumon d'elevage
descriptions.description_en: Farmed salmon is raised intensively with industrial feed, antibiotics, synthetic colorants, and possible contaminants like PCBs and dioxins; wild salmon is preferable.

descriptions.name: saumon ecossais
descriptions.description_en: Scottish salmon is intensively farmed with industrial feed, antibiotics, synthetic colorants, and possible contaminants like PCBs and dioxins. Consumption should be occasional due to these potential contaminants and additives.

descriptions.name: saumon keta
descriptions.description_en: Keta salmon is a wild fish rich in omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: saumon norvegien
descriptions.description_en: Norwegian salmon is intensively farmed with additives and possible contaminants like PCBs and dioxins. Consumption should be occasional due to these potential contaminants and additives.

descriptions.name: saumon quinnat
descriptions.description_en: Chinook salmon provides omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: saumon rose
descriptions.description_en: Pink salmon is a wild fish rich in omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: saumon rouge
descriptions.description_en: Red salmon is a wild fish rich in omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: saumon sauvage
descriptions.description_en: Wild salmon provides omega-3 EPA and DHA for brain and heart function, along with vitamin D and astaxanthin. It is leaner than farmed salmon and free of the feed, treatments and added colourants of aquaculture.

descriptions.name: saumon sockeye
descriptions.description_en: Sockeye salmon is a wild fish rich in omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: scallop
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: scallops
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: scamorza
descriptions.description_en: Scamorza offers valuable proteins and calcium to strengthen bones and muscles.

descriptions.name: scottish salmon
descriptions.description_en: Scottish salmon is intensively farmed with industrial feed, antibiotics, synthetic colorants, and possible contaminants like PCBs and dioxins. Consumption should be occasional due to these potential contaminants and additives.

descriptions.name: sea urchin
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: seaweed
descriptions.description_en: Seaweed provides iodine, iron, magnesium and soluble fibre, supporting thyroid function and overall nutrition. Nori and wakame are moderate, but kombu is by far the most iodine-dense food known and can disturb thyroid function if eaten regularly - health agencies advise limiting it, and using it for stock rather than eating it.

descriptions.name: seiche
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: sel d aspartame-acesulfame
descriptions.description_en: A combined salt of aspartame and acesulfame K (E962), used to balance the aftertaste of each. It carries the concerns of both parent sweeteners, including aspartame's IARC Group 2B classification.

descriptions.name: sel d epsom
descriptions.description_en: Sel d epsom is an industrial laxative at high doses that can disrupt electrolyte balance. It should be used cautiously to avoid health risks.

descriptions.name: sels d acides gras
descriptions.description_en: Fatty acid salts (E470), used as anti-caking and glazing agents rather than as a food fat. They are refined industrial derivatives typical of processed formulations.

descriptions.name: shark
descriptions.description_en: Long-lived top predators that concentrate the most methylmercury of any commercial fish. The FDA and EPA place swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel, bigeye tuna, orange roughy and Gulf tilefish on the Choices to Avoid list: pregnant women, breastfeeding women and children should not eat them at all, and other adults only rarely.

descriptions.name: sheep milk
descriptions.description_en: Smaller fat globules in goat, sheep and buffalo milk may make them easier to digest for some people. Nutritionally they are close to cow's milk, with slightly more medium-chain fats.

descriptions.name: shellac
descriptions.description_en: A resin (E904) secreted by the lac insect, used to glaze sweets, coffee beans and tablets. It is not absorbed, but it is of insect origin and therefore not vegetarian.

descriptions.name: shoyu
descriptions.description_en: Traditionally brewed soy sauce is fermented for months and carries the depth that comes with it. Two things are worth checking on the label: it is extremely salty, so a few tablespoons cover a large share of the daily sodium limit; and cheaper versions are made by acid hydrolysis rather than brewing, a process that can generate 3-MCPD, which the EU caps by law.

descriptions.name: shrimp
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: silicate aluminium
descriptions.description_en: Silicate aluminium is a calcium-aluminum anti-caking agent found in powdered products. It adds to aluminum burden, which is neurotoxic and linked to Alzheimer's; restricted in the EU.

descriptions.name: silicate alumino-calcique
descriptions.description_en: Calcium aluminosilicate (E556), an anti-caking agent that contributes to overall aluminium intake. EFSA has flagged dietary aluminium as a concern for accumulation in the body over time.

descriptions.name: silicate alumino-potassique
descriptions.description_en: Potassium aluminosilicate (E555), an anti-caking and glazing agent. Like other aluminium-based additives, it adds to total aluminium exposure, which EFSA considers should be kept low.

descriptions.name: silicate alumino-sodique
descriptions.description_en: Sodium aluminosilicate (E554), used to stop powders clumping. It contributes to dietary aluminium, which accumulates in the body and is why EFSA set a weekly tolerable intake.

descriptions.name: silicate d aluminium et de potassium
descriptions.description_en: Silicate d aluminium et de potassium is an aluminum-containing mineral used to improve powder flow. Frequent intake may increase total aluminum exposure, especially for vulnerable consumers.

descriptions.name: silicate d aluminium et de sodium
descriptions.description_en: Silicate d aluminium et de sodium is an industrial anti-caking mineral that contributes aluminum exposure. Cumulative aluminum exposure and incomplete long-term data raise health concerns.

descriptions.name: silicate de sodium
descriptions.description_en: Sodium silicate (E550), a technical anti-caking and preservation aid. It is strongly alkaline in concentrated form and serves purely industrial purposes, with no nutritional role.

descriptions.name: silice
descriptions.description_en: Silicon dioxide (E551), an anti-caking agent in powders and dried mixes. EFSA could not confirm the safety of its nanoparticle fraction in its re-evaluation and called for stricter specifications.

descriptions.name: silicon dioxide
descriptions.description_en: A finely divided mineral powder used to prevent clumping and improve flow in seasonings, powders, and supplements. Health: Current authorized food uses are not considered a general safety concern, but particle characterization and metal impurities require strict specifications.

descriptions.name: sirop d erable
descriptions.description_en: Maple syrup is simply concentrated maple sap, and it carries manganese, zinc and polyphenols that refining would remove. It is nonetheless about two thirds sugar and counts as a free sugar in dietary guidelines - a whole-food sweetener to use sparingly.

descriptions.name: sirop d'érable déshydraté
descriptions.description_en: Dehydrated maple syrup retains natural antioxidants and minerals, serving as an unrefined natural sugar alternative.

descriptions.name: sirop de ble
descriptions.description_en: A syrup made by breaking down wheat starch into sugars. It is marketed as a natural sweetener but behaves like any glucose syrup, with a high glycemic impact and no nutrients.

descriptions.name: sirop de datte
descriptions.description_en: Dates cooked down into a syrup. It keeps some of the potassium and polyphenols of the fruit, but the fibre is largely gone and what remains is concentrated fruit sugar, counted as a free sugar in dietary guidelines.

descriptions.name: sirop de dattes
descriptions.description_en: Dates cooked down into a syrup. It keeps some of the potassium and polyphenols of the fruit, but the fibre is largely gone and what remains is concentrated fruit sugar, counted as a free sugar in dietary guidelines.

descriptions.name: sirop de glucose
descriptions.description_en: A syrup produced by industrial hydrolysis of corn or wheat starch. It has a very high glycemic index, causes sharp blood-sugar spikes and brings no nutrients — a hallmark of ultra-processed food.

descriptions.name: sirop de glucose-fructose
descriptions.description_en: High-fructose corn syrup, a cheap industrial sweetener. Its fructose load is processed almost entirely by the liver and is linked to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and metabolic syndrome.

descriptions.name: sirop de mais
descriptions.description_en: Corn syrup is an industrial syrup made from often-GMO corn linked to obesity, fatty liver disease, and metabolic syndrome.

descriptions.name: sirop de mais a haute teneur en fructose
descriptions.description_en: High fructose corn syrup is an industrial sweetener extracted from corn, often GMO. It is strongly linked to obesity, type 2 diabetes, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, and metabolic syndrome, so it should be avoided.

descriptions.name: sirop de mais haute fructose
descriptions.description_en: High fructose corn syrup is an industrial sweetener extracted from corn, often GMO. It is strongly linked to obesity, type 2 diabetes, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, and metabolic syndrome, so it should be avoided.

descriptions.name: sirop de poire de terre
descriptions.description_en: Syrup from the yacon root, unusual in that most of its sweetness comes from fructo-oligosaccharides that the body does not absorb, so it feeds gut bacteria instead of raising blood sugar. Large amounts cause bloating for the same reason.

descriptions.name: sirop de polyglycitol
descriptions.description_en: A polyol syrup (E964) made by hydrogenating starch, used as a bulk sweetener in sugar-free products. Like all polyols it is poorly absorbed and carries a mandatory laxative warning above 10%.

descriptions.name: sirop de riz
descriptions.description_en: Rice syrup, often sold as a healthier sweetener. It is almost pure glucose with a very high glycemic index, and rice-based products can carry inorganic arsenic residues.

descriptions.name: sirop de yacon
descriptions.description_en: Syrup from the yacon root, unusual in that most of its sweetness comes from fructo-oligosaccharides that the body does not absorb, so it feeds gut bacteria instead of raising blood sugar. Large amounts cause bloating for the same reason.

descriptions.name: skyr
descriptions.description_en: Skyr is a high-protein dairy product that supports muscle health and digestion.

descriptions.name: sles
descriptions.description_en: SLES is a cosmetic surfactant used for cleaning and foaming. It may cause skin and eye irritation and can be contaminated with carcinogenic 1,4-dioxane, so prolonged contact should be avoided.

descriptions.name: SLES (Sodium Laureth Sulfate)
descriptions.description_en: SLES (Sodium Laureth Sulfate) is a cosmetic surfactant possibly contaminated with carcinogenic 1,4-dioxane. It can irritate skin and eyes, so prolonged contact should be avoided.

descriptions.name: SLS (Sodium Lauryl Sulfate)
descriptions.description_en: A powerful foaming detergent used in shampoos, toothpaste and cleaners. It is not carcinogenic, but it is a well-documented irritant that strips skin and scalp with frequent use.

descriptions.name: sockeye
descriptions.description_en: Sockeye is a wild fish rich in omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: sodium aluminium silicate
descriptions.description_en: Sodium aluminium silicate is an industrial anti-caking mineral that contributes aluminum exposure. Cumulative aluminum exposure and incomplete long-term data raise health concerns.

descriptions.name: sodium aluminium sulfate
descriptions.description_en: Sodium aluminium sulfate adds aluminum and sodium to the diet, increasing cumulative exposure concerns.

descriptions.name: sodium aluminum phosphate, acidic
descriptions.description_en: An acidic aluminum salt used in some baking powders and bakery products to control gas release. Health: It adds both aluminum and sodium. Heavy reliance on products containing aluminum additives can increase total exposure above recommended limits.

descriptions.name: sodium aluminum silicate
descriptions.description_en: An industrial anti-caking mineral that also contributes aluminum. The toxicology database has not supported a fully conclusive modern assessment. Health: Cumulative aluminum exposure and incomplete long-term data are the main reasons for concern.

descriptions.name: sodium aluminum sulfate
descriptions.description_en: An aluminum- and sodium-containing industrial salt used in some baking powders and processing applications. Health: It increases cumulative aluminum and sodium exposure. Frequent consumption of several aluminum-containing products is the main concern.

descriptions.name: sodium benzoate
descriptions.description_en: A preservative (E211) used in acidic drinks and sauces. Combined with vitamin C, and helped by heat or light, it can form traces of benzene — a reason to avoid drinks that list both.

descriptions.name: sodium diacetate
descriptions.description_en: Sodium diacetate (E262) is a preservative that adds salt-and-vinegar flavor to foods. It is well tolerated but adds sodium to the diet.

descriptions.name: sodium ethyl paraben
descriptions.description_en: The water-soluble sodium form of ethyl paraben. It is an industrial antimicrobial preservative and contributes to the same combined paraben exposure limit as ethyl paraben. Health: The main concern is cumulative exposure to parabens rather than an immediate toxic effect at permitted levels.

descriptions.name: sodium ferrocyanide
descriptions.description_en: A stable iron-cyanide complex used in salt to prevent clumping. It is not the same as free cyanide under normal food conditions. Health: Current authorized uses are low. Purity and compliance with exposure limits are more relevant than the alarming chemical name.

descriptions.name: sodium gluconate
descriptions.description_en: A refined sodium salt used to bind metals, stabilize products, and control acidity. Health: Its main nutritional concern is added sodium rather than specific toxicity.

descriptions.name: sodium hydroxide
descriptions.description_en: A powerful alkaline processing agent used for pretzels, olives, cocoa, and pH control. It is consumed only after reaction, neutralization, washing, or dilution. Health: The concentrated chemical is corrosive. Correct processing must prevent caustic residues in the final food.

descriptions.name: sodium laureth sulfate
descriptions.description_en: Sodium laureth sulfate (E-number not specified) is an ethoxylated ingredient that may contain traces of possibly carcinogenic 1,4-dioxane; quality varies by manufacturer. Its use should be limited due to potential health concerns related to 1,4-dioxane contamination.

descriptions.name: sodium methyl paraben
descriptions.description_en: The sodium salt of methyl paraben, designed to dissolve more easily in water. It is a synthetic preservative counted within the same combined exposure limit as methyl and ethyl parabens. Health: Repeated exposure from several sources is more relevant than a single food serving.

descriptions.name: sodium nitrate
descriptions.description_en: A curing salt (E251) that the body converts to nitrite, which can then form nitrosamines. IARC rates ingested nitrate under conditions leading to endogenous nitrosation as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic. The confirmed Group 1 classification applies to processed meat as a food, not to the additive on its own.

descriptions.name: sodium propyl paraben
descriptions.description_en: The sodium form of propyl paraben, also no longer authorized as a food additive in the European Union. Its safety could not be adequately confirmed from the available reproductive-toxicity evidence. Health: Avoid as a declared food additive where it is not authorized. The concern is insufficient safety assurance, especially for repeated exposure.

descriptions.name: sodium sulfates
descriptions.description_en: Refined sulfate salts used in processing and acidity control. Health: Large sulfate doses can draw water into the intestine and cause diarrhea. Sodium-containing forms also add to total sodium intake.

descriptions.name: sodium sulphite
descriptions.description_en: Sodium sulphite is a sulfite compound that can trigger asthma attacks and acts as an allergen. It should be consumed occasionally with caution due to these health risks.

descriptions.name: soja
descriptions.description_en: Soy in unspecified form, from whole beans to industrial isolates. Whole soy is nutritious, but most soy in processed food is heavily refined and frequently GM outside the EU.

descriptions.name: son d'avoine
descriptions.description_en: Oat bran is the outer layer of the oat grain, very rich in beta-glucans that help lower cholesterol.

descriptions.name: son de blé
descriptions.description_en: Wheat bran is the husk of the wheat grain, highly concentrated in insoluble fiber useful for intestinal transit.

descriptions.name: sorbate de potassium
descriptions.description_en: One of the most common mould inhibitors (E202), well tolerated and among the gentler preservatives. Some laboratory work suggests it may react with vitamin C, though food-level effects are not established.

descriptions.name: sorbitanes
descriptions.description_en: Sorbitan emulsifiers (E491–E495) used to stabilise fats in baked goods and confectionery. They belong to the synthetic emulsifier family under study for effects on the gut lining.

descriptions.name: sorbitol
descriptions.description_en: A polyol sweetener (E420) that is only partly absorbed, so it raises blood sugar less than sugar. EU law requires a laxative warning above 10%, as it commonly causes bloating and diarrhoea.

descriptions.name: soude caustique
descriptions.description_en: Sodium hydroxide (soude caustique) is a powerful alkaline agent used in food processing for pretzels and olives; it is corrosive and must be neutralized to avoid residues.

descriptions.name: soy hemicellulose
descriptions.description_en: Soy hemicellulose is a processed fiber fraction from soybeans used to thicken and stabilize food products. Residual soy proteins may affect people with severe soy allergies despite low toxicity of the additive.

descriptions.name: soybean hemicellulose
descriptions.description_en: A processed fiber fraction extracted from soybeans and used to thicken, stabilize, or keep particles suspended. It is mainly an industrial texture ingredient. Health: Residual soy proteins may matter for people with a severe soy allergy, even though the additive itself is not considered highly toxic.

descriptions.name: spice extract
descriptions.description_en: Spice extract is obtained by industrial solvent extraction using hexane and ethanol; it is very different from the whole spice.

descriptions.name: spice extracts
descriptions.description_en: Spice extracts are obtained by industrial solvent extraction using hexane and ethanol; they are very different from the whole spice.

descriptions.name: spices
descriptions.description_en: Herbs and spices are rich in antioxidants and enhance flavor without adding salt.

descriptions.name: spirulina
descriptions.description_en: A cyanobacterium dried into powder, dense in plant protein, iron and antioxidants. One caveat matters: the B12 it contains is pseudo-B12, inactive in humans, so it cannot be counted as a B12 source on a plant-based diet. Sourcing also matters, since poorly controlled production can carry microcystin contamination.

descriptions.name: spirulina extract
descriptions.description_en: A cyanobacterium dried into powder, dense in plant protein, iron and antioxidants. One caveat matters: the B12 it contains is pseudo-B12, inactive in humans, so it cannot be counted as a B12 source on a plant-based diet. Sourcing also matters, since poorly controlled production can carry microcystin contamination.

descriptions.name: spiruline
descriptions.description_en: A cyanobacterium dried into powder, dense in plant protein, iron and antioxidants. One caveat matters: the B12 it contains is pseudo-B12, inactive in humans, so it cannot be counted as a B12 source on a plant-based diet. Sourcing also matters, since poorly controlled production can carry microcystin contamination.

descriptions.name: squid
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: sriracha maison
descriptions.description_en: Sriracha maison benefits the body by providing fermented vegetables that support digestive health.

descriptions.name: ssamjang
descriptions.description_en: Ssamjang is a Korean condiment blending doenjang and gochujang with a naturally fermented base.

descriptions.name: stannous chloride
descriptions.description_en: A tin compound used mainly to preserve color in a limited number of canned foods. It requires strict concentration limits. Health: Excess inorganic tin can cause acute nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. This is the principal established health concern.

descriptions.name: starch sodium octenyl succinate
descriptions.description_en: Starch modified with octenyl succinic anhydride (E1450) to act as an emulsifier and encapsulating agent in drinks, dressings and powdered flavourings. EFSA's 2017 re-evaluation of modified starches found no safety concern and no need for a numerical ADI, but it remains a refined carbohydrate with no nutrients and a marker of industrial formulation.

descriptions.name: stearate de magnesium
descriptions.description_en: Magnesium stearate is an industrial lubricating agent that may reduce nutrient absorption.

descriptions.name: stearoyl lactylate de calcium
descriptions.description_en: Stearoyl lactylate de calcium (E481) is a dough conditioner that improves volume and shelf life in industrial bread. It is authorized at limited levels but unnecessary in traditional bread.

descriptions.name: stearoyl lactylate de sodium
descriptions.description_en: Sodium stearoyl lactylate (E481), a dough conditioner that improves volume and shelf life in industrial bread. It is authorised at limited levels but never needed in traditionally made bread.

descriptions.name: stevia
descriptions.description_en: Steviol glycosides (E960) extracted from stevia leaves — plant-derived but heavily refined. Approved with a daily limit of 4 mg/kg, they add no calories, though the aftertaste means they are often blended with other sweeteners.

descriptions.name: stevia entiere
descriptions.description_en: Whole stevia leaves offer a natural, calorie-free sweetener beneficial for reducing calorie consumption.

descriptions.name: stevia leaf
descriptions.description_en: Whole stevia leaf provides sweetness without calories or blood sugar impact.

descriptions.name: stilton
descriptions.description_en: Blue cheeses concentrate calcium, protein and B12, and their moulds give them their character. They are among the saltiest cheeses there are, and health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid blue-veined cheese unless it has been cooked until steaming hot.

descriptions.name: stracciatella
