descriptions.description_en: Stracciatella provides essential nutrients that support muscle function and bone health.

descriptions.name: substances laitieres modifiees
descriptions.description_en: A vague label covering dairy fractions altered or recombined industrially. It tells the consumer nothing about what is actually inside and signals a reconstituted rather than a real dairy product.

descriptions.name: sucralose
descriptions.description_en: A chlorinated artificial sweetener (E955) about 600 times sweeter than sugar. Approved by EFSA and the FDA, but studies suggest it may disturb gut bacteria, and it can form harmful compounds when heated in baking.

descriptions.name: sucre
descriptions.description_en: Refined sucrose, stripped of every nutrient. It is absorbed rapidly, driving blood-sugar spikes and insulin resistance, and regular intake contributes to obesity, type 2 diabetes and chronic inflammation.

descriptions.name: Sucre blanc raffiné
descriptions.description_en: Fully refined sucrose, stripped of all minerals. It is absorbed rapidly, spikes blood sugar and contributes to weight gain and metabolic disease when consumed regularly.

descriptions.name: sucre de canne
descriptions.description_en: Cane sugar, including raw, brown and demerara forms. It keeps a trace of molasses and minerals, but it is still around 95% sucrose and affects blood sugar much like white sugar.

descriptions.name: sucre de canne complet
descriptions.description_en: Unrefined cane sugar (rapadura, panela, muscovado, jaggery) keeps the molasses and with it iron, potassium and polyphenols that white sugar has lost. It is nonetheless still 85 to 95% sucrose and behaves in the body much like table sugar. Better, not harmless.

descriptions.name: sucre de dattes
descriptions.description_en: Date sugar is a natural sweetener made by grinding dried dates, retaining fiber, potassium, magnesium, and antioxidants.

descriptions.name: sucre inverti
descriptions.description_en: Sugar split into glucose and fructose to boost sweetness and keep products moist. Metabolically it behaves like table sugar, with the same effect on blood sugar and weight.

descriptions.name: sucres
descriptions.description_en: A catch-all label covering the added refined sugars in a product. They deliver energy with no vitamins, minerals or fibre, and regular consumption is tied to metabolic disease.

descriptions.name: sucroesters
descriptions.description_en: Sucroesters (E473) are synthetic emulsifiers made from sugar and fat, used to stabilize food products. They are authorized at limited levels but may affect the gut lining.

descriptions.name: sucroesters d acides gras
descriptions.description_en: Sucroesters d acides gras (E473) are synthetic emulsifiers made from sugar and fat, used to stabilize food products. They are authorized at limited levels but may affect the gut lining.

descriptions.name: sucroglycerides
descriptions.description_en: Industrial emulsifiers produced by reacting sucrose with food fats. They help oil and water remain mixed and create a stable, smooth texture in highly formulated foods. Health: Some exposure scenarios may approach or exceed the group acceptable daily intake. Large amounts may also contribute to digestive discomfort.

descriptions.name: sulfate d aluminium
descriptions.description_en: Sulfate d aluminium is an aluminum-containing processing salt used in limited applications that contributes to total dietary aluminum exposure. Aluminum can accumulate, so repeated exposure may exceed tolerable weekly levels, especially in those with reduced kidney function.

descriptions.name: sulfate d aluminium et d ammonium
descriptions.description_en: Ammonium aluminium sulfate is an aluminum-containing industrial salt used for firming or processing in limited foods. Repeated intake contributes to aluminum accumulation in the body, which is limited but concerning.

descriptions.name: sulfate d aluminium et de potassium
descriptions.description_en: Potassium alum, also known as sulfate d aluminium et de potassium, is used as a firming or processing agent adding aluminum to the diet. Long-term concern is about cumulative aluminum exposure, not immediate poisoning.

descriptions.name: sulfate d aluminium et de sodium
descriptions.description_en: Sulfate d aluminium et de sodium is an aluminum- and sodium-containing industrial salt used in some baking powders and processing applications. It increases cumulative aluminum and sodium exposure, with frequent consumption of aluminum-containing products being the main concern.

descriptions.name: sulfate de cuivre
descriptions.description_en: Copper sulfate (E519), used as a processing aid and firming agent. Copper is essential in trace amounts but toxic in excess, causing liver and kidney damage, so food use is tightly capped.

descriptions.name: sulfate de magnesium
descriptions.description_en: Magnesium sulfate is an industrial laxative that can cause electrolyte disruption at high doses.

descriptions.name: sulfate de potassium
descriptions.description_en: Potassium sulfate is a refined potassium salt used to regulate acidity or support processing; people with kidney disease must avoid excessive potassium intake. Excess potassium can disturb heart rhythm in sensitive individuals.

descriptions.name: sulfite de calcium
descriptions.description_en: A sulfite preservative (E226) used mainly in processed vegetables and drinks. It is a declarable allergen above 10 mg/kg and best limited by anyone sensitive to sulfites.

descriptions.name: sulfite de potassium
descriptions.description_en: A sulfite preservative (E225) used to stop oxidation and spoilage. Safe for most people, but an EU-declarable allergen that can trigger breathing difficulties in asthmatics.

descriptions.name: sulfite de sodium
descriptions.description_en: A sulfite preservative (E221) that keeps foods pale and stops spoilage. It is an EU-declarable allergen above 10 mg/kg and can provoke breathing problems in people with asthma.

descriptions.name: sulfuric acid
descriptions.description_en: A strong industrial acid used in controlled food processing and pH adjustment. It is neutralized or diluted before the food is consumed. Health: Concentrated sulfuric acid is severely corrosive, but properly manufactured food should not retain that corrosive hazard.

descriptions.name: sultana
descriptions.description_en: Sultanas supply important nutrients that support digestive and cardiovascular health.

descriptions.name: sultanas
descriptions.description_en: Sultanas provide antioxidants and vitamins that contribute to healthy metabolism.

descriptions.name: sultanines
descriptions.description_en: Sultanines offer natural sugars and nutrients that help maintain energy levels.

descriptions.name: sunflower lecithin
descriptions.description_en: A natural emulsifier pressed from sunflower seeds, used to blend fat and water. Unlike soy lecithin it is obtained mechanically rather than with solvents, involves no GM crop and carries no soy allergen - which makes it the cleanest emulsifier commonly found on a label.

descriptions.name: sweet potato
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: swordfish
descriptions.description_en: Long-lived top predators that concentrate the most methylmercury of any commercial fish. The FDA and EPA place swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel, bigeye tuna, orange roughy and Gulf tilefish on the Choices to Avoid list: pregnant women, breastfeeding women and children should not eat them at all, and other adults only rarely.

descriptions.name: tagatose
descriptions.description_en: A rare sugar that sweetens with almost no calories and no effect on blood glucose. It is authorised in the United States, Canada, Japan and Korea, but not in the European Union or the UK, where it is still going through novel food assessment. Large amounts cause bloating and digestive upset.

descriptions.name: tahini
descriptions.description_en: Rich in nutrients from sesame seeds, supporting overall health.

descriptions.name: talc
descriptions.description_en: Food-grade talc (E553b) used to stop powders sticking and clumping. IARC reclassified talc as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic to humans, in 2024, on limited evidence in humans, sufficient evidence in animals and strong mechanistic evidence. A separate and older concern is contamination with asbestos, which occurs naturally alongside talc deposits and is a confirmed Group 1 carcinogen.

descriptions.name: talc alimentaire
descriptions.description_en: Food-grade talc (E553b) used to stop powders sticking and clumping. IARC reclassified talc as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic to humans, in 2024, on limited evidence in humans, sufficient evidence in animals and strong mechanistic evidence. A separate and older concern is contamination with asbestos, which occurs naturally alongside talc deposits and is a confirmed Group 1 carcinogen.

descriptions.name: taleggio
descriptions.description_en: Taleggio cheese delivers proteins and minerals important for muscle maintenance and bone health.

descriptions.name: tamari
descriptions.description_en: Traditionally brewed soy sauce is fermented for months and carries the depth that comes with it. Two things are worth checking on the label: it is extremely salty, so a few tablespoons cover a large share of the daily sodium limit; and cheaper versions are made by acid hydrolysis rather than brewing, a process that can generate 3-MCPD, which the EU caps by law.

descriptions.name: tamarillo
descriptions.description_en: Tamarillo provides vitamins and antioxidants that contribute to immune support and skin health.

descriptions.name: tamarin
descriptions.description_en: Tamarind pulp is tangy and high in fibre, magnesium and polyphenols, used as a souring agent across South Asian and Latin American cooking. It is also naturally sugar-dense, so the concentrated pastes and blocks count as a sweet-sour ingredient rather than a fruit portion.

descriptions.name: tandoori
descriptions.description_en: Tandoori benefits the body by delivering curcumin with studied anti-inflammatory properties from dried spices.

descriptions.name: tangerine
descriptions.description_en: Tangerine is a citrus fruit rich in vitamin C, supporting immune function.

descriptions.name: tanin ferrique
descriptions.description_en: Iron tannate (E181), a colouring used on olives and some coatings. It is permitted at low levels but has little modern use and adds no nutritional value.

descriptions.name: tapioca dextrin
descriptions.description_en: A modified starch derived from cassava, used to coat, bulk and thicken. Like other dextrins, it is a refined carbohydrate that raises blood sugar quickly and adds no nutrients.

descriptions.name: tarama
descriptions.description_en: A spread made from salted fish roe. Traditional versions are simple, but industrial tarama is dominated by oil, salt and colouring, with a modest proportion of actual roe.

descriptions.name: taro
descriptions.description_en: Starchy tropical roots that must always be cooked. Raw taro and raw yam contain calcium oxalate crystals and other compounds that irritate the mouth and digestive tract; cooking destroys them. Once cooked they are a good source of complex carbohydrate, potassium and fibre.

descriptions.name: tartaric acid esters of mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
descriptions.description_en: Chemically modified fats used to strengthen dough, stabilize mixtures, and control texture. They are characteristic of industrial bakery and processed-food formulations. Health: No major specific disease risk is established at authorized levels. The relevant concern is cumulative intake and manufacturing impurities.

descriptions.name: tartrazine
descriptions.description_en: Yellow 5 (E102), a synthetic azo dye. EU law requires a warning that it may affect children's activity and attention; it can also trigger reactions in people sensitive to aspirin.

descriptions.name: taurine
descriptions.description_en: An amino acid the body produces naturally, added in large amounts to energy drinks. EFSA found no safety concern for taurine itself; the real issue is the caffeine and sugar it is usually paired with.

descriptions.name: tbhq
descriptions.description_en: Tert-butylhydroquinone (E319), a petroleum-derived antioxidant preservative. Not classified as a carcinogen by IARC, but high-dose animal studies show immune effects, and EFSA advises against use for infants.

descriptions.name: tea tree
descriptions.description_en: An essential oil with genuine antibacterial activity, used against acne. It must be diluted, as undiluted use causes irritation, and it is a recognised contact allergen that oxidises with age.

descriptions.name: teflon
descriptions.description_en: Perfluorinated compounds (PFAS) are near-indestructible "forever chemicals"; PFOA is a confirmed human carcinogen (IARC Group 1, 2023). PFOS is possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B); avoid exposure.

descriptions.name: tete de moine
descriptions.description_en: Tete de moine provides calcium and protein, supporting bone health and muscle maintenance.

descriptions.name: tetraborate de sodium
descriptions.description_en: Borax (E285), permitted in the EU for caviar only. It is classified as toxic to reproduction under EU chemical law and banned from general food use in most countries, including the US.

descriptions.name: thai rice
descriptions.description_en: Thai rice offers carbohydrates and minerals that supply energy and support bodily functions.

descriptions.name: thaumatine
descriptions.description_en: A sweet protein (E957) extracted from the West African katemfe fruit, around 2,000 times sweeter than sugar. It is plant-derived and digested like any protein, but it is a concentrated industrial extract with a lingering liquorice aftertaste.

descriptions.name: the noir
descriptions.description_en: Supplies antioxidants and moderate caffeine for alertness and protection.

descriptions.name: the vert
descriptions.description_en: Offers antioxidants and gentle caffeine with calming L-theanine effects.

descriptions.name: theine
descriptions.description_en: Contains natural stimulants that provide longer-lasting, milder energy than coffee.

descriptions.name: thon
descriptions.description_en: A nutritious source of protein and omega-3, but a large predator that accumulates methylmercury. Health agencies advise limiting intake, particularly for pregnant women and young children.

descriptions.name: thon obese
descriptions.description_en: Long-lived top predators that concentrate the most methylmercury of any commercial fish. The FDA and EPA place swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel, bigeye tuna, orange roughy and Gulf tilefish on the Choices to Avoid list: pregnant women, breastfeeding women and children should not eat them at all, and other adults only rarely.

descriptions.name: tige de rhubarbe
descriptions.description_en: Rhubarb stalks are very low in sugar and high in fibre and vitamin K, which makes them one of the few fruits used in desserts that adds almost no sweetness of its own. Only the stalk is edible: the leaves contain enough oxalic acid to be genuinely toxic and must never be eaten.

descriptions.name: tilapia
descriptions.description_en: A widely farmed white fish, affordable and lean but low in omega-3 and relatively high in omega-6. Farming conditions vary considerably, so sourcing matters.

descriptions.name: tile
descriptions.description_en: Long-lived top predators that concentrate the most methylmercury of any commercial fish. The FDA and EPA place swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel, bigeye tuna, orange roughy and Gulf tilefish on the Choices to Avoid list: pregnant women, breastfeeding women and children should not eat them at all, and other adults only rarely.

descriptions.name: tilefish
descriptions.description_en: Long-lived top predators that concentrate the most methylmercury of any commercial fish. The FDA and EPA place swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel, bigeye tuna, orange roughy and Gulf tilefish on the Choices to Avoid list: pregnant women, breastfeeding women and children should not eat them at all, and other adults only rarely.

descriptions.name: titanium dioxide
descriptions.description_en: A white colouring (E171) used in sweets, sauces and supplements. The EU banned it as a food additive in August 2022 after EFSA concluded that a concern for genotoxicity could not be ruled out and that no safe daily intake could be set. It remains permitted in the United States and in cosmetics.

descriptions.name: tobiko
descriptions.description_en: Flying fish roe used in sushi. It provides protein and omega-3, but it is very high in sodium and commercial versions are usually dyed and preserved.

descriptions.name: tofu
descriptions.description_en: Provides complete plant protein, calcium, and isoflavones for bone and muscle health.

descriptions.name: Toluène
descriptions.description_en: A solvent used in nail polish and adhesives. It is classified as toxic to reproduction in the EU, and its vapours affect the nervous system — good ventilation matters when using it.

descriptions.name: tomate
descriptions.description_en: Cooking increases lycopene, an antioxidant that supports heart and skin health.

descriptions.name: tomme
descriptions.description_en: Tomme provides calcium and protein, supporting bone strength and muscle health.

descriptions.name: tomme de savoie
descriptions.description_en: Tomme de Savoie offers calcium and protein, which contribute to healthy bones and muscles.

descriptions.name: tongue
descriptions.description_en: Exceptionally rich in vitamin A, B12, iron and copper - one of the most nutrient-dense foods there is. Its preformed vitamin A is so concentrated that health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid liver and liver products entirely, and a single weekly portion is enough for everyone else.

descriptions.name: topinambour
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: tourteau
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: triacetine
descriptions.description_en: A humectant and solvent (E1518) used to carry flavours and keep products moist. It breaks down into glycerol and acetic acid in the body and is considered safe at food levels.

descriptions.name: triclosan
descriptions.description_en: An antibacterial agent in some toothpastes, soaps and deodorants. The FDA banned it from consumer hand soaps in 2016; it is capped in the EU over hormonal effects and its contribution to antibiotic resistance.

descriptions.name: triethyl citrate
descriptions.description_en: A manufactured citrate ester used as a carrier, solvent, or plasticizer for flavors and coatings. Health: No major specific harm is established at authorized levels. Total exposure should remain within the acceptable daily intake.

descriptions.name: tripolyphosphate
descriptions.description_en: A phosphate (E451) used to make meat and seafood hold water, increasing their weight. It is permitted but contributes to a phosphate load that EFSA considers already high in European diets.

descriptions.name: turnip
descriptions.description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

descriptions.name: tzatziki
descriptions.description_en: Dips built on vegetables, yoghurt or nuts: tzatziki from cucumber and yoghurt, guacamole from avocado, baba ganoush from grilled aubergine, romesco and salsa verde from peppers, nuts and herbs. Made at home they are whole ingredients blended together, with nothing added.

descriptions.name: unpasteurised milk
descriptions.description_en: Milk that has not been pasteurised. It keeps enzymes and flavour that heat destroys, but it can carry listeria, salmonella and E. coli, which is why health agencies advise against it for pregnant women, young children, older adults and anyone immunocompromised. Its sale for direct consumption is prohibited in Canada.

descriptions.name: unpasteurized milk
descriptions.description_en: Milk that has not been pasteurised. It keeps enzymes and flavour that heat destroys, but it can carry listeria, salmonella and E. coli, which is why health agencies advise against it for pregnant women, young children, older adults and anyone immunocompromised. descriptions.name: unsweetened cocoa
descriptions.description_en: Unsweetened cocoa is pure 100% cocoa chocolate rich in antioxidants, magnesium, and fiber, promoting overall nutrition.

descriptions.name: unsweetened dark chocolate
descriptions.description_en: Unsweetened dark chocolate supports heart health with antioxidants, magnesium, and fiber from pure cocoa mass.

descriptions.name: valencay
descriptions.description_en: Valencay goat cheese supports digestion and provides lower fat content compared to hard cheeses.

descriptions.name: vanille
descriptions.description_en: Vanilla is a natural plant flavoring used in tiny amounts, with no additives or identified risks, distinct from synthetic vanillin.

descriptions.name: vermicelles de blé
descriptions.description_en: Thin noodles made from refined wheat flour. Convenient and quick to cook, but a refined carbohydrate with little fibre unless made from whole grain.

descriptions.name: vert 3
descriptions.description_en: Fast Green FCF (E143), a synthetic dye that is not authorised as a food colour in the European Union. It remains permitted in the US, where the FDA is working to phase it out.

descriptions.name: viande rouge
descriptions.description_en: Rich in bioavailable iron, zinc and vitamin B12, which support blood and immune function. IARC classified red meat as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic to humans, in 2015, based mainly on colorectal cancer - which is why it belongs in a balanced diet as a regular but moderate item rather than a daily one.

descriptions.name: viande transformee
descriptions.description_en: Meat preserved by salting, curing, smoking or nitrites (bacon, ham, sausages, deli meats). Classified IARC Group 1 human carcinogen in 2015: regular intake raises colorectal cancer risk. Best kept occasional.

descriptions.name: vinaigre
descriptions.description_en: Acetic acid in vinegar helps lower blood sugar response and enhances flavor without salt.

descriptions.name: vinaigre de riz
descriptions.description_en: Acidity from rice vinegar aids digestion and enhances flavor without added chemicals.

descriptions.name: vinaigre en poudre
descriptions.description_en: Vinegar dried onto a starch carrier, typically maltodextrin, to flavour crisps and seasoning mixes. It is a technical powder built for industrial dosing, not a natural vinegar.

descriptions.name: virgin coconut oil
descriptions.description_en: Virgin coconut oil is a basic culinary fat rich in medium-chain saturated fats that performs well in cooking and baking.

descriptions.name: vitamine c
descriptions.description_en: Vitamin C supports immunity, collagen production, and improves iron absorption.

descriptions.name: Vitamine E naturelle (tocophérol)
descriptions.description_en: Vitamin E protects cells from damage by acting as a natural antioxidant.

descriptions.name: wakame
descriptions.description_en: Seaweed provides iodine, iron, magnesium and soluble fibre, supporting thyroid function and overall nutrition. Nori and wakame are moderate, but kombu is by far the most iodine-dense food known and can disturb thyroid function if eaten regularly - health agencies advise limiting it, and using it for stock rather than eating it.

descriptions.name: wasabi
descriptions.description_en: Wasabi and horseradish are pungent roots from the brassica family, grated fresh and used in tiny amounts. Worth knowing that most wasabi sold in tubes and served in restaurants outside Japan is horseradish coloured green, with mustard and dye rather than real wasabi rhizome - the ingredient list will say.

descriptions.name: wasabia japonica
descriptions.description_en: Wasabi and horseradish are pungent roots from the brassica family, grated fresh and used in tiny amounts. Worth knowing that most wasabi sold in tubes and served in restaurants outside Japan is horseradish coloured green, with mustard and dye rather than real wasabi rhizome - the ingredient list will say.

descriptions.name: whelk
descriptions.description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

descriptions.name: whey
descriptions.description_en: Whey provides complete protein and essential amino acids for muscle repair and growth.

descriptions.name: wild atlantic salmon
descriptions.description_en: Wild Atlantic salmon provides omega-3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

descriptions.name: wild rice
descriptions.description_en: Wild rice is rich in fiber and protein, promoting digestive health and muscle maintenance.

descriptions.name: xylitol
descriptions.description_en: A polyol sweetener used in sugar-free gum, sweets and drinks. It is dose-dependently laxative, and a 2024 European Heart Journal study linked circulating xylitol to major cardiovascular events and showed heightened platelet reactivity in every volunteer after ingestion. The evidence is associative plus mechanistic rather than causal, but it places xylitol alongside erythritol rather than with the other polyols.

descriptions.name: yam
descriptions.description_en: Starchy tropical roots that must always be cooked. Raw taro and raw yam contain calcium oxalate crystals and other compounds that irritate the mouth and digestive tract; cooking destroys them. Once cooked they are a good source of complex carbohydrate, potassium and fibre.

descriptions.name: yangjo ganjang
descriptions.description_en: Korean brewed soy sauce supports digestion and provides beneficial nutrients from traditional fermentation.

descriptions.name: yaourt
descriptions.description_en: Yoghurt supplies beneficial bacteria that improve digestion and gut health.

descriptions.name: yaourt bulgare
descriptions.description_en: Bulgarian yogurt supports digestive health by providing beneficial probiotics and nutrients.

descriptions.name: yaourt grec
descriptions.description_en: Yaourt grec delivers protein and probiotics that benefit muscle and gut health.

descriptions.name: yaourt nature
descriptions.description_en: Yaourt nature contains probiotics that improve digestive health and nutrient absorption.

descriptions.name: yuzu
descriptions.description_en: Yuzu is a good source of vitamin C and antioxidants, enhancing immune response and skin condition.

descriptions.name: za atar
descriptions.description_en: Za atar is a traditional blend of herbs, seeds, and spices that adds antioxidants and flavor.

descriptions.name: zaatar
descriptions.description_en: Zaatar benefits the body by providing natural herbs and spices rich in antioxidants and nutrients.

descriptions.name: zinc pyrithione
descriptions.description_en: An antifungal once common in anti-dandruff shampoos, banned in EU cosmetics since March 2022 after being classified toxic to reproduction. It remains permitted in some other markets.

descriptions.name: 간장
descriptions.description_en: 간장 is Korean brewed soy sauce traditionally fermented; brewed versions are preferable to chemically acid-hydrolyzed ones.

descriptions.name: 고추장
descriptions.description_en: A Korean fermented paste of chilli, glutinous rice and soybeans. The traditional version is a genuine ferment; most supermarket jars list glucose-fructose syrup among the main ingredients, which puts them closer to a sweet sauce than to a ferment. The ingredient list decides which one you have.

descriptions.name: 라이코펜
descriptions.description_en: Lycopene (E160d) is the red pigment of tomatoes and a well-studied dietary antioxidant.

descriptions.name: 무가당 초콜릿
descriptions.description_en: 무가당 초콜릿 supports heart health with antioxidants, magnesium, and fiber from pure cocoa mass.

descriptions.name: 무설탕 초콜릿
descriptions.description_en: 무설탕 초콜릿 supports heart health with antioxidants, magnesium, and fiber from pure cocoa mass.

descriptions.name: 쌈장
descriptions.description_en: 쌈장 is a Korean condiment blending doenjang and gochujang with a naturally fermented base.

descriptions.name: 아세트산
descriptions.description_en: Vinegar acid (E260) helps preserve food and slightly lowers blood sugar response when taken with meals.

descriptions.name: 양조간장
descriptions.description_en: Korean brewed soy sauce supports digestion and provides beneficial nutrients from traditional fermentation.

descriptions.name: 청국장
descriptions.description_en: Cheonggukjang is rich in probiotics that support gut health and digestion.

descriptions.name: 커큐민
descriptions.description_en: The yellow pigment of turmeric (E100), used as a natural colouring. It is a plant-derived alternative to synthetic yellow dyes and raises no safety concern at food levels. The anti-inflammatory effects attributed to curcumin come from concentrated supplement doses, not from the trace amount used to colour a food.
